## Gate 1 / n/a / HTTPRoute retry — Which Gateway API channel is required for HTTPRoute retry at the pinned version?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.8.0
- Environment: n/a (documents only)
- Method: fetched, on 2026-09-05, in this session: `apis/v1/httproute_types.go`, `config/crd/standard/gateway.networking.k8s.io_httproutes.yaml`, and `config/crd/experimental/gateway.networking.k8s.io_httproutes.yaml`, all at tag `v1.6.2` (raw.githubusercontent.com); the v1.6.2 release's asset list (`gh api repos/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/tags/v1.6.2 --jq '.assets[].name'`); `https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/geps/gep-1731/`; `https://istio.io/latest/docs/ambient/usage/agentgateway/`; and, for the mirrored agentgateway docs version (nav shows "1.5 (latest)"), `https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/latest/about/gateway-api/` and `https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/latest/resiliency/retry/retry/` (both `curl -sL` 200, redirecting to `.../documentation/about/gateway-api/` and `.../documentation/resiliency/retry/retry/`, titled "Gateway API" and "Request retries").
- Result: Gateway API channel required for `HTTPRoute.spec.rules[].retry` at v1.6.2: **experimental**. `httproute_types.go` comments the field directly above `Retry *HTTPRouteRetry` (json tag `retry,omitempty`) with: "Retry defines the configuration for when to retry an HTTP request." / "Support: Extended" / "+optional" / "<gateway:experimental>" — the last two lines immediately preceding the field. The standard CRD (`config/crd/standard/.../httproutes.yaml`) has 0 occurrences of `retry:` and carries the annotation `gateway.networking.k8s.io/channel: standard`; the experimental CRD (`config/crd/experimental/.../httproutes.yaml`) has 2 occurrences of `retry:` and carries `gateway.networking.k8s.io/channel: experimental`. GEP-1731's page states "Status: Experimental (See status definitions.)". The v1.6.2 release's assets are `experimental-install.yaml` and `standard-install.yaml`. Istio's agentgateway usage page installs Gateway API with "kubectl apply --server-side -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.6.0/experimental-install.yaml" (experimental channel, at v1.6.0, not the v1.6.2 pinned here). Under "Supported and unsupported configuration," the same page lists the Gateway API resources Istio configures for agentgateway — "Gateway (using the istio-agentgateway or istio-agentgateway-waypoint class)", "HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute, TCPRoute, and TLSRoute", "InferencePool, ..." — and states "Istio configures agentgateway only through the Gateway API resources listed above"; the word "retry" does not occur anywhere on the page, and it makes no field-level statement about `HTTPRoute` retry in either direction. The agentgateway docs (Kubernetes, version 1.5) carry a conformance table row "| HTTPRoute Retries | [GEP-1731](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/geps/gep-1731) | ✅ Supported |"; the request-retries page states "This feature is experimental in the upstream Kubernetes Gateway API and subject to change." and its first setup step reads "Install the experimental Kubernetes Gateway API CRDs.", using the same `.../v1.6.0/experimental-install.yaml` command as the Istio page. Both agentgateway.dev pages document standalone agentgateway with its own Kubernetes controller, not Istio's `istio-agentgateway-waypoint`; whether istiod 1.31.0 translates `HTTPRouteRule.retry` onto an agentgateway waypoint is not established by any document read here.
- Interpretation: As documented — `HTTPRoute` retry is gated behind the experimental Gateway API channel at v1.6.2, consistent across the upstream Go type's comment, both CRDs' channel annotations and `retry:` field counts, and the GEP-1731 status. Istio's own agentgateway usage page is silent on the `retry` field specifically, naming only supported resource kinds, so neither support nor non-support can be read from it; agentgateway's own docs confirm the feature is supported and, like Istio, install it from the experimental channel, but those docs describe agentgateway under its own controller, not istiod's waypoint. Whether an agentgateway waypoint deployed by Istio 1.31.0 actually carries a `retry` block through to the data plane stays open and is answered by Gate 3's R2 run, not by anything read here.
- Follow-up: none

## Gate 1 / mockllm / deterministic — Are two runs comparable?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.8.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: Built `fixtures/mockllm` (Go, standard library only; no outbound HTTP calls, so no client retry setting to disable): `POST /v1/chat/completions` (JSON and SSE, `"stream":true`), `POST /control/inject`, `POST /control/reset`, `GET /healthz`; response `id` derived from `chatcmpl-` + first 16 hex chars of sha256(request body), `created`, and `usage` are fixed constants (never the clock or a live count); response text and latency from `MOCKLLM_RESPONSE_TEXT`/`MOCKLLM_LATENCY_MS` (defaults: fixed sentence, 200ms); `http.Server` timeouts set explicitly: `ReadHeaderTimeout=5s`, `ReadTimeout=10s`, `WriteTimeout=10s`, `IdleTimeout=60s`. Failure injection keyed by invocation count or `logical_work_item_id`, modes `http500`/`close`/`delay-then-close`/`stale`; `close` hijacks and closes the connection after reading the full request with no response written; `stale` tracks connections via `http.Server.ConnState`/`ConnContext` and closes the flagged `net.Conn` on `StateIdle`. One invocation-ledger JSON line per call and one control-ledger line per `/control/*` call, both on stdout. TDD: 7 unit tests written first against `net/http/httptest` (RED: `undefined: Config`/`undefined: newServer`, build failed; GREEN: all 7 pass, including under `go test -race`), covering: identical request twice → identical response bytes; count-keyed injection fires exactly on the configured invocation; work-item-keyed injection fires only for that id; header attribution wins over the prompt-token fallback; prompt-token fallback works when headers are absent; SSE stream ends with a `finish_reason":"stop"` chunk then `data: [DONE]`; `close` mode yields a client-side connection error with no response. Base image `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot@sha256:afa5c872c891853ca7fcf1f12c3edb23f7eeef36189728842dd51042ff57f7ab`, resolved in this session via `docker buildx imagetools inspect gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot` (`crane` not installed on this machine; `imagetools inspect` queried the registry the same way `docker manifest inspect` does and was used as its documented fallback), pinned in `.ko.yaml` (`defaultPlatforms: [linux/arm64]`). Created a kind v0.33.0 cluster (`kind-config.yaml`: one control-plane + one worker node, both `kindest/node:v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5`, from `versions.yaml`), ran `make cluster-kind step-1` (`ko` 0.19.1 building `ko://github.com/AhmadMasry/agent-mesh-lab/fixtures/mockllm` for `linux/arm64/v8`, loaded into the kind cluster as `kind.local`, applied via `deploy/step-1-nomesh` → `deploy/base` — namespace `lab`, one-replica Deployment, readiness probe on `/healthz`, Service `mockllm:8080`), rollout succeeded. Ran `experiments/gate1-mockllm-deterministic.sh` for real against the running Service, driven from a throwaway `kubectl run` curl pod (`curlimages/curl:8.11.1`) inside the cluster, no retry logic in the script (a failed request is recorded once, not repeated): (1) reset, then 20 identical `POST /v1/chat/completions` requests with a fixed body and `X-Logical-Work-Item-Id: det-001`, hashing each response body; (2) reset, armed `close` at `at_count=5`, sent 6 requests under `det-002`, recorded which one failed; (3) reset, armed `close` keyed to `lwi=det-003`, sent 2 requests under `det-003` and 2 under `det-004`, recorded outcomes. Collected the invocation ledger for all four work items via `make ledgers LWI=<id>` (four calls, concatenated) into the run directory.
- Result: `experiments/runs/2026-09-05-mockllm-deterministic/` (`invocation.jsonl`, 30 lines; `summary.csv`). identical_hashes = 20 of 20 (all 20 `det-001` responses shared one sha256, `80e9166feb70b5a665e55074c36924644d9c18861be1495412e0b2fb06427591`); latency_min_ms = 200.264, latency_max_ms = 209.447 (against `MOCKLLM_LATENCY_MS=200`, all 20 ledger lines for `det-001`); count-keyed injection fired at invocation 5 of 6 for `det-002` (ledger outcomes: ok, ok, ok, ok, **closed**, ok — matching the client-observed HTTP statuses 200,200,200,200,**000**,200); lwi-keyed injection fired 2 of 2 for `det-003` (both `outcome":"closed"`) and 0 of 2 for `det-004` (both `outcome":"ok"`).
- Interpretation: As documented — the fixture is deterministic under this configuration: 20/20 byte-identical response hashes for identical request bodies, latency bounded within ~10ms of the configured 200ms (kind-cluster/kubectl-exec scheduling jitter, not response-content variance), and both injection-selection paths (invocation count and `logical_work_item_id`) fired exactly where configured and nowhere else, confirmed by both the client-observed HTTP outcome and the server's own invocation ledger. One incidental finding: the container's one non-JSON startup line (`log.Printf`, written to stderr but merged with stdout by the container runtime in `kubectl logs`) broke a naive `jq select(...)` over the combined log stream; the `ledgers` Makefile target reads with `jq -R 'fromjson? | select(...)'` to skip non-JSON lines, which is the general fix for any container log stream that isn't pure JSON end to end, not specific to this one line.
- Follow-up: none

## Gate 1 / go / single clean request — Do the three ledgers count one request as one?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.8.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: built `agents/worker` on a2a-go v2.5.0 (`a2asrv.NewHandler` around the lab executor; `a2asrv.NewJSONRPCHandler` mounted at `/`; `a2asrv.NewStaticAgentCardHandler` at `a2asrv.WellKnownAgentCardPath` = `/.well-known/agent-card.json`; the A2A mux behind the pre-dispatch ingress middleware, the readiness probe outside it; the execution ledger as a decorator embedding `a2asrv.RequestHandler` that wraps `SendMessage` and `SendStreamingMessage`; the executor writes a state line for every Task state it emits; one shared line writer for all three), `fixtures/loadgen` on the a2a-go client (`agentcard.NewResolver(hc).Resolve`, then `a2aclient.NewFromCard` with `WithDefaultsDisabled()` and `WithJSONRPCTransport(hc)`), and `internal/httpclient` (one hand-built `http.Transport`: HTTP/2 off, keep-alives on, explicit timeouts, no proxy, no idempotency header; used by the worker's model client and by loadgen; its doc comment records which net/http replay behaviour remains). The ingress ledger writes two lines per physical delivery sharing `ts_arrival` and `body_sha256`: an `arrival` line before the SDK sees the request and a `response` line with the status afterwards; deliveries are counted on arrival lines. The worker's model client makes one non-streaming `POST /chat/completions` per message with the headers `X-Logical-Work-Item-Id`, `X-A2A-Message-Id`, `X-A2A-Task-Id`, `X-Caller`. Eighteen Go unit tests in the worker, loadgen, and httpclient packages (`go test -race ./...`), including the ingress parser on request bodies recorded from the a2a-go v2.5.0 and a2a-python 1.1.2 clients against a request-dump listener and on a hand-written 0.3 `message/send` body. Deployed with `make step-1` (ko 0.19.1, kind v0.33.0, node image v1.37.0); `experiments/gate1-three-ledgers.sh` reset the mock, ran one loadgen Job (`backoffLimit: 0`) for `logical_work_item_id=clean-112913-001` (the id carries a per-run nonce because pod logs outlive runs), and collected the four ledgers with `make ledgers LWI=clean-112913-001 OUT=experiments/runs/2026-09-05-three-ledgers`. Worker server timeouts: read-header 10 s, read 30 s, write 120 s, idle 120 s; model client timeout 60 s (`MODEL_TIMEOUT_S`).
- Result: for work item `clean-112913-001`: deliveries at the ingress ledger 1 (arrival line: JSON-RPC method `SendMessage`, `a2a_version` = `1.0`, body 280 bytes; response line: status 200); dispatches 1; distinct `messageId`s 1; Tasks created 1 (execution state lines `TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED`, `TASK_STATE_WORKING`, `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`); result kind `task`, final state `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`; model invocations 1 (`caller` = `worker`, `injection` = `none`, `outcome` = `ok`, latency 202.165 ms), and the invocation line carries the same `messageId` and `taskId` as the execution lines; the client line reports `result_kind` = `task`, `state` = `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`, `a2a_version` = `1.0`, and the card advertised protocol version `1.0`. `summary.csv`: `1,1,1,1,1,TASK_STATE_COMPLETED,1,1.0,task` (deliveries_ingress_jsonrpc, ingress_arrivals_for_work_item, dispatches, distinct_message_ids, tasks_created, task_final_state, invocations, a2a_version_seen, client_result_kind). Run output: `experiments/runs/2026-09-05-three-ledgers/` (`ingress.jsonl`, `execution.jsonl`, `invocation.jsonl`, `client.jsonl`, `summary.csv`).
- Interpretation: one request became one delivery, one dispatch, one Task, and one model invocation, and all three ledgers agree on `messageId` and `taskId`, so the instruments count one as one under this configuration. Task-versus-Message is decided by the executor in a2a-go v2.5.0: the SDK rejects an executor whose first event is a status update ("execution failed before a task was created: first event must be a Task or a message") and creates the Task when the executor emits `a2a.NewSubmittedTask` first, in `TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED`; this executor always does, so a `taskId` exists for every dispatched message. The load client's agent-card `GET` is a separate physical delivery that the ingress ledger records, but it carries no work-item id, so the per-work-item collection excludes it; counts above are per work item. Both SDK clients, captured against a request-dump listener while the parser was written, send `A2A-Version: 1.0` with the method name `SendMessage`; the on-cluster capture that the wire-version box requires is Task 5's run, not this one.
- Follow-up: none

## Gate 1 / go receiver / baseline step 1 — Is the no-mesh baseline retry-free?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.8.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: `make verify-baseline` (`experiments/gate1-baseline.sh`, `STEP=1`, `REPS=5`) on the step-1 overlay (no mesh), run as three chunks (`RUNS="1 2 3"`, `"4 5 6"`, `"7"`) on 2026-09-05. Seven run types, five repetitions each, every repetition a fresh work item whose id carries a per-run nonce; before each repetition the mock is reset and one injection is armed for that work item; one loadgen Job (`backoffLimit: 0`, one `SendMessage`) per repetition; the four ledgers are collected with `make ledgers` after the Job ends (after a 10 s wait for run 3, whose injection delays the mock's ledger line by 8 s). Deliveries are the ingress ledger's arrival lines per receiver; dispatches are the worker's execution dispatch lines; invocations are the mock's lines by `caller`, excluding `stale-closed` lines, which record a connection close, not a call. Run 3 set the worker's `MODEL_TIMEOUT_S=5` (default 60 s); runs 5 and 6 set the orchestrator's `PLAN_MODEL_CALL=on` with `MODEL_MAX_RETRIES=0` and `=2` respectively; the script restores all three afterwards. Retries were off everywhere by construction: the a2a-go client has no retry option and uses `internal/httpclient` (hand-built `http.Transport`, HTTP/2 off, keep-alives on, no `Idempotency-Key`; `Request.GetBody` is set by `http.NewRequest` for the byte-reader bodies both binaries send, so net/http can rewind a body for its nothing-written redial, and only for that: a written POST without an idempotency header is never replayed); the worker's model client uses the same transport and treats any non-200 as failure; the a2a-python client is built on `httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=0))` (httpx 0.28.1; its default is also 0) and the SDK has no retry code; the openai client (3.8.0) is constructed with `max_retries=0` (its documented default `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 2`) over `httpx2.AsyncClient(transport=httpx2.AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=0))` (httpx2 2.12.0); the loadgen Job and the script never repeat a request. Run outputs: `experiments/runs/2026-09-05-baseline-step1/` (`summary.csv`, one directory per work item with the four ledgers).
- Result (per run type, identical across all 5 repetitions unless stated; counts are per work item):
  - run 1, `close` at the model, loadgen → worker: deliveries at the worker 1, dispatches 1, invocations 1 (`worker`, outcome `closed`), Task `TASK_STATE_FAILED` with the worker's error `model call: Post ".../v1/chat/completions": EOF`; client result `task` / failed. Second deliveries: 0 of 5.
  - run 2, `http500`: deliveries 1, dispatches 1, invocations 1 (`http500`), Task failed with `model call: status 500`. Second deliveries: 0 of 5.
  - run 3, `delay-then-close` after 8 s against a 5 s worker timeout: deliveries 1, dispatches 1, invocations 1 (outcome `delayed-close`, latency 8001 ms), Task failed with `net/http: timeout awaiting response headers (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`. Second deliveries: 0 of 5.
  - run 4, `close` at the model, loadgen → orchestrator (forward mode) → worker: deliveries at the orchestrator 1, at the worker 1, worker dispatches 1, invocations 1 (`worker`); the worker's Task failed with the EOF error and the orchestrator's Task failed with `downstream task <id> ended in TASK_STATE_FAILED: …`; no second delivery at either hop in any repetition.
  - run 5, `close` at the model for the orchestrator's own call (`PLAN_MODEL_CALL=on`, `MODEL_MAX_RETRIES=0`): deliveries at the orchestrator 1, at the worker 0, invocations 1 (`orchestrator`, outcome `closed`), Task failed with the openai client's `Connection error.`; the message was not forwarded.
  - run 6, positive control, same injection with the openai client at its documented default `MODEL_MAX_RETRIES=2`: deliveries at the orchestrator 1, invocations 3 (`orchestrator`, outcomes `closed`, `closed`, `closed`), Task failed. The instrument records the retries when they exist: 3 of 3 attempts counted in every repetition.
  - run 7, `stale`: two sequential requests per work item with the mock closing its idle keep-alive connection after each response: deliveries at the worker 2, dispatches 2, invocations 2 (both `stale-armed`, i.e. served normally), plus 2 `stale-closed` lines (the connection closes 0.09 to 0.2 ms after each response); both Tasks completed. The second request is a second Job for the same work item that replaces the first, so `client.jsonl` holds the second request's client line only; both requests appear in the ingress, execution, and invocation ledgers. One invocation per request in 5 of 5 repetitions.
  - `summary.csv`: 35 rows, one per repetition, columns `run,label,work_item,deliveries_worker,deliveries_orchestrator,dispatches_worker,invocations,invocations_by_caller,client_result,notes`.
- Interpretation: under this configuration the no-mesh baseline is retry-free by the ledgers, not by configuration: across 25 injected failures at the model endpoint (runs 1 to 5) every one produced exactly one delivery per hop, one dispatch, and one model invocation, and the failure surfaced as a failed Task at the receiver and, in forward mode, as a failed Task at the orchestrator too. The control (run 6) shows the same instrument counting three invocations when the openai client's default retries are left on, so a retry anywhere on this path would have been visible. Run 7 shows that a connection the model closed while idle did not cause a second invocation: Go's transport either discards a connection it has seen closed or redials before anything is written, and neither reaches the server twice; that redial is invisible to a server-side ledger by construction and cannot duplicate work, which is why the discriminating scenario is a request that was received and then failed (runs 1 to 5). Three instrument lessons were recorded on the way and are now built in: work-item ids carry a per-run nonce because pod logs outlive runs and a reused id collected an earlier run's lines as if they were a retry; an injection that delays the mock's response delays its ledger line, so collection waits for it; and the ingress ledger writes an arrival line before dispatch so a delivery whose handler never returns is still counted. Checklist box 4 is ticked when the same runs have been repeated with the agentgateway waypoint on the path (step 2).
- Follow-up: none

## Gate 1 / go receiver / baseline step 2 — Is the baseline retry-free with the agentgateway waypoint on the path?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.8.0

- Method: `make step-2` on the running step-1 cluster, then `STEP=2 REPS=5 RUNS="1 2 3 4" experiments/gate1-baseline.sh` in one invocation on 2026-09-05 (runs 5 to 7 belong to the step-1 entry and were not repeated: 5 and 6 exercise the orchestrator's own model client, which is not behind the waypoint, and 7 exercises Go's transport against the model, likewise not behind it). `make step-2` applies the pinned Gateway API v1.6.2 experimental CRDs, runs `istioctl install --set profile=ambient --set values.pilot.env.PILOT_ENABLE_AGENTGATEWAY=true -y` (the command and the `PILOT_ENABLE_AGENTGATEWAY` gate are from istio.io/latest/docs/ambient/usage/agentgateway/, fetched 2026-09-05; the waypoint access log is admissible as request-scoped path evidence because agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/latest/documentation/observability/access-logs/view/, fetched 2026-09-05, states that access logs are written to stdout automatically for every request that passes through the gateway proxy and that no policy configuration is required to enable them, so nothing was configured to produce them), applies `deploy/step-2-ambient-agw` (namespace `lab` labelled `istio.io/dataplane-mode: ambient`; a `Gateway` `agentgateway-waypoint` of class `istio-agentgateway-waypoint` with listener `mesh`/15008/HBONE and the annotation `gateway.istio.io/agentgatewayImage: cr.agentgateway.dev/agentgateway:v1.5.0`; `istio.io/use-waypoint: agentgateway-waypoint` on the `worker` Service only; an `HTTPRoute` `worker` parented on that Service **with no `retry` stanza**), and restarts the three Deployments because ztunnel captures a pod when the pod starts. Every install step succeeded on its first attempt: Gateway API v1.6.2 experimental applied with no CRD error, so v1.6.0 was not tried; the `istio-agentgateway-waypoint` GatewayClass was Accepted, so the `istio-agentgateway` ingress class was not tried; the waypoint pod became Ready running the requested agentgateway v1.5.0, so neither v1.4.1 nor v1.0.1 was tried; Kubernetes stayed at 1.37.0 and nothing failed in a way attributable to it. Retries were off everywhere exactly as recorded in the step-1 entry — the same binaries, images, and environment defaults — with the waypoint added as a fourth party that was measured and not configured.
- Result (per run type, identical across all 5 repetitions unless stated; counts are per work item; run output `experiments/runs/2026-09-05-baseline-step2/`, `summary.csv` 20 rows):
  - Path evidence (`experiments/runs/2026-09-05-baseline-step2/path-evidence.txt`), for one clean loadgen → worker request, work item `p2-162903-path-01`, Task completed: `istioctl ztunnel-config service` shows `lab/worker` bound to `WAYPOINT agentgateway-waypoint` while `lab/mockllm` and `lab/orchestrator` show `None`; `istioctl ztunnel-config workload` shows the three lab app pods at `PROTOCOL HBONE`; the `Gateway` is `Programmed=True` ("assigned to service(s) agentgateway-waypoint.lab.svc.cluster.local:15008") and the `HTTPRoute` `Accepted=True` under `controllerName: istio.io/agentgateway-waypoint-controller`; the agentgateway access log carries the request itself (`route=lab/worker … http.method=POST http.host=worker.lab.svc.cluster.local http.path=/ http.status=200 protocol=http duration=203ms`, endpoint `10.244.1.124:8080`); ztunnel logs the HBONE hop (`src.workload="loadgen-p2-162903-path-01-…" … dst.addr=10.244.1.121:15008 dst.hbone_addr=10.96.152.32:8080 dst.service="worker.lab.svc.cluster.local" dst.workload="agentgateway-waypoint-…"`); and the worker's own pre-dispatch ingress ledger records `remote` `10.244.1.121:50839`, the waypoint pod, where at step 1 the same field held the client pod's address.
  - Hops through the waypoint: loadgen → worker (runs 1 to 3) and orchestrator → worker (run 4). Not through it: loadgen → orchestrator in run 4 (the `orchestrator` Service carries no `use-waypoint` label; its 5 arrivals came from 5 distinct loadgen pod addresses) and worker → mockllm (ambient/HBONE, no waypoint). All 20 arrivals at the worker across the four runs came from `10.244.1.121`, the waypoint pod, and all 20 responses were 200.
  - run 1, `close` at the model, loadgen → worker: deliveries at the worker 1, dispatches 1, invocations 1 (`worker`, outcome `closed`), Task `TASK_STATE_FAILED` with `model call: Post "http://mockllm.lab.svc.cluster.local:8080/v1/chat/completions": EOF`; client result `task` / failed. Second deliveries: 0 of 5.
  - run 2, `http500`: deliveries 1, dispatches 1, invocations 1 (`http500`), Task failed with `model call: status 500`. Second deliveries: 0 of 5.
  - run 3, `delay-then-close` after 8 s against a 5 s worker timeout: deliveries 1, dispatches 1, invocations 1 (outcome `delayed-close`, latency 8001 to 8010 ms), Task failed with the worker's client timeout (4 of 5 `net/http: timeout awaiting response headers (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`, 1 of 5 `context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`; step 1 produced the same two strings in the opposite proportion, so which of net/http's two deadlines fires first is a race inside the worker's own client, not a mesh effect). Second deliveries: 0 of 5.
  - run 4, `close` at the model, loadgen → orchestrator (forward mode) → worker: deliveries at the orchestrator 1, at the worker 1, dispatches 1 at each, invocations 1 (`worker`); the worker's Task failed with the EOF error and the orchestrator's with `downstream task <id> ended in TASK_STATE_FAILED: model call: … EOF`. Second deliveries: 0 of 5 at either hop.
  - Totals over the 20 work items: 20 deliveries at the worker, 20 dispatches, 20 model invocations (10 `closed`, 5 `delayed-close`, 5 `http500`), 20 client results `task/TASK_STATE_FAILED`, 5 deliveries and 5 dispatches at the orchestrator.
  - The waypoint's own count, as a fourth party (`waypoint-access-log.txt`, 38 lines): 21 `POST /` — the 20 baseline deliveries plus the one path-proof request — and 17 `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json`; every line `http.status=200`, `route=lab/worker`. So the waypoint logged exactly one POST per work item, 20 of 20, matching the receiver's ingress ledger. The 17 card fetches are 16 from the 16 one-shot loadgen Jobs that talked to the worker and 1 from the long-lived orchestrator, which resolved the worker's card once and reused it for all five run-4 requests. POST durations, mapped to runs by source address and by the container runtime's timestamp on the same line against each work item's `ts_arrival`: 1 to 2 ms for run 1, 202 to 204 ms for run 2, 1 to 42 ms for run 4, 5002 to 5005 ms for run 3, and 203 ms for the path-proof request. That is the shape the invocation ledger predicts — the mock closes at once for `close` (runs 1 and 4, `latency_ms` 0.018 to 0.041) and serves its fixed 200 ms latency before the 500 (run 2, 200.758 to 201.284 ms) — and for run 3 it means the waypoint held that single request open for the worker's whole 5 s timeout rather than abandoning and re-sending it.
  - Request unchanged across the hop: the worker's ingress ledger recorded `a2a_version` `1.0` and `body_len` 278 for all 15 a2a-go bodies and 297 for all 5 a2a-python bodies, the same byte counts as the corresponding step-1 work items (`b1-113315-r1-01` 278, `b1-113947-r4-01` 297), whose ids are the same length.
  - Observed agentgateway on the running waypoint pod: image `cr.agentgateway.dev/agentgateway:v1.5.0`, imageID `cr.agentgateway.dev/agentgateway@sha256:bf2f339ef326d32def2aaeb44b1b4549801293c19b89e764a4228667d97d9896`, and the binary's own startup line `"version": "1.5.0", "git_revision": "fe6732474a96a0363dfb9822859af4e9bab360fa"`. Recorded in `versions.yaml` under `agentgateway.observed` with the commands used.
- Interpretation: under this configuration the baseline stays retry-free with the agentgateway waypoint between caller and receiver: across 20 injected failures every work item produced exactly one delivery per hop, one dispatch, and one model invocation, and the waypoint's own access log independently counted one POST per work item, so no layer retried — not the client, not the SDK, not the model client, and not the gateway under its default configuration, which is a reportable result rather than an absence of one. Two limits on what this measures should be carried into Gate 3. First, the injected failure sits behind the worker, so the waypoint saw `http.status=200` on all 21 requests and never met a response class it might retry; the R2 row, which puts an experimental `retry` stanza on this same `HTTPRoute`, is what will exercise that, and it can now be read against a counted no-retry baseline on the identical path. Second, the waypoint was inserted without changing what the receiver saw: same protocol version, same body length, one 200 per request, and the only visible difference in the ledgers is the peer address, which is now the waypoint rather than the client — worth knowing before Gate 2 attributes a second delivery to a layer. Two incidental observations from the waypoint at this version: it logged `warn proxy::gateway hbone error: drain timeout` when short-lived loadgen Jobs exited mid-connection (4 lines over 21 requests) plus 2 `warn agent_hbone::client:inbound HBONE ping timeout/error` lines, neither class correlated with a second delivery (`waypoint-warnings.txt`, 6 lines), and it renders the sub-second part of its own log timestamps with leading zeros stripped, so 6 of 38 access-log lines — the ones whose printed fraction is shorter than six digits — show a fraction up to a hundred times larger than the container runtime's timestamp for the same line, and two lines can read as out of order (a further 4 of the 38 differ from the container runtime in the first three fraction digits by ordinary sub-millisecond clock skew of 81 to 471 µs, which is not the same effect and is not counted as one); that is a logging defect, not a traffic one, and the counts above come from the ledgers rather than from those timestamps.
- Follow-up: docs/upstream/agentgateway-access-log-timestamp-leading-zeros.md — filed as https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/issues/3369 (2026-09-08); fixed upstream by https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/pull/3370, merged the same day; v1.5.0 as pinned here still carries the defect

- Method: on 2026-09-07 the kind cluster from the 2026-09-05 runs was deleted (`make teardown`, 1 s; `kind get clusters` then reported none) and everything was rebuilt from the committed tree, in the order the README documents, with no edit to any script, manifest, or Makefile target: `make cluster-kind` (19 s), `make step-1` (60 s), `make verify-baseline` (887 s ≈ 14 m 47 s; `STEP=1`, `REPS=5`, the default `RUNS="1 2 3 4 5 6 7"`, one invocation, run with `run_in_background` and polled because a single foreground call is capped at 10 minutes), `make step-2` (178 s), then `STEP=2 REPS=5 RUNS="1 2 3 4" experiments/gate1-baseline.sh` (471 s ≈ 7 m 51 s, one invocation). On the rebuilt cluster the pins were re-observed rather than assumed: `kubectl version` server `v1.37.0` from the digest-pinned node image in `kind-config.yaml`, `istioctl version` control plane 1.31.0 and data plane 1.31.0, and before the step-2 run the waypoint pod reported image `cr.agentgateway.dev/agentgateway:v1.5.0`, imageID `cr.agentgateway.dev/agentgateway@sha256:bf2f339ef326d32def2aaeb44b1b4549801293c19b89e764a4228667d97d9896`, and the startup line `"version": "1.5.0", "git_revision": "fe6732474a96a0363dfb9822859af4e9bab360fa"` — the same three values already recorded under `agentgateway.observed` in `versions.yaml`, so the observed version did not differ.   - Step 2, same six columns, reference then reproduced, over 5 of 5 repetitions each: run 1 `1/0/1/1/worker=1/task/TASK_STATE_FAILED` vs the same; run 2 the same; run 3 the same; run 4 `1/1/1/1/worker=1/task/TASK_STATE_FAILED` vs the same.
  - Row-by-row: both diffs are empty with `work_item` blanked, so the `run`, `label`, five count, and `notes` columns are byte-identical to 2026-09-05 for all 55 repetitions.
  - Ledger detail behind the counts, reference vs reproduced: invocation `caller`/`outcome` tallies identical at both steps (step 1: 5 `worker/closed`, 5 `worker/http500`, 5 `worker/delayed-close`, 5 `worker/closed`, 5 `orchestrator/closed`, 15 `orchestrator/closed`, 10 `worker/stale-armed` + 10 `worker/stale-closed`; step 2: 10 `worker/closed`, 5 `worker/delayed-close`, 5 `worker/http500`); failure strings identical (`model call: … EOF`, `model call: status 500`, `Connection error.`, `downstream task <id> ended in TASK_STATE_FAILED: …`); every ingress arrival at both steps recorded `a2a_version` `1.0` with `body_len` 278 for the a2a-go bodies and 297 for the a2a-python ones, the same byte counts as 2026-09-05; and at step 2 all 20 worker arrivals came from one address, the waypoint pod (`10.244.1.55` today, `10.244.1.121` on 2026-09-05), while the 5 orchestrator arrivals came from 5 distinct loadgen pod addresses, the same shape as the reference.
  - The waypoint's own count as a fourth party (`waypoint-access-log.txt`, 36 lines): 20 `POST /` and 16 `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json`, every line `http.status=200`, `route=lab/worker` — exactly one POST per work item, 20 of 20, matching the receiver's ingress ledger. The reference file has 38 lines, 21 POST and 17 GET; the extra pair is its one path-proof request (`p2-162903-path-01`), which this reproduction did not run, so 20 baseline POSTs and 15 one-shot loadgen card fetches plus 1 from the long-lived orchestrator are the same per-request counts. POST durations, mapped to runs by source address as the reference maps them, fall in the same four groups: 1–2 ms for run 1, 201–203 ms for run 2 (the mock's fixed 200 ms latency before the 500), 5001–5009 ms for run 3 (the worker's whole 5 s timeout held open on one request), and 1–42 ms for run 4, whose 5 POSTs all came from the one long-lived orchestrator address.
  - Differences, all outside the six compared counts and reported as observed: work-item ids carry today's per-run nonces (`b1-203920-*`, `b2-205951-*`); timestamps, pod addresses, and latency values within the same order differ; run 3's two net/http deadline strings landed 3 `context deadline exceeded` to 2 `net/http: timeout awaiting response headers` at step 1 (reference 4:1) and 2 to 3 at step 2 (reference 1:4), the documented race inside the worker's own client; the waypoint's warning lines number 12 today (10 `hbone error: drain timeout`, 2 `HBONE ping timeout/error`) against 6 on 2026-09-05 (4 and 2), a larger count of the same two classes, and as before neither class coincided with a second delivery — all 20 work items counted 1; and the access-log timestamp defect reproduced at this version, 3 of 36 lines carrying a sub-second fraction shorter than six digits against 6 of 38 in the reference.
- Interpretation: both baselines reproduce from a deleted cluster on the committed tree alone — as documented. Every one of the 55 repetitions produced the same delivery, dispatch, invocation, caller and client-result counts as the corresponding 2026-09-05 repetition, at both steps, and the two summary files are byte-identical to the reference once the per-run work-item nonce is set aside; the run-6 control again counted 3 invocations where the openai client's default retries are left on, so the instrument that would have shown a retry was working in this cluster too, and the waypoint again counted one POST per work item on its own. What varied between the two dates is only what the ledgers do not count: identities, addresses, timestamps, latencies within an order, which of net/http's two deadlines won a race, and how many `drain timeout` warnings the waypoint emitted while short-lived loadgen Jobs exited mid-connection — 10 today against 4, on the same 20 requests that each arrived exactly once. Two limits on what this checks. The reproduction is clean at the cluster level only: the host still held the kind node image, the Paketo builder and run images, so a machine without them would additionally have to pull them, and `make step-1` showed the tree needs Docker Hub reachable for the buildpacks lifecycle image whether or not the builder is cached. Neither page could be fetched from agentgateway.dev on this machine, which did not resolve the host; both were read from the website project's own source files at `assets/agw-docs/pages/integrations/istio/ambient/ambient-{ingress,egress}.md` in github.com/agentgateway/website, as was the install snippet `assets/agw-docs/snippets/agentgateway/get-started.md`. `make step-2b` runs the two documented Helm installs (`helm upgrade -i agentgateway-crds … --create-namespace --namespace agentgateway-system --version v1.5.0`, then `helm upgrade -i agentgateway … --version v1.5.0 --wait`; both reported `STATUS: deployed`, `REVISION: 1` on the first attempt, `experiments/runs/2026-09-08-baseline-step2b/step-2b-install.txt`), labels `agentgateway-system` ambient as the ingress page does, applies `deploy/step-2b-agw-ingress-egress` with `ko apply` like the other steps, and waits for both Gateways to be Programmed and for the rollouts. `ko apply` rebuilds the Go images, so it rotated the mock as well as the two agents at the step-2b apply and the mock's invocation ledger starts from that point; the path proof and the baseline both ran afterwards, so no counted request spans that restart. Four recorded departures from the documented commands and manifests, each forced by this cluster or this lab rather than chosen: (1) the documented `--set controller.image.pullPolicy=Always` is omitted, because a pinned tag is not re-pulled; (2) the pages' generated Service is a LoadBalancer reached with `kubectl port-forward`, and kind has no load balancer and every request here is sent from inside the cluster, so `AgentgatewayParameters` forces both Services to ClusterIP; (3) the ingress page pins a listener hostname and the egress page routes to httpbin.org on port 80, whereas this ingress listener matches any host and the egress destination is the lab's mock addressed as `model.lab.internal` on 8080, with the `agentgateway.dev/internal-ports` annotation and the `inner-http` listener set to 8080 as the egress page's step 9 instructs; the egress page's `ResponseHeaderModifier` filter is not used, since the ledgers count the hop; (4) the documentation installs Gateway API 1.6.0 and this lab keeps its pinned v1.6.2 experimental CRDs, already installed by `make step-2` and not reapplied. One thing the pages do not anticipate, and the only change to an agent's own configuration: an A2A client is built from the agent card, so the card's advertised interface URL is what a client sends to. `fixtures/loadgen` calls `a2aclient.NewFromCard`, which takes its endpoint from the card, so a client pointed at the ingress would have fetched the card through the gateway and then sent the request straight to the agent's own Service. The step-2b overlay therefore patches the orchestrator's `PUBLIC_URL` to the ingress Service address, which is how A2A addresses an agent that sits behind a gateway; the worker's `PUBLIC_URL` is unchanged. Both agents' `MODEL_BASE_URL` moves from the mock's Service to `http://model.lab.internal:8080/v1`, the external host of a `MESH_EXTERNAL` ServiceEntry whose single endpoint address is `mockllm.lab.svc.cluster.local`: the mock stays in the cluster and is modelled as the external provider, so pointing this at a real provider later is a change of host rather than of shape, and the egress page's instruction to keep the client pointed at the backend address rather than the waypoint address is followed. The istiod-driven ingress Gateway added to step 2 on 2026-09-08 (class `istio-agentgateway`) and its HTTPRoute were deleted from the cluster and removed from the step-2 overlay; no experiment had ever routed through them. Retries stayed off everywhere exactly as the step-1 and step-2 entries record — same binaries, same images, same environment defaults, `MODEL_MAX_RETRIES=0` — and none of the three HTTPRoutes carries a `retry` stanza; the two new proxies were measured and not configured, with no agentgateway-native policy resource applied to either. Before the run `istioctl ztunnel-config certificates --node agent-mesh-lab-worker` reported `VALID CERT true` with `NOT AFTER 2026-09-09T19:21:16Z`, so ztunnel was not restarted. `go test ./...` and `uv run pytest -q` in `agents/orchestrator/` were unchanged (4 packages ok, 18 passed).

That is exactly one POST per run-4 work item, 5 of 5, matching the orchestrator's ingress ledger, plus one card fetch per run-4 loadgen Job and the one from the path proof. The 5 POSTs came from 5 distinct loadgen pod addresses, each reusing the source port of its own card fetch. POST durations 47 to 104 ms.

Of the 20: 10 `http.status=503` with `error="upstream call failed: SendRequest: connection closed before message completed" reason=UpstreamFailure` (runs 1 and 4, where the mock closes the connection), 5 `http.status=500` passed through from the mock (run 2), and 5 with no status at all and `duration=5000` to `5002ms` (run 3, where the worker's 5 s client timeout cancelled the request while the mock was still holding it for 8 s). Every line `route=agentgateway-egress/model-via-agw`, `endpoint=mockllm.lab.svc.cluster.local:8080`.

The invocation count did not change — 1 per work item at both steps — so this is a change in what the caller can distinguish, not in what happened.
  - Observed on the running proxies: the ingress and the egress pods both report image `cr.agentgateway.dev/agentgateway:v1.5.0`, imageID `cr.agentgateway.dev/agentgateway@sha256:bf2f339ef326d32def2aaeb44b1b4549801293c19b89e764a4228667d97d9896`, and the startup line `"version": "1.5.0", "git_revision": "fe6732474a96a0363dfb9822859af4e9bab360fa"` — the same build the istiod-driven waypoint already runs; the controller reports `cr.agentgateway.dev/controller:v1.5.0`, imageID `cr.agentgateway.dev/controller@sha256:319489cb86b7f901a52a3fc532ad07f136c92756f88cf02a4040909e20001120`. Recorded in `versions.yaml` under `agentgateway-controlplane.observed` with the commands used.
  - Warnings over the run: the ingress logged none. The egress logged 2 `warn proxy::gateway hbone error: drain timeout`. The waypoint logged 12 `drain timeout`, 2 `HBONE ping timeout/error`, and 1 xDS reconnect (`XDS client error … retrying in 10ms`) at 19:52:55, while the new control plane's CRDs were being reconciled. No warning of any class coincided with a second delivery: all 20 work items counted 1.
- Interpretation: under this configuration the baseline stays retry-free with an agentgateway ingress in front of Agent A and an agentgateway egress waypoint in front of the model, both driven by agentgateway's own control plane, on top of the istiod-driven waypoint between the two agents. Across 20 injected failures every work item produced exactly one delivery per hop, one dispatch, and one model invocation, and each of the three proxies independently counted one request per work item on its own path segment — 5 POSTs at the ingress, 20 at the egress, 21 at the waypoint including the path proof — so no layer retried: not the client, not either SDK, not the model client, and not any of the three gateways under their default configuration. Every count column matches the step-2 reference for all 20 repetitions, which is the point of the comparison: two proxies were added to the path and the counts did not move. Three things this run establishes for later gates. First, the egress proxy is now the layer that meets the model's failure, and at this version it converts a mid-response connection close into `503 UpstreamFailure` and a client-cancelled request into an access-log line with no status; a caller behind it can no longer tell a transport failure from an upstream 5xx, which is exactly the distinction Experiment C has to map, and it also means the egress is the first hop in this lab that sees a response class a proxy could plausibly retry. Second, the request reached the receiver unchanged through both new hops: same protocol version, same body length for the id length, one 200 per request, and the only difference visible in the ledgers is the peer address, which at Agent A is now the ingress pod. Third, the two control planes coexisted without contention — istiod kept the waypoint Programmed and serving while the agentgateway controller provisioned and programmed two Gateways of its own class — and that division is what the proposal note says Experiment C must state per hop, since only the two proxies under agentgateway's own control plane can receive agentgateway-native policy.
- Follow-up: none

- Method: on 2026-09-08 the orchestrator's model client was re-pinned from openai-python 3.8.0 to 3.9.0 (PyPI release of the same day; `uv lock` moved only that package, its HTTP client httpx2 stays 2.12.0; the local environment was rebuilt from the lockfile with `uv sync`, which also removed 37 packages that were installed but absent from the lockfile; `uv run pytest -q` 18 passed; the runtime reports `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 2` as the source at tag v3.9.0 does). The orchestrator image was rebuilt with `make orchestrator-image`, loaded on both nodes, and rolled out at 20:32:33Z; `kubectl exec` into the new pod reports openai 3.9.0. Then `STEP=2b RUN_ITEM=2026-09-08-openai-3.9.0-runs-5-6 REPS=5 RUNS="5 6" experiments/gate1-baseline.sh` on the step-2b cluster: run 5 sets the orchestrator's `PLAN_MODEL_CALL=on MODEL_MAX_RETRIES=0`, run 6 the openai default `MODEL_MAX_RETRIES=2`, both with a `close` injection keyed to the orchestrator's own model call; the script restored both variables afterwards (verified on the Deployment: `PLAN_MODEL_CALL=off`, `MODEL_MAX_RETRIES=0`). Path at step 2b: loadgen fetches the agent card from the orchestrator Service, the card advertises the ingress, so the `SendMessage` POST enters through the agentgateway ingress; the orchestrator's model call goes to `model.lab.internal` through the agentgateway egress waypoint to the mock. Runs 5 and 6 were last counted at step 1 on 3.8.0 (entry of 2026-09-05); they were not part of the step-2 or step-2b baselines. Run outputs: `experiments/runs/2026-09-08-openai-3.9.0-runs-5-6/` (`summary.csv` 10 rows, one directory per work item with the four ledgers, `egress-access-log.txt` with the egress lines from the rollout onward).
- Result (per run type, identical across all 5 repetitions; counts per work item):
  - run 5, `max_retries=0`: deliveries at the orchestrator 1 (all 10 arrivals of runs 5 and 6 from the ingress pod 10.244.1.92), at the worker 0, invocations 1 (`orchestrator`, outcome `closed`), Task `TASK_STATE_FAILED`. Reference at step 1: 1. Reproduced 5 of 5.
  - run 6, control, `max_retries=2`: invocations 3 (`orchestrator`, `closed` ×3), Task failed. Reference at step 1: 3. Reproduced 5 of 5.
  - Totals across the 10 work items: 20 invocations, all `orchestrator/closed`; the egress access log holds 20 POSTs to `/v1/chat/completions` for the same window, every one `http.status=503` with `src.identity=spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default`, i.e. one egress line per model attempt, 5 for run 5 and 15 for run 6.
  - Failure shape changed with the egress on the path: the orchestrator's Task error is now `upstream call failed: SendRequest: connection closed before message completed` in all 10 work items, the egress gateway's 503 body relayed by the openai client, where at step 1 the same injection produced the client's own `Connection error.`.
- Interpretation: as documented. openai-python 3.9.0 behaves as 3.8.0 did under this configuration: with `max_retries=0` one injected failure is one model invocation, and with the documented default of 2 the same failure is three invocations, 5 of 5 repetitions each, so the positive control still shows the instrument counting retries when they exist. The egress waypoint converts the mock's connection close into an HTTP 503 towards the client, and the openai client retries that 503 under its default exactly as it retried the raw connection error at step 1; the egress itself added no attempt, 20 egress lines for 20 mock invocations. The path through the ingress for the client leg is a consequence of the agent card advertising the gateway and is stated so that the counts are read against the right topology. From this entry on, entries cite openai-python=3.9.0; the earlier Gate 1 entries ran on 3.8.0 and stay as recorded.
- Follow-up: none

## Gate 2 / instruments / single clean request — Do the ledgers count one request as one after the executor-entry line?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.9.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: the three instruments changed before any Gate 2 agent behaviour, then one clean request per receiver was counted through them. What changed: (1) each executor writes an `execute` line at its own entry, carrying the message id, the work item, and the task and context ids, before the first Task state it emits, so a dispatch now means the executor ran rather than that the SDK accepted a request; (2) the wrapper's entry event was renamed `dispatch` to `received` in both agents, and the three Gate 1 scripts now count dispatches from `event=="execute"`; (3) each receiver gained `POST /control/inject` and `POST /control/reset` in front of the ingress ledger, arming one injection per work item that fires once and disarms itself, so a later task can fail a request that has already been counted as arrived; (4) the Python ingress middleware's replayed `receive` now hands the rest of the ASGI conversation back to the real `receive` after replaying the body it read, where it previously answered every later call with a synthetic `http.disconnect`; (5) three fixture fixes: the mock rejects `at_count` below 1, writes its invocation line from a `defer` so a call is counted even when serving it does not finish, and the load client's request builder moved to `internal/a2areq` for the replay harness to share. Nothing was armed for this run: both receivers and the mock were reset before each request, and `experiments/runs/2026-09-09-instruments-single-clean/control-endpoints.txt` probes both control endpoints in-cluster and leaves both injectors unarmed. Pins were re-fetched and none moved, so `versions.yaml` is unchanged (`pins-check.txt` in the same directory: a2a-go still v2.5.0, a2a-sdk still 1.1.2 on PyPI, httpx 0.28.1 in the lockfile with `retries: int = 0` on both transports, a connect-failure retry only, passed through to httpcore 1.0.9, which repeats the connect attempt on `ConnectError`/`ConnectTimeout` and nothing else). Both agents were rebuilt and rolled out before the run: the worker through the step-2b overlay with `ko apply`, the orchestrator with `make orchestrator-image`; `istioctl ztunnel-config certificates --node agent-mesh-lab-worker` showed `VALID CERT true` for `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default` before the run and no ztunnel restart was needed. Unit tests: 40 Go tests across the four packages that have them and 28 Python tests, all passing. Run: `experiments/gate2-single-clean.sh`, one clean loadgen request per receiver, no repetitions; output `experiments/runs/2026-09-09-instruments-single-clean/`.
- Result (`summary.csv`, two rows; per-work-item counts scoped to the named receiver's own ledgers, except invocations, which are counted for the work item as a whole because a forwarded work item's model call is made downstream):
  - `worker,g2c-010813-worker,1,1,1,1,1,task/TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` — 1 delivery, 1 `received`, 1 `execute`, 1 Task with a `TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED` line, 1 model invocation (`caller worker`, `injection none`, `outcome ok`), client result a completed Task. Path: loadgen to the worker Service through the istiod-driven waypoint; the arrival came from `10.244.1.55`, the waypoint pod.
  - `orchestrator,g2c-010813-orchestrator,1,1,1,1,1,task/TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` — the same five counts at the orchestrator, and the same five again at the worker it forwards to (its execution ledger holds `received,execute,state,state,state,result` for each of the two agents, 12 lines for the work item). The single model invocation is the worker's. Path: the card was fetched from the orchestrator Service and advertises the agentgateway ingress, so the `SendMessage` POST entered through it; the arrival at the orchestrator came from `10.244.1.92`, the ingress pod, and the arrival at the worker from the waypoint.
  - Every arrival carried `a2a_version` `1.0` and every response was 200. No ingress line in either work item carries an `injection` field, which is the unarmed path recorded: the field appears only when an injection fires. Two shapes to filter on from here: an arrival line carries no `status` key at all, and a response line always carries one, including an explicit 0 for a connection closed before any status was written. Both receivers emit it the same way.
  - Control endpoints, probed in-cluster after the run (`control-endpoints.txt`): both receivers answer `POST /control/reset` 204, `POST /control/inject` 204 for an armed work item, 400 for an unknown mode and for a missing `lwi`, and 405 for a GET on either path. The Go receiver arms `close-after-read` (204); the Python one rejects it 400 with `{"error":"close-after-read is not supported by this receiver"}`. Both were reset last, so nothing is left armed.
  - Buildpacks exclude (`image-exclude.txt`): `agents/orchestrator/project.toml` excludes `.venv`, `.pytest_cache`, and `tests`, and after `make orchestrator-image` the application directory in the image holds only `.python-version`, `Procfile`, `orchestrator`, `project.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, and `uv.lock` — the three paths are gone. **pytest is still importable in the image**, from `/layers/paketo-buildpacks_python-package-managers-run/uv-env/venv/`, not from any excluded path. `paketo-buildpacks/python-package-managers-run` 0.6.3 runs plain `uv sync` with no `--no-dev` (`pkg/packagers/uv/uv_runner.go`, `args := []string{"sync"}`; its only group variable, `BP_UV_INSTALL_GROUPS`, adds groups and cannot remove one), and uv includes the `dev` group by default, which is where `pytest==9.1.1` comes from in `uv.lock`.
  - One behaviour found and fixed while measuring, before the recorded run: the Go worker first registered its control routes with method-qualified patterns (`POST /control/inject`), so a GET fell through to the catch-all and was answered 200 by the A2A JSON-RPC handler and written to the ingress ledger. The in-cluster probe caught it; the unit tests did not, because they called the handlers directly. The routes are now registered without a method, the handler's own 405 applies, and `TestControl_RoutedMethodNotAllowedAndNotLedgered` asserts the routed contract through the same mux the process serves. The worker was rebuilt and rolled out, and the recorded run is from the fixed build.
- Interpretation: as documented for the counts. After the executor-entry line, one clean request is still one delivery, one `received`, one `execute`, one Task, and one model invocation at every receiver on both paths, so renaming the wrapper's event and adding an earlier line changed what "dispatched" means without changing what is counted. That is the point of doing it before the replay work: from here a `received` without a matching `execute` is a request the SDK accepted and never dispatched, which is exactly the case a duplicate delivery or an injected failure has to be told apart from. The injection hooks exist on both receivers and are unarmed, and the one asymmetry is recorded rather than hidden: the Go receiver can hijack a connection and close it, the Python one cannot do so portably under ASGI and says so at the control endpoint, which is why A.2's close-after-read trigger is the Go receiver. Two things did not come out as the plan expected. The Buildpacks exclude removed the three paths from the image but not pytest, because pytest is installed by the buildpack's own `uv sync` from the lockfile's dev group, not carried in from the excluded directories; removing it would take changing the lockfile's default groups, which would also take `uv run pytest -q` with it, so the exclude is recorded for what it does and the dev group is left alone. And the control routes needed a second pass: the unit tests asserted the handlers and the cluster probe asserted the routing, and only the second one saw the fall-through, which is the argument for probing an instrument in the place it will be used before trusting it to count.
- Follow-up: none

## Gate 2 / go receiver / A.1 M1 exact transport replay — When the identical request arrives twice, what does a2a-go do?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.9.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: `MODE=M1 RECEIVER=go REPS=20 experiments/gate2-a1.sh`, one invocation on 2026-09-09 covering both stimulus paths, twenty repetitions each, forty in all. Each repetition is one `make replay`, which is the duplicate-delivery harness `fixtures/replay` in mode M1: one `SendMessage` body built from `internal/a2areq` and delivered twice over one client with retries off, the second delivery byte-identical to the first — same JSON-RPC `id`, same A2A `messageId`, same bytes. Two deliveries per work item and no more; the harness has no retry logic and neither does the script, and a repetition that failed would have been recorded in the row's `notes` and never re-run. **Topology, as measured in Task 1 and unchanged here**: each receiver Service is bound to an istiod-driven agentgateway waypoint of its own and the two are not shared — `Service/worker` to `agentgateway-waypoint`, `Service/orchestrator` to `agentgateway-waypoint-orch`, two waypoint instances in `lab` — so the in-cluster stimulus is a ztunnel-captured Job that reaches the worker through the worker Service's own waypoint, while the external stimulus runs the harness on the host through a `kubectl port-forward` to the agentgateway ingress Service — port-forward is a TCP tunnel and not an HTTP proxy, so it forwards bytes and rewrites nothing and the `Host: worker.lab.internal` the harness sets is what the gateway matches on — and the ingress dials the worker pod on 15008 rather than the Service VIP, so no waypoint is on that hop. Nothing was armed: `POST http://worker.lab.svc.cluster.local:8080/control/reset` answered 204 before the run (`control-reset.txt`), the mock was reset before every repetition, and no ingress line in the whole run carries an `injection` field. `istioctl ztunnel-config certificates --node agent-mesh-lab-worker` showed `VALID CERT true` for `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default` before the run and no ztunnel restart was needed (`certificates.txt`). No Deployment was changed: the script's model-mode switch applies to `RECEIVER=py` only, and the worker is in model mode as deployed. Work-item ids carry a per-run nonce, because pod logs outlive a run and a repeated id would collect an earlier run's lines as if they were this run's. **Counting rules**: `deliveries` are the worker's pre-dispatch ingress arrival lines with `method == "SendMessage"`; `executes` are executor-entry lines (`event == "execute"`, what a dispatch has meant since Task 0), not the SDK's `received`; `distinct_message_ids` is `unique` over those arrivals' `messageId`; `tasks_created` is `unique` over the `taskId` of `TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED` lines; `invocations` are the mock's invocation lines excluding `stale-closed`; the second response's shape and its `taskId` come from the harness's own attempt-2 client line, and `same_task` compares that `taskId` with attempt 1's. The pins are unchanged from the previous entry and are cited from `versions.yaml`. What the running cluster itself reports is committed as `cluster-versions.txt` in the run directory, captured with read-only commands after the run on the same cluster: istio 1.31.0 for client, control plane and data plane, `cr.agentgateway.dev/agentgateway:v1.5.0` on both Gateway pods, and kubelet v1.37.0 on both nodes. That file also names the two Gateway pods with the addresses the Result cites, and both pods were created before the run. **Every timestamp in the committed ledgers is UTC**, so they read 2026-09-08 for a run this entry dates 2026-09-09: local time is UTC+3 and the run directory is named by the local date. Wall time, from those UTC client-line timestamps: 6 min 33 s for the twenty in-cluster repetitions (23:33:51 to 23:40:24), 1 min 15 s for the twenty external ones (23:40:30 to 23:41:45).
- Result (`experiments/runs/2026-09-09-a1-m1-go/`, `summary.csv`, forty rows; `notes` is empty on every row):
  - `waypoint` (in-cluster, through the worker's istiod-driven agentgateway waypoint) — 2 deliveries in 20 of 20; 2 executes in 20 of 20; 1 distinct `messageId` in 20 of 20; 2 tasks created in 20 of 20; 2 model invocations in 20 of 20. Second response: HTTP 200, `task`/`TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` in 20 of 20, naming a `taskId` different from attempt 1's in 20 of 20. All 40 arrivals came from `10.244.1.55`, the `agentgateway-waypoint` pod.
  - `ingress` (out-of-cluster, through the agentgateway ingress, no waypoint on the hop) — 2 deliveries in 20 of 20; 2 executes in 20 of 20; 1 distinct `messageId` in 20 of 20; 2 tasks created in 20 of 20; 2 model invocations in 20 of 20. Second response: HTTP 200, `task`/`TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` in 20 of 20, naming a `taskId` different from attempt 1's in 20 of 20. All 40 arrivals came from `10.244.1.92`, the `agentgateway-ingress` pod.
  - The stimulus held: each of the forty work items has exactly two client lines sharing one `(id, messageId, body_sha256)` triple, so the second delivery was byte-identical on all forty. The first response was HTTP 200 `task`/`TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` in 40 of 40 as well, so both paths answered both copies.
  - Ledger detail, identical on both paths: every work item's execution ledger holds `received=2, execute=2, state=6, result=2`, and the two `execute` lines carry two distinct `taskId`s; the six `state` lines are `TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED`, `TASK_STATE_WORKING`, `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` for each of the two Tasks. All 80 model invocations are `caller worker`, `outcome ok`, no injection, and for every work item the two invocation `taskId`s are exactly the two `execute` `taskId`s, so each duplicate's model call is attributable to its own Task. All 160 ingress-ledger lines are the worker's and none the orchestrator's, so nothing was forwarded; all 80 arrivals carry `a2a_version` `1.0`; all 80 response lines carry status 200.
  - Latency, the one measured difference between the paths: through the waypoint the first attempt took 311 ms on average against 206 ms for the second, while through the ingress the two attempts took 213 ms and 209 ms. The ledgers count the same thing on both paths; what the extra 100 ms on the first in-cluster attempt is was not investigated here.
- Interpretation: as documented. Under this configuration a2a-go v2.5.0 does not deduplicate an exact transport replay: it accepts the second delivery, dispatches it to the executor, creates a second Task, calls the model a second time, and answers with the new Task, on both stimulus paths and in 20 of 20 repetitions each. Two deliveries of one `messageId` produced two of everything downstream, which is the "does the work again" arm of the question and not the "deduplicates" or "returns the same Task" arm. The SDK says as much itself: `internal/taskexec/local_manager.go` mints a fresh `a2a.NewTaskID()` for any message that carries no `TaskID`, and `createExecution` keys only on that `TaskID`, above the comment `TODO(yarolegovich): handle idempotency once spec establishes the key`; message-level deduplication exists in v2.5.0 only as an extension point on the cluster-mode work queue, whose `Lease.TaskID` may return a different id "to support idempotency (e.g. dedup by message ID and map to an existing TaskID)", and this lab runs the local manager. The specification at the pinned commit agrees that this is conformant: §3.3.1 says Send Message operations **MAY** be idempotent and that agents *may* use the `messageId` to detect duplicates, so a receiver that does not is not violating anything. The two paths are indistinguishable in the ledgers, which is the useful negative result for A.3: neither the istiod-driven waypoint nor the agentgateway ingress collapsed, dropped or altered the duplicate, so a second delivery counted at the worker in a later matrix row can be attributed to whatever produced it rather than to the path it took. The practical consequence is that at this version any layer that replays a POST — a gateway retry, a client retry, a transport resend — costs a second Task and a second model call at this receiver, and nothing in the receiver prevents it.
- Follow-up: none. The observed behaviour matches the SDK's own documented state and the specification's `MAY`, so there is nothing to report upstream.

Under this configuration a2a-python 1.1.2 does not deduplicate an exact transport replay either: it accepts the second delivery, dispatches it to the executor, creates a second Task, calls the model a second time, and answers with the new Task, on both stimulus paths and in 20 of 20 repetitions each — the same five counts, the same second-response shape, and the same `same_task: no` in every one of the forty rows that the Go receiver produced under the identical stimulus. The SDK's own code agrees with what it does: `DefaultRequestHandlerV2._setup_active_task` (`a2a/server/request_handlers/default_request_handler_v2.py`) builds a `RequestContext` with `task_id=None` whenever the incoming message carries no `task_id`, and `RequestContext._check_or_generate_task_id` (`a2a/server/agent_execution/context.py`) then mints one with `UUIDGenerator.generate` (`a2a/server/id_generator.py`, `str(uuid.uuid4())`), a call that takes only the task and context ids as context and never looks at `messageId`; nothing in the path from `SendMessage` to task creation reads the incoming `messageId` at all. Comparing with the Go receiver under the same mode: both SDKs did the work twice, both produced ledgers indistinguishable from each other's shape, and both stimulus paths were transparent to the duplicate at both receivers. That is the useful negative result this pair of entries gives A.3: a second delivery counted at either receiver in a later matrix row can be attributed to whatever produced it rather than to the receiver's SDK or to the path it took.
- Follow-up: none. The observed behaviour matches the SDK's own code and the specification's `MAY`, so there is nothing to report upstream.

## Gate 2 / a2a-go client / A.2 retry identity — On retry, does a2a-go reuse the messageId, the JSON-RPC id, and the body?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.9.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: `CLIENT=go LAYER=http REPS=20 experiments/gate2-a2.sh`, `CLIENT=go LAYER=http RETRY_ON=transport+503 REPS=20 experiments/gate2-a2.sh` and `CLIENT=go LAYER=sdk REPS=20 experiments/gate2-a2.sh`, three invocations on 2026-09-09, twenty repetitions each, sixty in all. **a2a-go v2.5.0 offers no retry of its own** — the entry below on where retries are configured records the source lines — so the retry under test is one the lab added, opt-in, in two places, and the row names which one it switched on. At the HTTP layer, `CLIENT_RETRIES=1` makes `fixtures/loadgen` build its client with `httpclient.NewRetryingOn`, whose `retryTransport` re-sends the request with the body rewound through `Request.GetBody` and no header added; **what it re-sends on is a second knob, and the HTTP layer was therefore run twice**. `CLIENT_RETRY_ON=transport`, the default, re-sends on a transport error and on nothing else, so any response of any status ends the request; `CLIENT_RETRY_ON=transport+503` also re-sends once on an HTTP 503, and on no other status. The second mode exists because of what this path does to the injected failure, measured below: through the worker's waypoint the failure reaches the client as a 503, so a transport-error policy is a policy that can never fire here, and 503 is the only thing an HTTP-layer retry has to act on. At the SDK layer, `CLIENT_SDK_RESEND=on` makes loadgen hand the same `*a2a.SendMessageRequest` to `client.SendMessage` a second time and print a second client line carrying `attempt: 2`. Every knob defaults to off and the mode defaults to `transport`: `TestNew_DefaultsHaveNoRetries`, `TestKnobs_DefaultOff`, `TestKnobs_UnreadableValuesLeaveTheKnobOff` and `TestParseRetryOn_DefaultsToTransport` fail if any default changes or if a value that is not a positive integer, not exactly `on`, or not exactly `transport+503` is read as widening anything; `TestNewRetrying_DoesNotRetryOnResponse` and `TestNewRetrying_DoesNotRetryOn503ByDefault` fail if the default mode ever re-sends after a response, and `TestNewRetrying_503ModeDoesNotRetryOnOtherResponses` fails if the 503 mode re-sends after a 200, 500, 404, 502 or 504. The mode is not itself a switch, which `TestKnobs_RetryOnModeIsAskedForByName` asserts: with `CLIENT_RETRIES` unset there is no retry to widen, and the run script refuses the mode on rows that have no HTTP-layer resend rather than labelling a run with a knob it cannot reach. The rendered Job (`deploy/base/loadgen-a2-job.yaml`) always writes all three variables, at `0`, `off` and `transport` for whatever the row is not testing, so no repetition can leave a knob on by omission. **The failure the client was asked to retry** is one `close-after-read` armed at the worker for that repetition's work item and nothing else: `POST http://worker.lab.svc.cluster.local:8080/control/inject` `{"mode":"close-after-read","lwi":…}` through an in-cluster curl pod, answered 204 on all sixty, twenty per run, counted from the three runs' own `control.txt` files, the middleware writing the arrival line before it consults the injector and `take` disarming the work item as it fires, so exactly one delivery per repetition was refused and every later one was served; the injector is per process and this receiver runs a single replica (`cluster-versions.txt`: `worker` replicas 1). The worker's injector was reset before each run and again after each repetition's collection, all replies 204 and recorded in `control.txt`, and the mock was reset before every repetition. **Topology**: worker Service on its own istiod-driven agentgateway waypoint (`agentgateway-waypoint`), orchestrator Service on its own (`agentgateway-waypoint-orch`) — two Services on one shared waypoint misroute, `docs/upstream/istio-waypoint-shared-by-two-services-misroutes.md`; each now has its own. A.2 is in-cluster only: each repetition is a ztunnel-captured Job that reaches the worker through the worker's waypoint, so there is no external stimulus, no agentgateway ingress and no `kubectl port-forward` anywhere in this entry. All hundred worker arrivals across the three runs — twenty in the `transport` row, which was refused once and never re-sent, and forty in each of the other two — came from `10.244.1.55`, the `agentgateway-waypoint` pod. **What that waypoint does to a `close-after-read` is the reason the rows differ, and it was measured rather than inferred** (`experiments/runs/2026-09-09-a2-go-http/waypoint-503-probe.txt`, whose second section is the unedited command lines and output of a re-capture, with the worker's own ledger lines for both work items copied from `kubectl logs`): one `close-after-read` armed and one request sent through the worker Service VIP gives the client HTTP **503** with `curl` exiting 0, while the same injection armed again and the same request sent straight to the worker pod IP, where no Service and so no waypoint is on the hop, gives the client **no HTTP status at all** — `curl` exit 52, empty reply from server. The worker's own ledger is identical in both cases (arrival line, then a response line with `status: 0` and `injection: close-after-read`), so the difference is entirely the waypoint turning an upstream connection that went away mid-request into a synthesised 503. **Counting rules**, all from the worker's pre-dispatch ingress ledger for the work item: `arrivals` are arrival-phase lines with `method == "SendMessage"`; `messageId_reused`, `id_reused` and `body_identical` compare the first two arrivals' `messageId`, JSON-RPC `id` and `body_sha256`, and are `n-a` when there was only one arrival; `injection_fired` counts the worker's lines carrying an `injection` field; `executes` are executor-entry lines (`event == "execute"`); `invocations` are the mock's lines excluding `stale-closed`; `client_result` is read from loadgen's own client lines and nothing else. `istioctl ztunnel-config certificates --node agent-mesh-lab-worker` showed `VALID CERT true` for `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default` before each run and no ztunnel restart was needed (`certificates.txt`).
