## Gate 3 / both receivers / orchestrator image on Amazon Linux 2023 — Do the counts and the trace shape survive the base change, and what does the scan count?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.9.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: the Python agent's image was rebuilt on a different foundation and nothing else moved, then the committed shape was re-counted and the five images re-scanned. **The image.** `agents/orchestrator/Dockerfile` is now three stages: a **builder** on `public.ecr.aws/amazonlinux/amazonlinux:2023` that installs `python3.14`, copies the uv binary from `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest` and resolves `/app/.venv` from the lockfile with the same uv-guide settings as before plus `UV_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3.14`; a **rootfs** stage on the same base that assembles the runtime root under `/rootfs` with `dnf --installroot`, the route `https://docs.aws.amazon.com/linux/al2023/ug/barebones-containers.html` documents ("Using the `--installroot` option to `dnf` in this manner is how we create the other AL2023 images", with its `--releasever=$(rpm -q system-release --qf '%{VERSION}')` idiom and `--setopt=install_weak_deps=False`); and a **final `FROM scratch`** holding that root, the virtual environment and the agent package. Three packages are asked for by name — `python3.14`, `system-release`, `ca-certificates`; `bash`, `coreutils` and `coreutils-common` are then removed with `rpm -e --nodeps`, **not** with `rm`, so the RPM database and the filesystem make one statement rather than two; `dnf`, `rpm` and `microdnf` are never installed into the root at all. The RPM database and `system-release` are **kept**, being how a scanner identifies the distribution and enumerates what is installed. **glibc's locale archive is kept too**, on the author's decision of 2026-09-11 taken after the cost was measured: the rootfs stage's second `rm -rf` no longer takes `/usr/lib/locale`, which in this root holds one locale — `C.utf8`, 12 files, 351817 bytes — while `/usr/share/locale`, the message catalogues, is still removed. That decision is why this entry was re-taken: the image was rebuilt, rolled out and re-counted with the archive in it, and the measurements of the same image without it are kept beside the new ones in `experiments/runs/2026-09-10-orchestrator-al2023/pre-locale/`. **The pins**, every one fetched this session and recorded in `versions.yaml` under the new key `amazonlinux-2023`, with `python-base` kept and marked `used: "no"`. The base is referenced **by tag**, on the author's standing decision, and AWS documents `:2023` as exactly the floating one — "To get the latest version of the AL2023 container image, use the `:2023` tag" (`ug/base-container.html`). Observed at this build from the `--progress=plain` log: `public.ecr.aws/amazonlinux/amazonlinux:2023@sha256:a0646b8bd35abf5ca3ab94d8cdb5691b9024e19c357531eeefd0ac4762836438`, the same index digest `docker buildx imagetools inspect` read from the registry the same day (amd64 `sha256:79c418a5…`, arm64/v8 `sha256:574a1ca2…`); `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest`, which `--pull` re-resolved at the re-take to `sha256:b485bd65…` while every builder step that uses it answered `CACHED` — hits on the layers the build of 2026-09-10T21:29:41Z made from that same digest, a build that ran the `COPY --from` step and printed `uv 0.12.13` — so the environment in this image is the one **uv 0.12.13** from `sha256:b485bd65…` built (corrected 2026-09-11; the text read 0.12.12 from sha256:73d2665b…; the evidence is `uv-correction.txt`, and `image-after.txt` was re-taken); `rpm -q --qf '%{VERSION}' system-release` printing **2023.12.20260909**, the newest release the release-notes index lists; and the interpreter **python3.14-3.14.7-1.amzn2023.0.1**, which `relnotes-2023.12.20260831.html` lists under **Core Updated Packages** as the row `python3.14-3.14.7-1.amzn2023.0.1` — the release before the observed one, the observed one's own notes naming only `containerd` and `system-release`. The in-stage `dnf … upgrade`, kept in the same `RUN` as the install on the author's upgrade-at-build rule, applied nothing: "Nothing to do." **The rollout.** The certificate check ran first and printed `VALID CERT true` for `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default`, so ztunnel was not restarted. Then `make orchestrator-image` (build, `kind load` onto both nodes) and `kubectl -n lab rollout restart deployment/orchestrator`. At the re-take the rootfs stage answered `CACHED`, the identical assembly having been built on this host when the locale cost was measured, so the package list was read back out of the RPM database the image ships rather than out of the build log — which is what keeping that database is for. **No step target ran**: no Go source changed, and `worker` and `mockllm` keep their pod names, their start times of 2026-09-10T18:12:34Z, their image ids, `restartCount` 0 and the guard annotation `lab.agent-mesh/go-sources=fdcc8676569986ce1046b91b146223b5f41313f8`, which equals this checkout's hash. **The counts.** `RUN_ITEM=2026-09-10-orchestrator-al2023/clean-check experiments/gate2-single-clean.sh`, one clean request per receiver, both control endpoints reset before and after and nothing armed; then `REPS=2 RUN_ITEM=2026-09-10-orchestrator-al2023 experiments/gate3-trace-per-work-item.sh`, four work items, nothing injected and no retry knob set. **The scan.** `make scan-images SCAN_OUT=experiments/runs/2026-09-10-orchestrator-al2023/scan` over the same five images: **Kubescape 4.0.14**, build commit `031cd40cc8de696fa30a648001853443019ec97a`, build date 2026-09-09T12:24:41Z, **vulnerability database built 2026-09-10** — the same scanner version and the same database date as the two scans it is compared with, which is what makes the three counts comparable — host-side CLI, nothing installed in the cluster. Telemetry pins unchanged and the telemetry pods unrestarted by this task, read back into `telemetry-pods.txt` after the run: all three up since 2026-09-09, `restartCount` 1 apiece from a last termination at 2026-09-10T12:53:34Z with exit 255 — the Docker Desktop restart of that morning, six hours before this rollout and already recorded in the entry for the Go module move — and this task ran no step target, applied no overlay and restarted only `deployment/orchestrator`. Pins: collector=otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.160.0, jaeger=jaegertracing/jaeger:2.20.0, prometheus=prom/prometheus:v3.14.0, otel-go=v1.46.0, otel-go-contrib=v0.71.0, and for the Python agent the OpenTelemetry distro 0.65b0 with exporter 1.44.0 and the Starlette and httpx instrumentations at 0.65b0.
- Result: **every counted figure reproduced, the image is smaller and has no shell, and the scan counts 0 in all five images where it counted 170 in this one.** Image, before → after, both arm64 and both CPython 3.14.7: exported root filesystem (`docker create` + `docker export | wc -c`) **220009472 → 186577920 bytes** — 209.8 → 177.9 MiB, the new one **84.8%** of the former; `docker image inspect .Size` **67132499 → 52750200 bytes** (64.0 → 50.3 MiB), that field being the sum of the gzipped layers rather than the same quantity; layers **9 → 5**; user 65532:65532 in both; application files root-owned at `0o755` in both. The assembled root holds **45 packages and one `gpg-pubkey` entry** and `/usr/bin` holds **25 files**; `bash`, `coreutils` and `coreutils-common` are absent by name from `rpm -qa`, and that list is **identical line for line** to the one taken before the locale archive was kept — keeping a tree that packages already claimed moved no package and no version. **The locale archive costs 364032 bytes**: the exported root filesystem is 186213888 without it and 186577920 with it, an increase of **0.20%**, and `.Size` moves 52685920 → 52750200 (+64280). What it buys, measured in both places: on the host `locale.setlocale(LC_ALL, "C.UTF-8")` returns **`'C.UTF-8'`** where it raised `unsupported locale setting` before, `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` now resolves `LC_CTYPE` to `C.UTF-8` rather than to `C`, and `locale.getlocale()` reads **`('C', 'UTF-8')`** where it read `(None, None)`; `en_US.UTF-8` raises either way, this root carrying `glibc-minimal-langpack` and no language pack. Read against the RPM database, keeping the tree takes the number of paths the database claims and the filesystem does not have from **276 to 261** of 5546, the 15 `/usr/lib/locale` paths `filesystem` and `glibc-common` claim now all being present. On the host under `docker run --rm --read-only --user 65532:65532 … python -c`: uid/gid **65532/65532**, `sys.executable` `/app/.venv/bin/python` resolving to `/usr/bin/python3.14`, glibc **2.34**, `platform.machine()` **aarch64**, `/etc/os-release` `NAME="Amazon Linux"`; `a2a` 1.1.2, `openai` 3.9.0, `starlette` 1.6.0, `opentelemetry-sdk` 1.44.0 and `orchestrator.server` all import; `import pytest` is **ModuleNotFoundError**; writes to `/x`, `/app/x`, `/tmp/x` and `/app/orchestrator/x` are all refused with **EROFS**; `/bin/sh`, `/bin/bash`, `/usr/bin/rpm`, `/usr/bin/microdnf`, `/usr/bin/dnf`, `/usr/bin/ls`, `/usr/bin/cat`, `/usr/bin/env` and `/bin/busybox` are all **absent**. Started read-only as 65532, the image answers `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` with **HTTP 200** and `protocolVersion` **"1.0"** over the JSONRPC binding, and its log holds **exactly the two pre-dispatch ingress ledger lines** that request produced, arrival and response with `status` 200. `uv run pytest -q` is **43 passed** on Python 3.14.7, `uv.lock` unchanged. In the pod, every proof a `python -c` because there is no shell to run anything else: uid/gid **65532/65532**, **aarch64**, **3.14.7**, `/app`, `/app/.venv` and `/app/orchestrator` **root-owned**, writes to `/x`, `/app/x` and `/tmp/x` all **EROFS**, `/bin/sh` and `/bin/bash` **absent**, `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io` **absent**, `/usr/lib/locale` present and holding `C.utf8` alone with `setlocale(LC_ALL, "C.UTF-8")` returning **`'C.UTF-8'`** and `/usr/share/locale` absent; the pod carries both `securityContext` blocks verbatim with `automountServiceAccountToken: false`, **no volume and no volumeMount at all**, and is Running and ready at **`restartCount` 0**. Clean check, both receivers: **1 delivery, 1 SDK entry, 1 executor entry, 1 Task created, 1 model invocation**, client `task`/`TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`. Trace re-count, **2 of 2 repetitions per receiver**, the same figures as the committed shape: worker receiver **8 spans across 2 trace ids** (`loadgen`=2, `worker`=3, `agw-egress`=2, `mockllm`=1), `lab.work_item` on **3 of 8**; orchestrator receiver **62 spans across 2 trace ids** (`loadgen`=2, `agentgateway-ingress`=2, `orchestrator`=53, `worker`=2, `agw-egress`=2, `mockllm`=1), `lab.work_item` on **5 of 62**. Ledgers per work item: worker receiver 2 ingress lines, 1 `received`, 1 `execute`, 1 Task through `SUBMITTED`→`WORKING`→`COMPLETED`, 1 invocation; orchestrator receiver 4 ingress lines, 2 `received`, 2 `execute` and 2 Tasks, one at each agent on the forward path, 1 invocation, which is the worker's. Hops that produced no span: the istiod-driven agentgateway waypoints and only those, and exactly **2 dangling parents per work item**. No ingress line carries a `truncated` field. Every one of those figures is the second reading of it: the same four counts, the same per-service split, the same attribute coverage and the same two dark hops were counted on this image before the locale archive was kept, and are kept in `pre-locale/`. Scan, from `scan/summary.csv`, as `total (critical/high/medium/low/negligible/unknown)`: **orchestrator 0**, **worker 0**, **mockllm 0**, **loadgen 0**, **replay 0** — **0 across the five images**, where the scan before the Go module move counted 175 and the scan after it counted 170, all 170 in this one image. All five `<image>-findings.csv` are **header only, 0 data rows** (42 bytes each), so each row count still equals that image's `total`. `scan/orchestrator.json` reports `distro {"name":"amazonlinux","version":"2023"}` with an empty `matches` array, and at **5715 bytes** it is small enough to keep, so **all five JSON reports are committed** where the two runs before the base change omitted the orchestrator's 757325-byte one. Run outputs: `experiments/runs/2026-09-10-orchestrator-al2023/` — the top level is this re-take (the build log, the image and package records, the host and pod proofs, the locale and ownership measurements, `clean-check/`, the four work items and `scan/`), and `pre-locale/` is the same set taken on 2026-09-10 with `/usr/lib/locale` removed, kept as the removed side of the locale comparison.
- Interpretation: as documented, and the comparison is the point. The image's foundation was replaced outright — a different distribution, a different package manager, a different libc build of the same CPython 3.14.7, an assembled root instead of a vendor base, and no shell, no package manager and no coreutils in what ships — and **not one count moved**: the same 8 and 62 spans over the same two trace ids, the same per-service split, the same 3-of-8 and 5-of-62 attribute coverage, the same two dark waypoint hops, the same two dangling parents, and 1/1/1/1/1 with a completed Task at each agent. That repeats, on a second and larger base change, what the 2026-09-10 rebuild entry found: the earlier Gate 3 figures describe the mesh and the SDKs at these pins, not the way either image happens to be assembled. The **170 → 0** is a base change and not a code change, and saying which is the whole value of it: no Python source, no lockfile entry and no dependency version moved in this commit, and the previous entry had already counted why the 170 could not be fixed from inside — 166 of them carried an empty `fixed_in`, including all 7 Criticals and all 58 Highs, so there was no version to move to. What removed them was removing the userland they lived in. `perl-base`, which carried 5 of the 7 Criticals, is not in this image because nothing in the dependency graph of `python3.14`, `system-release` and `ca-certificates` asks for it; nor are `bsdutils`, `libblkid1` or the rest of a general-purpose Debian root. What the image no longer carries is worth naming plainly: no shell of any kind, so `kubectl -n lab exec deploy/orchestrator` can only start `python` — which is why every in-pod proof above is a `python -c` — and no `dnf`, `rpm` or `microdnf`, so nothing in the container can fetch or install a package. Two things bound the 0 rather than being smoothed over. It is **0 matches against the 2026-09-10 database**, not a demonstration that 45 packages were each walked and found clean: the report's `matches` array is empty and an empty array says nothing about how many packages were enumerated. Controls were run and do not discriminate — the AL2023 base itself and `amazonlinux:2` both answer 0 as well (`scan-control.txt`) — so what can be said is that the image identifies itself, the `distro` line reading `amazonlinux 2023`, which it can only have got from the `/etc/os-release` the Dockerfile keeps on purpose, and that the same scanner and database counted 170 on the image this one replaces. And the count is a function of the database date as much as of the image; the same five images next week give other numbers. Two smaller things are recorded rather than tidied away. `rpm -e` rather than `rm` is the difference between an image that describes itself accurately and one that lies to its own scanner about owning a shell, which is why the removal is written that way and why the RPM database stays. And `make orchestrator-image` produces the same image manifest and config over a warm cache under a different manifest **list** digest each time, BuildKit regenerating the attestation manifest beside the image; `.Id` reports the index, so it moves while the image does not — three invocations of this re-take's build exported one image manifest `sha256:ad5d668c…` and one config `sha256:6cd309dc…` under indexes `3c8c1d7e…`, `548212cf…` and `e67c133f…`, of which the last is what `kind load` pushed and what the pod runs, and `image-after.txt` tabulates them rather than leaving three digests to be reconciled later. **The locale archive is the one thing this re-take changed, and it changed no count.** Keeping `/usr/lib/locale` costs 364032 bytes, 0.20% of the root filesystem, and buys `setlocale(LC_ALL, "C.UTF-8")` on both the host and in the pod where it raised before; the clean check is 1/1/1/1/1 on both receivers either side of it, the trace shape is 8 and 62 spans over two trace ids either side of it, and the scan is 0 on all five images either side of it. So this is not a fix for anything counted: nothing in the lab reads a locale — 0 of the 3107 `.py` files under `/app`, the agent's own sources and every installed dependency, mention `setlocale` — and the archive was kept so that a later locale-sensitive result is one less thing to have to rule out, at a price that was measured before it was paid. It also closes a small gap between the database and the filesystem: `glibc-common` claims those 15 paths and now has them, taking the claimed-but-absent count from 276 to 261 of 5546, which is a smaller version of the same argument the `rpm -e` paragraph makes. The remaining 261 are the man, doc, info and message-catalogue trees this image cannot display and the dnf configuration it must not carry.
- Follow-up: none
