The four waypoint spans on the worker path are two per request, inbound and outbound — `GET /*` with `GET worker.lab.svc.cluster.local:8080` for the card fetch, `POST /*` with `POST worker.lab.svc.cluster.local:8080` for the SendMessage — the same client/server pair the ingress and the egress each produce. **Nothing else moved** in any of the four configurations: `agentgateway-ingress` stays 2 spans per orchestrator work item and `agw-egress` 2 per work item, `mockllm`=1, `worker`=3, `orchestrator`=53, `loadgen`=2, trace ids 2 per work item throughout, and the ledgers per work item are the committed shape — worker receiver 2 ingress lines, 1 `execute`, 1 invocation; orchestrator receiver 4 ingress lines, 2 `execute`, 1 invocation. The `lab.work_item` numerators are unchanged at 3 and 5; only the denominators grew, by the new waypoint spans, which carry no work-item attribute. `/config_dump` after the kept configuration reads `tracing={"endpoint":"http://otel-collector.telemetry.svc.cluster.local:4317","protocol":"grpc","random_sampling":"true","client_sampling":"true","path":"/v1/traces",…}` on both proxies. It also reads `policies` of length **1** where the clean state and the attempt-(a) state both read 0, and the object there was read rather than assumed: `{"key":"frontend/tracing","name":null,"target":{"gateway":{"gatewayName":"agentgateway-waypoint","gatewayNamespace":"lab"}},"policy":{"frontend":{"tracing":{"inlineBackend":"otel-collector.telemetry.svc.cluster.local:4317","randomSampling":"true","clientSampling":"true","path":"/v1/traces","protocol":"grpc","attributes":{},"resources":{},"remove":[]}}}}`. The proxy has turned its own `config.tracing` section into an internal `frontend.tracing` policy targeting its own Gateway. Read beside the ingress proxy, which is configured the documented way by agentgateway's control plane, the two are the same structure: the ingress carries `key:"frontend/agentgateway-system/tracing:frontend-tracing:agentgateway-system/agentgateway-ingress"`, `name:{"kind":"AgentgatewayPolicy","name":"tracing","namespace":"agentgateway-system"}`, and a `policy.frontend.tracing` whose `attributes`, `resources`, `remove`, `randomSampling`, `clientSampling`, `path` and `protocol` fields are identical — differing only in provenance (`name` names the AgentgatewayPolicy, against `null` for the synthesised one) and in how the collector is addressed (`service:{"name":"telemetry/otel-collector.telemetry.svc.cluster.local","port":4317}` against `inlineBackend:"otel-collector.telemetry.svc.cluster.local:4317"`). The ingress's own `config.tracing` is `null`, the mirror image of the waypoint's. Run outputs: `experiments/runs/2026-09-12-waypoint-tracing/` — `apply.txt` (every command and output in order, including the three refusals that sent commands to the controller), `certificates.txt`, `cluster-versions.txt`, the four Istio-only work items with `summary.csv`, and `probe-a/`, `probe-b/`, `kept/`, `kept-renamed/`.
- Interpretation: as documented on the Istio side, and undocumented on the side that worked. Istio's page for agentgateway says istiod "configures agentgateway **only** through the Gateway API resources listed above" and lists `Telemetry` by name among the APIs "**not** applied to agentgateway proxies", so a Telemetry resource that istiod accepts, pushes, and never turns into proxy configuration is the documented behaviour rather than a fault, and the counts say exactly that: three objects accepted, zero spans, `"tracing": null`. The provider and the Telemetry objects are kept anyway, as the documented default configuration for a mesh whose L7 hops might not all be agentgateway. What closed the trace was the proxy's own configuration document: istiod already composes a `--config` argument for each waypoint and leaves it `{}`, and agentgateway's `config.tracing` fields are documented for exactly this. The two halves are each documented by their own project — the fields by agentgateway, the `parametersRef` Deployment overlay by Istio — and **the combination is documented by neither**; Istio's page says "agentgateway's own native configuration format and custom resources are likewise not managed by Istio". So this is recorded as a probe that was measured, not as a supported route, and it is the part of this pipeline most likely to break when either project moves. One version fact belongs with that reading and is recorded rather than acted on: agentgateway's own version-support table gives 1.5.x an Istio range of **1.23 - 1.30**, and this cluster runs **1.31.0**, one minor above it. Nothing here was changed for that, and nothing measured is attributed to it — but a result about two control planes meeting is worth less if the reader does not know that one of them is a minor outside the range the other states. The two configuration surfaces meet inside the proxy, which is the sharpest thing this task measured and was found only by reading the `policies` list rather than trusting the count of it: `config.tracing` and an `AgentgatewayPolicy` with `frontend.tracing` are compiled into the same internal object, differing in provenance and in how the collector is addressed and in nothing else. The waypoint's policy list going 0 → 1 is the proxy synthesising that object from its own configuration document. So the proxy's support for the documented policy is complete and working — the ingress proves it with a policy, the waypoint proves it with a configuration file, and both end up at the identical `frontend.tracing` structure. What is missing when a policy targets an istiod-driven waypoint is only delivery: agentgateway's controller does not program that class, istiod does not translate that CRD, and the policy's own status says `Attached: True` regardless. Two further things the measurement settles. The waypoints were never silent about trace context: the parent ids that dangled before were theirs, and turning on an exporter made those same spans appear rather than changing how the proxy handles a request — which is why the ingress, egress, agent and model counts are untouched. And the environment-variable route failed for a reason the proxy itself states: `--help`, read inside the running container, offers `-c/--config`, `-f/--file`, `--validate-only`, `-V`, `--version` and `-h`, and no environment option, which matches agentgateway's documentation naming no environment variable anywhere in its configuration or tracing pages. The trace for one work item now has no dark hop: every L7 proxy on both paths exports, and ztunnel does not, by design, being L4. Two trace ids per work item remain, and are not a defect — the card fetch and the SendMessage are two separate client requests, as earlier entries record. Separately, and not applied here, the documented alternative to an istiod-managed agentgateway waypoint was looked for at the author's request and does not exist in a current form: the agentgateway website source tree holds `integrations/istio/ambient/waypoint.md`, but it is deprecated ("The waypoint integration for Envoy-based gateway proxies is deprecated and is planned to be removed in version 2.2"), its GatewayClass is `kgateway-waypoint` with an Envoy data plane (`server: envoy` in its own example output, listener `15088`/`istio.io/PROXY` rather than `15008`/`HBONE`), it is not published on the site — which lists only `ambient-ingress` and `ambient-egress` under Istio integrations — and it says nothing about tracing.
- Follow-up: docs/upstream/agentgateway-policy-attached-to-istiod-driven-waypoint.md, updated with the 2026-09-12 measurements — the policy-attachment reproduction re-taken the same day at these versions, the internal policy object both configuration surfaces compile to, and a second suggested direction for the Istio side.

## Gate 3 / n/a / agentgateway telemetry — Which of the ingress, egress, waypoints and control plane report traces, metrics and access logs to the OpenTelemetry pipeline at v1.5.0, and what do they count for one work item?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.9.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: the three telemetry channels agentgateway documents at v1.5.0 were read from the project's own pages before anything was written, and only what they describe was applied; telemetry pins unchanged (collector=otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.160.0, jaeger=jaegertracing/jaeger:2.20.0, prometheus=prom/prometheus:v3.14.0). The `/docs/kubernetes/latest/` set is the v1.5.0 documentation: its version-support table's first row reads `1.5.x | 27 Aug 2026 | Kubernetes 1.32 - 1.37 | Gateway API 1.4 - 1.6 | Helm >= 3.12 | Istio 1.23 - 1.30`, which also records, without acting on it, that this cluster's Kubernetes 1.37.0 is inside the supported range while its Istio 1.31.0 is one minor above the top of the range agentgateway states. **Access logs** are exportable over OTLP and now are: `deploy/step-3-stress/agentgateway-access-logs.yaml` adds `spec.frontend.accessLog.otlp` to the ingress and the egress waypoint, the two proxies agentgateway's own control plane drives, using the policy shape the project's export page gives ("agentgateway formats each access log as an OTLP `LogRecord` and sends it to an OpenTelemetry Collector"), and the collector gained a `logs` pipeline whose only exporter is a second `debug` instance at `verbosity: detailed` — the page's own "Standalone debug" shape, "a minimal OTel collector that receives OTLP and writes each log record to its own pod output". No log store was added. Nothing already counted is lost, because "Log export happens in addition to the standard stdout output". **Metrics** are not exportable over OTLP at this version and were left as a scrape: the proxy's metrics are a Prometheus endpoint on 15020, and `spec.frontend.metrics` carries only label additions ("The Kubernetes API only supports adding labels. Removing default metric labels or an entire metric is not supported via AgentgatewayPolicy resource"). **The control plane** was not scraped at all before this: the existing `agentgateway-proxies` job keeps only pods carrying `gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name`, which the controller pod does not, so `deploy/step-3-stress/prometheus.yaml` gained an `agentgateway-controlplane` job on port 9092 ("The agentgateway control plane exposes Prometheus-compatible metrics on port 9092"; "No additional configuration is required to enable them"), selected by the pod's own named `metrics` port rather than a hard-coded address. The chart's `monitoring.enabled=true` route creates a ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor and is documented, but needs the Prometheus Operator CRDs, which this cluster does not have and the component list does not admit. **No control-plane tracing exists to configure**: every traces page in the v1.5.0 set is about the proxy, and none is applied. **How it was applied, and a correction to how this overlay must be applied.** The change was pushed with `kubectl apply -k deploy/step-3-stress`, which configured the two ConfigMaps and created both access-log policies as intended — **but also wrote the raw `ko://` image references into `deployment/worker` and `deployment/mockllm`**, because only the step target's `kubectl kustomize … | ko apply` resolves them, and each Deployment gained one `InvalidImageName` pod beside its running one. Undone immediately with `kubectl -n lab rollout undo deploy/worker deploy/mockllm`: both returned to their `kind.local` images, the `lab.agent-mesh/go-sources=fdcc8676…` guard annotation was intact, the bad pods went, and the serving pods never changed. The lesson is in the tree where the next person will meet it, in the step-3 comment in the `Makefile` and in the README's step-3 paragraph: a telemetry-only change to this overlay is applied by file, or by the step target that pipes through `ko`, never by a plain `apply -k`. Then `kubectl -n telemetry rollout restart deploy/otel-collector deploy/prometheus`, whose ConfigMaps had changed (new pods at 15:08:42Z), and one `REPS=1 RUN_ITEM=2026-09-12-waypoint-tracing/agentgateway-otel experiments/gate3-trace-per-work-item.sh`. The waypoints and the agents were not touched, so the span counts stay comparable with the entry above.
- Result: **traces verified unchanged, metrics and access logs as the documents describe.** Prometheus targets, before → after: **8 → 9 active, all `up`** (`targets-before.json`, `targets-after.json`); the new one is `agentgateway-controlplane`, beside `agentgateway-proxies`=4, `ztunnel`=2, `istiod`=1, `otel-collector`=1. Its scrape returns **8 control-plane series names**, more than the five the reference table lists because the histogram expands: `agentgateway_controller_build_info`, `agentgateway_controller_reconcile_duration_seconds_bucket`, `_count` and `_sum`, `agentgateway_controller_reconciliations_running`, `agentgateway_controller_reconciliations_total`, `agentgateway_xds_auth_rq_success_total`, `agentgateway_xds_auth_rq_total`. The per-hop request counter `agentgateway_requests_total` returns **7 series across all four proxies**, summing to `agentgateway-ingress`(agentgateway-system)=28, `agw-egress`(agentgateway-egress)=56, `agentgateway-waypoint`(lab)=10, `agentgateway-waypoint-orch`(lab)=6 — cumulative since each pod started, not per-run, and the waypoint figures are small because those two pods were restarted most recently; the point counted here is that every hop reports, with `gateway_name`, `namespace`, `route`, `listener`, `method` and `protocol` among its labels. **Access logs reached the collector: 3 records for the run's 2 work items**, which is exactly the two proxies' place on the two paths — `agentgateway-egress/agw-egress` **2** (the model call on both paths) and `agentgateway-system/agentgateway-ingress` **1** (the `SendMessage` on the orchestrator path only) — in `access-log-records.csv`, which carries one row per record with its gateway, method, path, status, trace id and span id, whether each id is present, and the work item, service and operation of the committed span that span id resolves to — so every claim in this sentence is read off that file rather than off a transcript. Each record carries `http.method`, `http.host`, `http.path`, `http.version`, `http.status`, `route`, `endpoint`, `src.addr`, `src.identity`, `protocol`, `duration`, and **`trace.id` and `span.id` on all 3 of 3**; the orchestrator work item's ingress and egress records share one trace id (`a0e51307…`), so an access log line joins to the trace that produced it without any work of ours. **The trace counts did not move**: `agentgateway-otel/` counted orchestrator **66 spans across 2 trace ids** (`agentgateway-ingress`=2, `agentgateway-waypoint`=2, `agentgateway-waypoint-orch`=2, `agw-egress`=2, `loadgen`=2, `mockllm`=1, `orchestrator`=53, `worker`=2), `lab.work_item` 5 of 66, and worker **12 spans across 2 trace ids** (`agentgateway-waypoint`=4, `agw-egress`=2, `loadgen`=2, `mockllm`=1, `worker`=3), `lab.work_item` 3 of 12, **0 dangling parents** and `hops_without_span: none` on both — identical to the entry above. Ledgers per work item unchanged: 2 ingress lines, 1 `execute`, 1 invocation on the worker path; 4, 2 and 1 on the orchestrator path. Run outputs: `experiments/runs/2026-09-12-waypoint-tracing/agentgateway-otel/` — `targets-before.json`, `targets-after.json`, `controlplane-metrics.json`, `requests-total.json`, `access-log-records.csv`, and the two work items with `summary.csv`.
- Interpretation: as documented, on all three channels, with one operational finding that was not about agentgateway at all. Of the three signals the proxy produces, v1.5.0 documents OTLP export for two — traces and access logs — and a Prometheus endpoint for the third, and that is exactly what this configuration now uses; no OTLP metrics exporter was invented, because none is described. The access-log records arriving with `trace.id` and `span.id` already set is the useful part: the proxies correlate their own logs to the trace without the collector being asked to, so a log line and a span for the same hop are joinable, and the count of records is itself a per-hop delivery count that does not depend on the trace pipeline. The control plane is now visible for the first time, and the reason it was not is worth keeping: the proxy job selects on the Gateway label the controllers stamp on data-plane pods, and the controller pod does not carry it, so it fell through a filter that was correct for what it was written to do. What the scrape returns is reconciliation and xDS health — the controller's view of the same pushes this lab has been reading from istiod's logs — and it documents no tracing of its own, so it contributes metrics and nothing else. The one thing that did go wrong belongs to this repository rather than to either project: `kubectl apply -k` on an overlay that carries `ko://` image references is not a telemetry-safe operation, and the brief's instruction to use it was followed and produced two `InvalidImageName` pods. It cost nothing — the serving pods never changed, the rollout undo restored both Deployments, and the guard annotation that exists to catch stale images was intact throughout — but it would have cost a measurement if it had happened mid-run, so it is recorded in the Makefile and the README rather than only here.
- Follow-up: none

## Gate 3 / both receivers / mTLS enforced — Does STRICT PeerAuthentication refuse plaintext into the mesh, do both flows still count, and what connection security does each hop report?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.9.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: two attempts on the same day, both counted. **Attempt 1** applied only the mesh-wide policy `deploy/step-2-ambient-agw/peer-authentication.yaml` — `security.istio.io/v1`, name `default`, namespace `istio-system`, `spec.mtls.mode: STRICT`, no selector and no `portLevelMtls`. Every field is cited in the file: STRICT is "Connection is an mTLS tunnel (TLS with client cert must be presented)", the placement is "For mesh level, put the policy in root-namespace according to your Istio installation", the absent selector is "Note: PeerAuthentication policies with workload selectors are ignored when deployed in the root namespace", and the root namespace was read from this cluster (`kubectl -n istio-system get cm istio -o jsonpath='{.data.mesh}'` reads `rootNamespace: istio-system`) rather than assumed. One object and not three, because the ambient Layer 4 page settles the scope question: "If the policy is in the Istio root namespace (traditionally `istio-system`), then it will target all namespaces. If it is in any other namespace, it will target only that namespace." **Attempt 2** added the two changes the author and the controller ruled after reading attempt 1, and is the shape the tree ships: the mock model **opts out of ambient** with the pod-template label `istio.io/dataplane-mode: none` in `deploy/base/mockllm.yaml`, documented on the ambient add-workloads page — ambient "mode is used for a pod if — The namespace or pod has the label `istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient` — The pod does not have the opt-out label `istio.io/dataplane-mode=none`", with the label reference giving it as Beta on "Namespace or Pod (latter has precedence)" — because the mock stands in for an external provider and the egress waypoint's call to it is this lab's external plaintext leg by design; and the agentgateway ingress pod's scrape port gets one port-level exception, `deploy/step-2b-agw-ingress-egress/peer-authentication-ingress-metrics.yaml`, a selector-scoped `PeerAuthentication` in `agentgateway-system` with `mtls.mode: STRICT` and `portLevelMtls: {15020: {mode: PERMISSIVE}}`. The `telemetry` namespace was deliberately **left out** of the mesh: enrolling it would have made the collector refuse plaintext OTLP from every emitter that is not ztunnel-captured — the mock once opted out, the egress proxy and both waypoints — and the trace would have lost those hops, the same "reject any plaintext traffic" mechanism the probe measures. The probe on each side of the policy is a `kubectl run` curl pod in `telemetry` (`curlimages/curl:8.11.1`, the non-root `securityContext` of `deploy/base/worker.yaml`), requesting each agent's Agent Card over plain HTTP with `curl --retry 0`, once per URL per phase; the exit code is recorded as well as the status, because a refused connection has no status. Then `experiments/gate2-single-clean.sh` once per receiver, and in attempt 2 also `REPS=1 experiments/gate3-trace-per-work-item.sh`. Per-hop connection security from `istio_tcp_connections_opened_total` and its `connection_security_policy` label — the metric the Istio metrics reference names and the ambient verification page prescribes reading ("Validate that the `connection_security_policy` value is set to `mutual_tls` along with the expected source and destination identity information") — through a `kubectl port-forward` to the Prometheus in `telemetry` opened and closed per reading, four readings in attempt 1 and two in attempt 2. The mock's label was applied as a targeted `kubectl patch` of the pod template and not as an `apply` of base, because `deploy/base/mockllm.yaml` carries a `ko://` image reference that only the step target's `kustomize | ko apply` resolves — the lesson recorded in the Makefile and README on 2026-09-12; the resulting pod's image was checked to be the unchanged `kind.local` reference. Certificate check before each attempt's first cluster step, `VALID CERT true` for `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default` both times, so no ztunnel restart was needed. Nothing else was restarted, no image rebuilt, no step target run, no injector armed, no retry knob touched; the probe pod was removed after each attempt.
- Result: **plaintext is refused in both attempts; the lab's own flows failed in attempt 1 at one named hop and hold in attempt 2 with every hop counted.** The probe, identical for both receivers in both attempts: **before — curl exit 0, HTTP 200**; **under — curl exit 56, no status, `Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`**. Attempt 1 added a third phase after its revert — **HTTP 200 again**, which is what attributes the refusal to the policy rather than to anything else that moved. **Attempt 1 (`attempt-1/`).** The clean check counted, for both receivers, `deliveries=1 received=1 executes=1 tasks_created=1` and then **`invocations=0`, `client_result=task/TASK_STATE_FAILED`**: the request arrived, the SDK dispatched it, a Task was created, and the model was never called. The worker's execution ledger gives the reason verbatim, `"error":"model call: status 503"`, and `invocation.jsonl` is empty for both work items. The refused hop is **`agw-egress` → `mockllm`**, named by both ends — the egress waypoint's access log reads `endpoint=mockllm.lab.svc.cluster.local:8080 src.identity=spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default http.status=503 error="upstream call failed: SendRequest: connection error: Connection reset by peer (os error 104)" reason=UpstreamFailure`, and mockllm's receiving ztunnel reads `src.workload="agw-egress-674bb755bc-9gd66" src.namespace="agentgateway-egress" direction="inbound" error="connection closed due to policy rejection: explicitly denied by: istio-system/istio_converted_static_strict"`. So the `worker` → `agw-egress` leg was fine and arrived carrying the lab identity; the leg that refused is the egress proxy's own upstream. ztunnel logged **12 refusals**, from three sources: the probe 2, that hop 2, and Prometheus → the ingress pod's `:15020` **8**, one per 15 s scrape, spanning 105 s from 15:53:03Z to 15:54:48Z, which cost a scrape target — **9/9 up before, 8/9 under the policy, 9/9 after the revert**, the lost one being `agentgateway-proxies` on `http://10.244.1.48:15020/metrics` with `read: connection reset by peer`. The policy was deleted and the clean check re-run: **`1,1,1,1,1` and `task/TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` for both receivers**. The trace run was not taken in attempt 1, because the clean check failed first. The pre-apply record predicted two refusals, and only one happened: the second, the egress proxy's XDS connection to the agentgateway control plane, **was never exercised**. Its series reads 7 in all four readings — flat across the apply, the runs and the revert — because that stream is long-lived and was already established hours earlier, and a policy that refuses new inbound connections does not tear down an open one. Recorded as not measurable in this attempt rather than as a cleared risk: the leg has the same shape as the one that did refuse, an uncaptured pod dialling a captured one in plaintext, so a reconnection while the policy was in force would have met the same refusal. **Attempt 2 (`attempt-2/`), with the mock outside ambient and the port exception in place.** The mock's new pod reads `PROTOCOL=TCP` in `istioctl ztunnel-config workloads` where it read `HBONE` before, and the agents still read `HBONE`. The clean check counted **`1,1,1,1,1` and `task/TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` for both receivers**, `invocations=1` on both. The `REPS=1` trace run counted orchestrator **66 spans across 2 trace ids** (`agentgateway-ingress`=2, `agentgateway-waypoint`=2, `agentgateway-waypoint-orch`=2, `agw-egress`=2, `loadgen`=2, `mockllm`=1, `orchestrator`=53, `worker`=2) and worker **12 spans across 2 trace ids** (`agentgateway-waypoint`=4, `agw-egress`=2, `loadgen`=2, `mockllm`=1, `worker`=3), `hops_without_span: none` on both and **0 dangling parents** on both, recomputed from each work item's `spans.csv` — column for column the figures the preceding two entries established, so enforcing mTLS cost no span and moved no count. `mockllm`=1 survives the opt-out because the mock's OTLP export goes to the collector in `telemetry`, which is not in the mesh. The egress access log shows the model call reaching the now-unenrolled mock, `http.status=200` at ~200 ms, still carrying `src.identity=spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default` on the way in. **Prometheus stayed at 9/9 across both readings, including `http://10.244.1.48:15020/metrics`** — the target attempt 1 lost — and ztunnel logged **exactly 2 refusals** under this policy, both the probe's, with none for the egress leg and none for the scrape (`attempt-2/ztunnel-refusals.txt`, whose header names the command and the window it covers). One series in attempt 2 reconciles only when named: between the two readings the worker received **two** plaintext inbound connections but the `mtls-probe` series gained one and an anonymous `source_workload="unknown"` series gained the other. It is the probe's own first request: ztunnel's access log shows that connection at 16:14:56.634799Z from the prober's pod IP `10.244.1.163` **with no `src.workload` field at all**, and the next connection 59 ms later already carrying `src.workload="mtls-probe"` — the pod had been created about a second earlier and ztunnel had not yet resolved its identity. It is one of the two probe legs, not a hop of either flow, which is why `hops.csv` does not carry it; the reconciliation is in `attempt-2/anonymous-series.txt`. **Per-hop connection security** (`hops.csv` per attempt, built by `hops.py` from the raw series in each `metrics.txt`): in both attempts every hop of both flows that ztunnel reports reads **`mutual_tls`** — `loadgen`→worker Service (source), `agentgateway-waypoint`→`worker` (destination), `worker`→`model.lab.internal` (source), `loadgen`→orchestrator Service (source), `agentgateway-waypoint-orch`→`orchestrator` (destination), `loadgen`→`agentgateway-ingress` (both sides), `agentgateway-ingress`→`orchestrator` (destination), `orchestrator`→worker Service (source). Two hops have **no series at all** in either attempt — `loadgen`→`agentgateway-waypoint` and `worker`→`agw-egress`, each the inbound side of an agentgateway proxy that is not ztunnel-captured. The `agw-egress`→`mockllm` hop read **`unknown` at `reporter="destination"`** in attempt 1 and in attempt 2 **gains no connections at all**, its series left over from the earlier reading: with the mock outside ambient there is no receiving ztunnel to report that hop. The probe legs read `unknown` by construction. Run outputs: `experiments/runs/2026-09-12-mtls-enforced/` — `attempt-1/` and `attempt-2/`, each with `apply.txt` (every command and output in order), `plaintext-probe.csv` and its per-phase logs, the clean-check ledgers and `summary.csv`, `ztunnel-refusals.txt`, `metrics.txt` and `hops.csv`; `attempt-2/trace/` additionally; and the four scripts both attempts share.
- Interpretation: as documented on both sides, and the two attempts together say what "mTLS end to end" can mean for a mesh with agentgateway proxies on the path. The probe result is the documented effect — "Enabling `STRICT` mode means that pods will only accept mTLS-encrypted traffic" — and 200 → connection reset → 200 across attempt 1's three phases attributes it to this policy alone. Attempt 1's refusal of the model leg was also documented once the shape is read out rather than assumed: `agentgateway-egress` is deliberately not ambient-enrolled, because that is agentgateway's documented ambient egress shape, and the model is a `MESH_EXTERNAL` `ServiceEntry` bound to the `agw-egress` waypoint, so the egress proxy carries an Istio identity on the way in and dials its upstream in plaintext on the way out. The pre-apply reading had already shown that leg as `unknown` at `reporter="destination"` while every other hop read `mutual_tls`; the apply turned a label into a counted refusal, which is the difference between a suspicion and a finding. What attempt 2 changes is not the policy — its text is identical — but what the mesh contains: naming the mock as outside the mesh makes the egress-to-model leg the external plaintext leg it always stood for, and then STRICT has nothing left to refuse except what should be refused. So the measured answer is: enforced and mutually authenticated on every ztunnel-captured hop; terminated by identity at each agentgateway proxy, which is why two legs have no ztunnel series rather than a plaintext one — the egress access log records the caller's SPIFFE identity on every request; and plaintext on the one leg that leaves for the model, by design and now by declaration. The `telemetry` namespace staying out is the same reasoning applied in the other direction and is worth stating because it is counter-intuitive: enrolling the observability namespace would have made the collector enforce mTLS on inbound OTLP and so refuse the spans of every emitter that is not captured — the mock, the egress proxy and both waypoints — and the trace would have lost exactly the hops the preceding two entries worked to light up. Enforcement and observability pull against each other at that boundary, and this lab resolves it by keeping the collector reachable in plaintext rather than by losing hops. Three readings are recorded against the documents rather than acted on. First, `portLevelMtls`: the field is documented and requires a selector, but the ambient Layer 4 page — the page that says peer authentication "modes, are supported by ztunnel" — never mentions a port-level mode, and no current Istio page states whether ztunnel honours one. This measurement answers it: with the exception in place the ingress scrape target stayed up across both readings and ztunnel logged no refusal on that port, where without it the target went down inside 15 s and ztunnel logged eight refusals, one per 15 s scrape, spanning 105 s. So ztunnel does honour `portLevelMtls` at this version — recorded as measured, not as documented support, and it is the part of this configuration most likely to move. Second, `connection_security_policy`: the metrics reference says it is `mutual_tls` only "when… report is from destination" and `unknown` "when report is from source", and ztunnel does not behave that way here — it reports `mutual_tls` at `reporter="source"` too, matching the sample on the ambient verification page, and `unknown` at `reporter="destination"` for the legs that really were plaintext, so in this mesh the label reads as a property of the connection rather than of the reporting side. Third, the counter counts connections and not requests — "incremented for every opened connection" — and the two legs of the model call show it differently, which is worth keeping apart. On `worker` → `agw-egress` the worker opened **one** connection and reused it throughout: the egress access log shows `src.addr=10.244.1.83:53236` (the worker pod) carrying both refusals under the policy and both successes after the revert, and `attempt-1/hops.csv` gives that hop `+1` under the policy and `+1` after it. On `agw-egress` → `mockllm`, the leg that was actually being refused, the egress proxy had to open a **new** upstream connection for each attempt, so that hop reads `+2` under the policy against `+1` after the revert, where one reused connection served both model calls. A refused connection still increments the counter — ztunnel accepts the TCP connection and then closes it on the policy — which is why the refused leg counts higher than the working one.
- Follow-up: `docs/upstream/istio-ambient-portlevelmtls-reach-undocumented.md` — no behaviour here is a defect; both projects did what their own documents describe. But rule 11 is about project gaps, and one was found with a reproduction already in hand: no current Istio page states whether ztunnel honours `portLevelMtls`, the ambient Layer 4 page not mentioning it at all while being explicit about the one mode ambient cannot use, and the only statement touching mode variety in ambient is on a retired alpha-era page that now 404s. The draft carries the two silent pages, the manifest, and the measurement both ways — eight refusals in 105 s and a lost scrape target without the exception, zero refusals and 9/9 with it — and names the sentence the ambient page needs. The pins stay in `versions.yaml` under `istio-peerauth-portlevel`. Not filed; no link until a human files it.
- Note (2026-09-12, correction): **the attempt-2 result above stood on a connection this entry read, predicted to be refused, and did not re-check after the apply.** Its after-policy counts — clean check 1/1/1/1/1, Prometheus 9/9, the only ztunnel refusals the probe's own two — were true of that cluster, but the egress proxy `agw-egress` was holding an XDS stream to the agentgateway control plane that predated the policy, and ztunnel enforces per connection, so the policy never examined it. This entry's own records bound when that stream opened: in the pod listing stamped 15:48:48Z (`attempt-1/apply.txt`) the controller reads `3 (72m ago)`, a container restart at about 14:36Z on 2026-09-12 that ends every XDS stream to it, and the policy was first applied at 15:52:50Z (again at 16:15:06Z in attempt 2) — so the stream opened on 2026-09-12 between about 14:36Z and the policy. The leg was not unread: the baseline reading at 15:52:12Z in the same file lists `agw-egress -> agentgateway.agentgateway-system.svc... destination unknown` and says STRICT "would break … the egress waypoint's XDS connection", and that the scrape of `agentgateway:9092` is "expected to be refused"; attempt 2's hops table then covered the traffic path without the control-plane legs, and the attempt-2 in-mesh result was taken as the answer. A from-scratch rebuild on 2026-09-12 exposed it with the controller captured: ztunnel refused Prometheus's scrape of 9092 under this policy and named it, and the egress proxy's own log read `Connection reset by peer` on its XDS dial to 9978 (no ztunnel line for that connection was kept), so it never became ready, the clean check counted invocations=0 with both tasks `TASK_STATE_FAILED`, and the target roster read 7/9. **The lab's shape now opts the control plane out of ambient** (`deploy/step-2b-agw-ingress-egress/agentgateway-values.yaml`, the chart's `podLabels`), as infrastructure rather than traffic path, the way this entry already treats the mock model; the ingress proxy stays captured and keeps its 15020 exception. **What was re-counted.** Rebuild #2 — from a deleted cluster, at the tree that carries the opt-out, with no manual step — re-counted the after-policy plaintext probe (refused on both receivers), the clean check (1/1/1/1/1), Prometheus (9/9), the ztunnel refusals (only the probe's two) and the per-hop security of the traffic path, and all hold; rebuild #1 had re-counted the same after applying the opt-out to its cluster in place. **Not re-counted by either rebuild**: the before-policy probe (curl exit 0, HTTP 200) and attempt 1's reverted probe; attempt 1's own counts (invocations=0, `model call: status 503`); the port-level measurement (eight refusals in 105 s and a lost scrape target without the exception, zero and 9/9 with it); and the hops table's per-phase deltas. **The 9092 scrape, measured by this entry's own counters.** The baseline predicted its refusal, yet the `agentgateway-controlplane` target stayed `up` under STRICT in both attempts, while rebuild #1 counted that target down with ztunnel refusing it. This entry's `istio_tcp_connections_opened_total` counters into the controller (`destination_service` `agentgateway.agentgateway-system.svc.cluster.local`, reporter `destination`) read `source_workload="prometheus"` **1** and `source_workload="agw-egress"` **7**, unchanged across all six readings from 15:51:30Z (attempt 1, before its apply) to 16:17:56Z (attempt 2, under STRICT): `attempt-1/metrics.txt:85-86`, `:193-194`, `:307-308`, `:427-428` and `attempt-2/metrics.txt:85-86`, `:209-210`. A count of connections opened that does not move means neither client opened a new connection to the controller across either apply: the scrape's one connection was held open, and per-connection enforcement never re-examined it — the same mechanism as the XDS stream. The metric carries no port label, so the tie to 9092 rests on the scrape configuration, whose one job that dials the controller is `agentgateway-controlplane` on that port. (The sentence in `attempt-1/metrics.txt` that "ztunnel logged no connection to :9092 at all" is about ztunnel's access log in that window; the counters in the same file record the one connection.) Istio behaved as documented throughout, so there is no upstream draft. The counts before and after are `## Gate 3 / both receivers / Helm-first installation`, whose hops tables add the three control-plane legs this one lacked: the egress proxy's XDS and Prometheus's scrape of the controller, unreported because neither end is captured, and the ingress proxy's own dial to the controller.

## Gate 3 / both receivers / no sampling — With every emitter explicit at 100 %, does every hop appear on every one of ten work items?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.9.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: the author's decision of 2026-09-12 was that nothing in this lab samples, so every span emitter on the path was audited against a document fetched that session before anything was changed, and the audit is recorded as the `otel-sampling` key in `versions.yaml` (emitter → setting → file → document). Five emitters, with the collector counted separately as the pipeline rather than as a sixth emitter: the three Go binaries share `internal/otel`, which sets `sdktrace.WithSampler(sdktrace.AlwaysSample())` in code and reads no sampler variable (the fourth fixture, `replay`, carries no OpenTelemetry code at all and emits nothing by construction); the agentgateway ingress and the egress waypoint carry `randomSampling: "true"` and `clientSampling: "true"` on their `AgentgatewayPolicy`; the two istiod-driven waypoints carry the same pair as `config.tracing` booleans; Istio's three `Telemetry` objects carry `randomSamplingPercentage: 100`, kept as the documented default although the 2026-09-12 measurement found they reach neither waypoint; and the collector's traces pipeline carries `[filter, transform, batch]` with no `probabilistic_sampler` and no `tail_sampling` anywhere under `deploy/`. **Four of the five already stated their setting; one did not.** The Python orchestrator was taking the SDK default, so the one change was `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on` in `deploy/step-3-stress/orchestrator-instrumentation.yaml`. Applying it needed care that is recorded because it was measured: that file is listed under `patches:` in the overlay's kustomization, so `kubectl apply -f` on the path itself was rejected — "spec.selector: Required value ... spec.template.spec.containers[0].image: Required value" — and the Deployment was instead rendered out of the overlay and applied as that single document, `kubectl diff` first showing the added variable and nothing else changing. A plain `apply -k` of the overlay was not used, since it carries the Go Deployments' `ko://` references. The template change rolled the pod without a `rollout restart`; in the new pod `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER='always_on'` and the SDK resolves it to `AlwaysOnSampler`. Certificate check before the step read `VALID CERT true` for `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default`. Then `REPS=5 RUN_ITEM=2026-09-12-no-sampling experiments/gate3-trace-per-work-item.sh` — five repetitions per receiver, ten work items, one clean `SendMessage` each, nothing injected and no retry knob set. Telemetry pins unchanged: `opentelemetry-collector`, `trace-backend`, `prometheus`, `otel-go`, `otel-go-contrib` and `otel-python-distro` as recorded in `versions.yaml`.
- Result: **every hop produced a span on every one of the ten work items; `hops_without_span` reads `none` on all ten rows, trace ids 2 on all ten, dangling parents 0 on all ten.** Ledgers, which are the ground truth the spans are checked against: 30 ingress deliveries, 15 executions, 10 model invocations, every task `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` — uniform per row at 2 ingress / 1 execute / 1 invocation on the five worker items and 4 ingress / 2 execute / 1 invocation on the five orchestrator items. Span shapes against the followups-6 reference: all five worker rows are exactly 12 with `agentgateway-waypoint=4|agw-egress=2|loadgen=2|mockllm=1|worker=3`; four of the five orchestrator rows are exactly 66 with `agentgateway-ingress=2|agentgateway-waypoint=2|agentgateway-waypoint-orch=2|agw-egress=2|loadgen=2|mockllm=1|orchestrator=53|worker=2`. **No row is below the shape.** One row is above it: `r1-orchestrator` counts 70, with `agentgateway-waypoint=4`, `orchestrator=54` and `worker=3`. The four extra spans were read rather than assumed and are one agent-card fetch from the orchestrator to the worker, confirmed span by span against `spans.csv`: `orchestrator GET` (the outbound client span, 16:53:33.068Z, 8.26 ms), `agentgateway-waypoint GET /*` and `GET worker.lab.svc.cluster.local:8080` (the waypoint pair, both 16:53:33.075Z), and `worker GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` (the server span, 16:53:33.076Z, 0.05 ms) — the three inner spans nesting inside the client span's 8.26 ms in that order, which is one request crossing the worker's waypoint and nothing else. It is **the first forward the newly rolled orchestrator pod made** — the pod started 16:51:36Z on commit 1's rollout and this is the first orchestrator work item of the run (r1-worker ran before it; the run itself started 16:52:44Z) — and the four other orchestrator work items carry **zero** of it: worker card fetch 0, waypoint `GET` spans 0, orchestrator client `GET` 0 on each of r2–r5. That is the a2a-python client resolving the downstream card once per process and reusing it, so the count is four additional spans on one row rather than a shortfall on any. The card fetch that *is* in the shape — loadgen fetching the orchestrator's own card through `agentgateway-waypoint-orch` — is present once on all five orchestrator rows, r1 included. Run output: `experiments/runs/2026-09-12-no-sampling/` (`summary.csv` and, per work item, the three ledgers, `client.jsonl`, `spans.csv` and `trace.json`).
- Interpretation: as documented, and the counted answer to the question is yes. Worth stating plainly what the one change did and did not do: the default it replaced, `parentbased_always_on`, would have sampled every span this lab produces as well, since a root is always sampled and every inbound parent here arrives sampled — so the measurement did not move because the behaviour did not change, and the honest description is that the change is to the record rather than to the traffic. What it buys is that no emitter's sampling is now inherited; all five are stated in a file, which is what a lab that counts hops needs, and the audit table is the artefact. It is also worth being exact about what "all traces" means here, because the phrase is broader than the pipeline: it means every L7 hop of every request, on both paths, which is what the ten rows show. It does not mean every packet. ztunnel contributes no spans at all — it is the L4 layer by design, and the L7 hop is the waypoint — so an ambient mesh at 100 % sampling still has an L4 segment that traces cannot describe, and the connection-security counts from ztunnel's own metrics remain the instrument for that leg. Two other components on the path emit no traces either, and are named here so the enumeration is exhaustive rather than apparently exhaustive: the agentgateway control plane in `agentgateway-system`, which documents no tracing of its own and contributes metrics and nothing else (followups-6's entry recorded that when Prometheus was pointed at its port 9092) — it drives the ingress and the egress waypoint, and those two do emit and are in the table — and the `replay` fixture, which carries no OpenTelemetry code at all. The collector's `filter` also still drops health-probe spans, which is kept: it is a named exclusion of traffic that is not a work item, not a fraction of work-item traffic, and removing it would add noise without adding a hop. The `r1` excess is the one result that would have been easy to record wrongly, and it is worth naming for what it is: first-request agent-card resolution after a restart. The orchestrator pod was rolled by this task's own change, and the a2a-python client inside it resolves the downstream worker's card on its first forward and then reuses it, so the first work item that pod served crossed the worker's waypoint once more than the four after it. Read to its operations and timestamps that is a real request the other nine work items genuinely did not make — not a sampling result in either direction, since a count *above* a reference shape cannot be a sampled-away span, and `hops_without_span` still reads `none` on that row. This is what "all traces" has to look like when a process makes an extra request: the shape is a reference for what a work item normally crosses, not a quota, and an instrument at 100 % is supposed to show the extra hop rather than smooth it away. The reading to avoid is treating the reference shape as the expected answer and the excess as noise; the ten rows are kept as counted.
- Follow-up: none

## Gate 3 / both receivers / Helm-first installation — Does the lab rebuild from a deleted cluster on the Helm route with the same counts, trace shape, mTLS and scan results, and what did rebuilding find that the running cluster had hidden?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.9.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: the author's direction of 2026-09-12 — install every component through Helm where a chart exists, fall back to the previous route when `helm` is absent, and move the configuration this lab passed through the IstioOperator file into the Helm deployment — then prove it from a deleted cluster. Chart versions, each fetched this session and each chosen because its appVersion is the component version this lab already counted against: istio `base`/`istiod`/`cni`/`ztunnel` 1.31.0 from `https://blob.istio.io/istio-release/charts`, `opentelemetry-collector` 0.173.1 (appVersion 0.160.0), `jaeger` 4.13.1 (2.20.0), `prometheus` 29.28.1 (v3.14.0), and the two agentgateway OCI charts already at v1.5.0; telemetry pins unchanged (collector=otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.160.0, jaeger=jaegertracing/jaeger:2.20.0, prometheus=prom/prometheus:v3.14.0, otel-go=v1.46.0, otel-go-contrib=v0.71.0, and for the Python agent the OpenTelemetry distro from the unchanged `uv.lock`). `helm` on the host is v4.3.0, and the Makefile pins nothing: the guard is `HELM := $(shell command -v helm 2>/dev/null)`, so a target takes the Helm route when any helm answers and the previous route when none does; `make -n step-2 step-2b step-3` was rendered twice, once with helm on PATH and once with its directory removed, and both are committed. **Two components have one route only, and both targets say so**: Gateway API publishes no chart for its CRDs (its install page gives only `kubectl apply --server-side -f …experimental-install.yaml`), so step-2 applies them identically either way; and agentgateway documents only its two OCI charts for the control plane, so `make step-2b` stops with that sentence — which means **a rebuild with helm off PATH cannot pass step 2b at all**, and the fallback route is recorded as not reproducible end to end rather than merely not exercised on this date. **Istio's own words, not a paraphrase**, because the direction's phrasing was broader than the project's: Istio deprecated its *in-cluster* operator in 1.23 and removed it in 1.24, and says "This deprecation only affects users of the In-Cluster Operator. Users who install Istio with the istioctl install command and an IstioOperator YAML file are not affected", while recommending "most users migrate to Helm". This lab never ran the in-cluster operator, so the move is taken on that recommendation and the IstioOperator file is kept as the fallback. Its Helm translation was not done by hand: `istioctl manifest translate -f deploy/step-2-ambient-agw/istio-meshconfig.yaml`, the command Istio documents for exactly this, produced the `meshConfig` block key for key, and the two files' blocks are byte-equal after the two-space indentation offset (same sha256, both recorded). **Two rebuilds from a deleted cluster, and they are not the same kind of evidence.** **Rebuild #1** ran at the commit "build(deploy): drop the three telemetry manifests from their old paths" — deploy subtree `2d62ff242f0c…`, Makefile `e8097d3f1e54…`, the rest in `tree-identity.txt`, whose map resolves the pre-rewrite SHA 5dcb7c9 that `build.txt` records — with one uncommitted change (the Prometheus values fix below): `make teardown`, then `cluster-kind`, `step-1`, `step-2`, `step-2b`, `step-2c`, `step-3`, each timed (`build.txt`). Two changes were then applied to that rebuilt cluster in place, each by the same `helm upgrade -i` its step recipe uses rather than by another teardown — the seven-day workload certificates added by the author's addition of the same date, and the control-plane ambient opt-out — and two manual steps were taken that no make target runs: `kubectl -n telemetry rollout restart deploy/prometheus` after the second failed step-3, and the deletion of the backing-off `agw-egress` pod so it would dial its controller afresh. Rebuild #1's counts after the remedy therefore describe a cluster that was rebuilt and then patched. **Rebuild #2** ran from a deleted cluster at the tree that deploys all of it — with an empty `git status --short` held through the whole build, at a fix-round commit since folded away by autosquash, so the commit and tree SHAs in `rebuild-2/build.txt`'s header are pre-rewrite. What it built is identified by content instead: deploy subtree `1d0025adfe2e…`, Makefile `d5ccb2437ca6…`, agents `878ce64e4449…`, fixtures `e6e6682ac210…`, experiments/lib `0cc3db9375f0…` and every `experiments/*.sh` blob, all carried unchanged by the last commit on this branch, "docs(runs): re-render the two make -n routes so the record matches the tree" (full IDs, the check commands and the old-to-new SHA map in `tree-identity.txt`; the same IDs are appended to `rebuild-2/build.txt`) — with the same seven targets and **no manual step**: no pod deleted, no rollout restarted, no helm upgrade outside a make target. After each rebuild: the certificate check, the clean check, `REPS=2` trace per work item, the plaintext probe, the per-hop connection-security reading, `make scan-images`, the Prometheus target roster and the pod hardening reads; on rebuild #2 also the Istio images, ztunnel's policy rejections before and after the checks, the egress waypoint's first XDS stream, and an absence check for the charts' optional components.
- Result: **rebuild #2 reproduces every committed count from a deleted cluster, at the tree that deploys it, with no manual step; rebuild #1 is where the latent fault that made that necessary was found.** **Rebuild #1** (`build.txt`): teardown 3 s, cluster-kind 19 s, step-1 62 s, step-2 93 s, step-2b 66 s, step-2c 22 s, step-3 24 s on the run that reported exit 0 — about 5 min on the green path and about 14 min including two failed step-3 attempts. **step-3 failed twice before it passed, both times on Prometheus and both times for reasons now written into the tree.** The first (342 s) was a defect in the values file as first written: `global` was given both in `server.global` and under `serverFiles."prometheus.yml"`, and the chart's ConfigMap template emits `global:` from the former and then appends whatever keys remain in the latter, so the pod got two `global` keys and refused the file — `line 77: field global already set in type config.plain`. The corollary is the chart fact: `server.global` is the only place that block may be given, and a `global` under `serverFiles` is additively wrong rather than ignored. The second (202 s) failed because **this chart puts no config-checksum annotation on its server Deployment**, unlike the collector chart whose Deployment carries `checksum/config`, so a ConfigMap-only change does not roll the server; with the chart's `configmap-reload` sidecar disabled under scope rule 6 a scrape-configuration change needs an explicit restart, which is the handling the manifest route already needed, so the two routes behave alike. One manual `kubectl -n telemetry rollout restart deploy/prometheus`, and step-3 then reported exit 0. **The latent fault, found on rebuild #1 with the controller captured.** `make step-2b` labels the whole `agentgateway-system` namespace ambient for the ingress *proxy*'s sake and had captured the controller pod with it, and its two plaintext clients failed differently: ztunnel refused Prometheus's scrape of the controller's 9092 and named the policy itself (`explicitly denied by: istio-system/istio_converted_static_strict`), and the egress waypoint's own log read `XDS client connection error: … Connection reset by peer (os error 104)` on its dial to the controller's XDS on 9978 — no ztunnel line for that connection was kept, so the policy is not quoted as its cause (`strict-refuses-egress-xds.txt`). The egress waypoint failed its startup probe 301 times over 13 minutes and never became ready: the clean check counted `deliveries=1 received=1 executes=1 tasks_created=1` but **`invocations=0` with both tasks `TASK_STATE_FAILED`**, against the committed `1/1/1/1/1` and `COMPLETED`, and Prometheus read **9 targets discovered, 7 up** against the committed 9/9. It had been invisible because on the cluster that stood before the teardown the egress waypoint's XDS stream predated the STRICT policy and ztunnel enforces per connection; followups-7's own records bound its opening to 2026-09-12, between the controller's last container restart at about 14:36Z and the policy's first apply at 15:52:50Z. The remedy is the per-pod opt-out `istio.io/dataplane-mode: none` on the controller, through the chart's `podLabels`, this lab's posture for a component off the traffic path that must be reachable in plaintext (the treatment the mock model already has) rather than holing the mesh-wide policy for two ports. On rebuild #1 it was applied in place and the backing-off egress pod was deleted by hand, after which `istioctl ztunnel-config workloads` read the controller as TCP and the ingress proxy as HBONE, the new egress pod logged `Stream established`, and the only policy rejections were the probe's two (`controlplane-optout.txt`); the counts then returned on that patched cluster — clean check 1/1/1/1/1 `COMPLETED`, trace 12/66 spans with 0 dangling parents, Prometheus 9/9, the probe refused, the scan 0 on all five images. **Rebuild #2** (`rebuild-2/`), from a deleted cluster at the final tree: teardown 2 s, cluster-kind 19 s, step-1 56 s, step-2 99 s, step-2b 65 s, step-2c 20 s, step-3 86 s — **347 s, every target exit 0 on its first run, no manual step**. The Istio images are `ztunnel:1.31.0-distroless`, `install-cni:1.31.0-distroless` and `pilot:1.31.0-distroless`, with `ISTIO_META_ENABLE_HBONE=true` in ztunnel's env (`rebuild-2/certificates.txt`). **The egress waypoint went Ready on its first XDS stream**, the from-scratch proof of the opt-out that rebuild #1 could not give: one `Stream established` in its first second, 0 XDS connection errors, 0 readiness failures, 0 restarts, one ReplicaSet and no failed-probe event, with the controller reading `istio.io/dataplane-mode=none` and TCP and the ingress proxy HBONE (`rebuild-2/egress-first-stream.txt`). ztunnel's policy rejections read 0 on both nodes before any check and **exactly 2 after** the clean check, the trace and the probe — one per receiver, both from `telemetry/mtls-probe` (`rebuild-2/ztunnel-rejections-baseline.txt`, `rebuild-2/ztunnel-rejections-after.txt`). Clean check: **`1/1/1/1/1` with `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`** on both receivers. Trace, four rows at `REPS=2`: both worker rows exactly **12** spans with `agentgateway-waypoint=4|agw-egress=2|loadgen=2|mockllm=1|worker=3`, both orchestrator rows exactly **66** with `agentgateway-ingress=2|agentgateway-waypoint=2|agentgateway-waypoint-orch=2|agw-egress=2|loadgen=2|mockllm=1|orchestrator=53|worker=2`, `trace_ids` 2 and `hops_without_span` `none` on all four, and **0 dangling parents** with 2 roots on all four (`rebuild-2/trace/`). Prometheus: **9/9 up** — `agentgateway-proxies`=4, `ztunnel`=2, `istiod`=1, `agentgateway-controlplane`=1, `otel-collector`=1. Plaintext probe from the unenrolled `telemetry` namespace: **curl exit 56, no status, `Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`** on both receivers. Per-hop connection security (`rebuild-2/hops-security.csv`, now with `destination_workload` and every row explained by letter): `mutual_tls` on every hop between mesh workloads; `unknown` only on the ingress proxy's own XDS dial to its controller (plaintext since the opt-out — its measured cost, and not a hop any work item crosses), Prometheus's scrapes of the ingress proxy accepted by its 15020 exception, control-endpoint resets to the opted-out mock, span and access-log export to the unenrolled collector with the ingress proxy's own export included, and the refused probe; and `not-reported`, because neither end is captured, on the egress waypoint's XDS and Prometheus's scrape of the controller, the model leg's second half, and the other uncaptured emitters' telemetry. With the ingress proxy's dial those are **three control-plane legs** that followups-7's table lacked; rebuild #1's table is regenerated from its own raw reading to the same shape. `make scan-images`: **0 in every severity for all five images**. An absence check over pods, services, Deployments, DaemonSets and StatefulSets in every namespace finds no alertmanager, node-exporter, pushgateway or kube-state-metrics object and no OAuth2, Spark or Elasticsearch job, and every telemetry pod runs one container (`rebuild-2/cluster-after.txt`). **The ztunnel image, which the Helm route had changed.** Rebuild #1's Helm route ran `docker.io/istio/ztunnel:1.31.0`, not the `1.31.0-distroless` that the istioctl route and every earlier Gate 3 count ran, and its ztunnel lacked `ISTIO_META_ENABLE_HBONE`: the ambient Helm page passes no profile to ztunnel, and a comparison of object names could show neither. `profile: ambient` in `ztunnel-values.yaml` restores both — rendered with and without it, the ztunnel output differs in exactly those two places — and against `istioctl manifest generate` every workload image, the four settings the lab sets and the ztunnel env names are now identical (`istio-two-routes-images.txt`). Rebuild #1's counts were taken on the non-distroless ztunnel; rebuild #2's on the distroless one. **The seven-day certificates take two settings, not one, and the one the addition named is not the operative one.** istiod's `DEFAULT_WORKLOAD_CERT_TTL` is "Applied when the client sets a non-positive TTL in the CSR", and ztunnel *does* set a positive TTL: its source at release-1.31 has `const DEFAULT_TTL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60 * 60 * 24)` behind the `SECRET_TTL` variable and builds its CSR with `validity_duration: self.secret_ttl`, which is why the leaves read 24 h on rebuild #1's first certificate check. Both were set, on both routes, and both renderings were checked to reach containers rather than only the values ConfigMap (`fallback-route-ttl-render.txt`, and section 3 of `istio-two-routes-images.txt`); `MAX_WORKLOAD_CERT_TTL` permits seven days at its 2160h default and was left alone. Istio publishes no ztunnel command reference at all (`/docs/reference/commands/` lists only install-cni, istioctl, pilot-agent, pilot-discovery), so that side is read from ztunnel's source as this lab already does for its metrics ports. Applied on rebuild #1 through `helm upgrade -i istiod` and `ztunnel`, the env change rolled the DaemonSet on its own. **The proof, stated exactly rather than rounded**: on rebuild #1 both leaves read `NOT BEFORE 2026-09-12T18:24:28Z`, `NOT AFTER 2026-09-19T18:26:28Z`, which is **168h02m** by subtraction, not 168h. Read forward from issuance it is exact: the new ztunnel pods came up at 18:26:27Z and 18:26:28Z, and 18:26:28Z + 168h is 2026-09-19T18:26:28Z to the second, with `NOT BEFORE` backdated two minutes. That the two minutes are a constant is evidenced by the pre-change reading in the same run directory — the 24 h leaf read 24h02m by the same subtraction and 24h exactly forward from its own issuance — so the offset is unchanged by this task and no mechanism is claimed for it. On rebuild #2, set from the start: `lab/sa/default` `NOT BEFORE 2026-09-12T19:27:08Z`, `NOT AFTER 2026-09-19T19:29:08Z`, and `agentgateway-system/sa/agentgateway-ingress` `NOT BEFORE 2026-09-12T19:28:18Z`, `NOT AFTER 2026-09-19T19:30:18Z` — the same 168h02m, 168h forward from issuance. Coverage: those two are the only identities issued, both on the worker node; the control-plane node's ztunnel holds no leaf (a header-only reading; no captured workload is scheduled there), and `telemetry`, `agentgateway-egress` and the opted-out controller have no identity because none of their pods is captured (`rebuild-2/certificates.txt`). **Pod hardening** on the chart-installed pods: read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation and all capabilities dropped on all three, at the container level; non-root on all three but not at one level — `runAsNonRoot` and `runAsUser` at the pod level on the collector (set by its values file) and on Prometheus (the chart's default), while on Jaeger `runAsNonRoot` is set at the container level by `jaeger-values.yaml` and `runAsUser` 10001 is the chart's pod-level default (`rebuild-2/pod-hardening.txt`); no ServiceAccount token on the collector and the trace backend. What the charts would not give: Prometheus keeps its token, which its `role: pod` and `role: endpoints` discovery needs, and its ClusterRole is wider than the manifest's — adding `nodes/metrics`, `ingresses` and `configmaps` and the `networking.k8s.io` ingress resources — with no narrower one on offer. Every optional sub-component is disabled by name even where the chart already defaults it off: the Prometheus chart's four subcharts and its `configmap-reload` sidecar, the collector chart's nine presets, cluster role, PodMonitor and ServiceMonitor, and the Jaeger chart's OAuth2 sidecar, Ingress, HTTPRoute, NetworkPolicy (`networkPolicy.enabled: false`), Spark job and three Elasticsearch maintenance jobs. Rendered against the manifests they replace: the collector's receivers, processors, exporters, extensions, all three pipelines and `service.telemetry` are identical with one key renamed — the chart rewrites exporter `otlp` to `otlp_grpc`, which at collector 0.160.0 is that component's current name and the manifest's is the alias its factory registers — and Prometheus renders the same five scrape jobs in the same order and the same six object kinds. The Jaeger chart runs Jaeger v2 all-in-one with in-memory storage as its own default, so it is used rather than kept as a manifest; its Service publishes fourteen ports where the manifest publishes three, which changes no listener and is recorded. Run outputs, under `experiments/runs/2026-09-12-helm-first/`: rebuild #1 — `build.txt`, `certificates.txt`, `certificates-168h.txt`, `clean-check/`, `clean-check-after/`, `trace/`, `mtls/`, `hops-security.csv`, `tcp-connection-security-raw.txt`, `prometheus-targets.txt`, `pod-hardening.txt`, `cluster-after.txt`, `prometheus-first-attempt-failure.txt`, `strict-refuses-egress-xds.txt`, `controlplane-optout.txt`, `scan/`; rebuild #2 — `rebuild-2/build.txt`, `rebuild-2/certificates.txt`, `rebuild-2/egress-first-stream.txt`, `rebuild-2/ztunnel-rejections-baseline.txt`, `rebuild-2/ztunnel-rejections-after.txt`, `rebuild-2/clean-check/`, `rebuild-2/trace/`, `rebuild-2/mtls/`, `rebuild-2/hops-security.csv`, `rebuild-2/tcp-connection-security-raw.txt`, `rebuild-2/tcp-connection-security-raw-1938.txt`, `rebuild-2/prometheus-targets.txt`, `rebuild-2/pod-hardening.txt`, `rebuild-2/cluster-after.txt`, `rebuild-2/scan/`; tree identity — `tree-identity.txt`; route and chart comparisons — `istio-two-routes-images.txt`, `istio-two-routes-objects.txt`, `fallback-route-ttl-render.txt`, `chart-vs-manifest.txt`, `meshconfig-block-equality.txt`, `readonly-rootfs-check.txt`, `make-n-helm.txt`, `make-n-nohelm.txt`, `istioctl-manifest-translate/`.
- Interpretation: on what was compared and counted, the Helm route reproduces this lab, and the second rebuild is what entitles the entry to say so. On the installation question the answer is as documented on every side, limited to what the records compare: Istio's four ambient charts with the mesh configuration as Helm values render the same object names as `istioctl install -f` bar one `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` that the Helm route renders and istioctl creates at run time, the same four settings the lab sets, and — once the ztunnel chart took the ambient profile too — the same image for every workload and the same ztunnel environment; and the three telemetry charts produce the same pipelines, the same five scrape jobs, the same images and the same Service names as the manifests they replace, the collector's one textual difference being a rename inside a single component. That the image comparison had to be added is itself worth keeping: a comparison of object names passed while the Helm route ran a different ztunnel build from the one every earlier count was taken on. What the rebuilds added is the more valuable finding, and it is a methodological one: a policy applied to a running cluster is only tested against connections opened after it, and ztunnel enforces per connection, so mesh-wide STRICT had been sitting over an egress-waypoint XDS stream whose dial rebuild #1 then saw reset, and nobody could see it. The counts from followups-7 and followups-8 are not wrong — they were taken on a cluster whose traffic did flow — but they were not evidence that the configuration in the tree could bring that cluster up from nothing. Rebuild #1 is not that evidence either, because its remedy was applied in place and one pod was deleted by hand; **rebuild #2 is** — from a deleted cluster, at the tree that deploys the remedy, with no manual step, the egress waypoint Ready on its first stream and every committed figure re-counted — and the statement rests on rebuild #2 alone. That argues for the from-scratch rebuild, with no manual step, being the acceptance test for any change to who is captured. Two smaller things are worth keeping. The two failed step-3 runs are both chart behaviour a reader would otherwise rediscover: only `server.global` carries Prometheus's global block, and that chart does not roll its server when its ConfigMap changes. And the seven-day certificates are a case where doing what was asked would have produced a figure that looked right for the wrong reason: setting only istiod's default would have left ztunnel's leaves at 24 h, because ztunnel asks for a lifetime and istiod's default applies only when the client asks for none. The 168h02m span is reported as measured rather than rounded to the figure the brief predicted, with the two minutes attributed to a backdated `NOT BEFORE` that the pre-change reading shows to be constant.
- Follow-up: none

  - clean check: deliveries, received, executes, tasks, invocations, client result;
  - A.1: deliveries, executes, distinct messageIds, tasks, invocations, first response, second response, same task;
  - A.2: arrivals, messageId reused, JSON-RPC id reused, body identical, injection fired, executes, invocations, client result;
  - A.3: deliveries, dispatched, distinct messageIds, tasks, invocations, client result, second-delivery layer;
  - trace rows: trace ids, spans, spans by service, hops without span, `lab.work_item` on all;
  - three ledgers: JSON-RPC deliveries, arrivals for the work item, dispatches, distinct messageIds, tasks, final state, invocations, `A2A-Version` seen, client result kind;
  - mockllm deterministic: identical response hashes of 20, the count-keyed injection's firing position, work-item-keyed hits on det-003 and on det-004;
  - gateway retry mechanics: arrivals at the worker, invocations at the mock, retried, identity source, messageId same, JSON-RPC id same, taskId same, caller same, body sha256 same, body length same, executes, client result.
