  **The differences, named:**
  - **A.3 trace columns, 14 rows, 28 cells: differs.** Every committed matrix row was counted on 2026-09-09/10. That was before followups-6 gave the two istiod-driven waypoints their tracing configuration, the change the trace instrument recorded as 8→12 spans on the worker flow and 62→66 on the orchestrator flow. From every `spans.csv` on both sides, each row's span multiset is identical in 20/20 repetitions on each side, and **the current multiset is the committed one plus waypoint spans only, with no span lost from any service**.
    - Go rows gain the worker waypoint's card fetch (`GET /*`, `GET worker.lab.svc.cluster.local:8080`) plus one `POST /*`/`POST worker…:8080` pair per delivery through that waypoint:
      - +4 on baseline, R3 and egress (one delivery);
      - +6 on R1 http and sdk (two client deliveries, each a separate waypoint request);
      - +5 on R2 waypoint and R4 (one `POST /*` route span over **two** `POST worker…:8080` upstream spans, which is the waypoint's own HTTPRoute retry now visible inside the waypoint).
    - Python rows gain only the orchestrator waypoint's card fetch (`GET /*`, `GET orchestrator.lab.svc.cluster.local:8080`), +2. The matrix unsets `DOWNSTREAM_A2A_URL`, so there is no forward to the worker and so none of the instrument's other two waypoint spans. The POST enters by the ingress, which dials the pod.
    - **R2 go ingress and R2 py ingress are the same** (9 and 54 spans, identical multisets): the stimulus comes from this host through the ingress, and no waypoint is on either path.
  - **A.3 notes, 2 cells (R2 go waypoint, R4 go): differs.** This is the one place where the evidence behind a label changed while the label held. `second_delivery_layer` is `gateway` in 20/20 repetitions on both sides of both rows. What changed is the branch of `experiments/lib/derive-layer.sh` that derives it:
    - **Committed rows: the shared-parent rule** (`:329-331`). "The two worker server spans share one parent span id … so one proxy span sent the request twice". Its header comment (`:32-35`) says it was measured on the istiod-driven waypoint, "where both `POST /` server spans named one dangling parent".
    - **Current rows: the converging-grandparent rule** (`:333-336`). "The two worker server spans have distinct parents … both agentgateway-waypoint spans under one agentgateway-waypoint span … so one proxy made both attempts". Its header comment (`:36-39`) says it was measured on the agentgateway ingress.
    - **Why.** followups-6's waypoint spans now exist: the waypoint that was dark when these rows were counted exports one route span with one upstream span per attempt, the ingress's shape. The parent the committed rows shared was one of those unexported spans. Counted from every `spans.csv`, dangling parents over each of these two rows' 20 repetitions were 60 committed and are 0 now. Across the 16 matrix rows they were 20–60 on the 14 rows whose path crosses an istiod-driven waypoint and 0 on the two R2 ingress rows, and are 0 on all 16 now.
    - **Consequence.** The shared-parent branch the committed entries quote is not reached by any matrix row at the lab's current tracing configuration. Those entries are the A.3 R2 entry (`findings.md:381`), the A.3 R4 entry (`:476`, `:624`) and the trace-attribution entry (`:614`, `:636`). They stand for the configuration they counted; this is a record, and no code changed.
  - **A.2 notes, 2 cells (go http, py http resend): differs.** The records show:
    - The committed rows' knob label does not print `CLIENT_RETRY_ON`. `experiments/gate2-a2.sh` prints it (`KNOB_NAMES=(CLIENT_RETRIES CLIENT_RETRY_ON)` at line 127, `KNOB_NAMES=(CLIENT_TRANSPORT_RESEND CLIENT_RETRY_ON)` at line 145, rendered at line 159) both at HEAD and at 09979c2 and f4ed395, the commits that committed those two run directories. So the committed rows were counted by an uncommitted state of the label; no record dates it.
    - The two runs set the same retry behaviour. An unset `CLIENT_RETRY_ON` parses to `transport` in both clients: in Go at `fixtures/loadgen/main.go:109` through `internal/httpclient/httpclient.go:82-87`, tested with the variable empty at `fixtures/loadgen/main_test.go:20-30`; in Python at `agents/orchestrator/orchestrator/forward.py:83`.
    - Every count in both rows is the same.
  - **Gate 3 gateway retry mechanics trace, 2 cells: differs; route and identity counts same.** All three routes fired their retry in 5/5 with byte-identical second deliveries, as committed: arrivals, invocations, identity fields, executes and client result are the same on every route. Each proxy's `/config_dump` holds the policy, with 1, 2 and 1 retry policies on the waypoint, ingress and egress, as committed. The trace columns differ for the same reason as the matrix's, with no span lost:
    - the waypoint route gains the worker waypoint's card fetch and one `POST /*` route span over two `POST worker…:8080` upstream spans, 9→14;
    - the egress route gains the worker waypoint's card fetch and one POST pair, 10→14;
    - the ingress route, which no waypoint serves, is the same at 9.
  - **Gate 1 mockllm deterministic, 2 timing cells: differs; counts same.** `latency_min_ms` and `latency_max_ms` measure the mock's fixed 200 ms latency: 200.264–209.447 ms committed, 200.165–204.721 ms now. They are wall-clock measurements, not counts. Every count is the same: 20 of 20 identical response hashes, the count-keyed injection firing at request 5, and 2 and 0 work-item-keyed hits. The shared response sha256 is `80e9166feb70b5a665e55074c36924644d9c18861be1495412e0b2fb06427591`, the value the 2026-09-05 entry records, so the mock's output is byte-identical across the two dates.
  - **Gate 1 three ledgers: same.** One clean request, 1/1/1/1/1 with `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`, one invocation and `A2A-Version` 1.0. The path now crosses the worker's waypoint; at 2026-09-05 it did not.
- Interpretation: at the latest releases read on 2026-09-12, and from a deleted cluster, this lab reproduces what it has counted since Gate 1. That covers:
  - the retry-free baselines at the three steps they were counted on;
  - A.1's deduplication results for both SDKs over both paths, and A.2's retry identity for both clients;
  - every A.3 matrix row and the egress row on both receivers, and the gateway retry mechanics on all three routes;
  - the three-ledgers and mock-determinism checks;
  - the clean check, the wire version, the followups-6 trace shape with no dangling parent, mTLS refusing plaintext, 9/9 scrape targets and a clean scan. Much of that is as expected, since few pins moved.

  The two moves that bear on a counted behaviour are both confirmed rather than assumed:
  - openai-python moved four minor versions. The orchestrator's `max_retries=0` still gives one invocation and the library default of 2 still gives three, in the baseline's runs 5 and 6, and R3 py's model-client retry still counts exactly two invocations.
  - The curl image moved. The probe's refusal reads the same. All ten scripts that start a curl pod ran on 8.22.0, the last three in fix round 1, and each exited 0 on its first run.

  The Gate 1 step-2 and step-2b baselines were first counted before mesh-wide STRICT existed, and now run under it from the moment step 2 applies. Their counts under STRICT are the same as before it, for these run types. At step 2 one leg those runs cross is the worker's plaintext call to the opted-out mock, which STRICT does not govern. The A.1, R2 and retry-mechanics ingress paths, reached by `kubectl port-forward` to a captured proxy, also count the same under STRICT, which no committed run had exercised.

  The only differences are in columns the ledgers do not produce, and each has a cause the records show. The trace columns are the most useful to keep. Re-read against spans, they show the waypoint's HTTPRoute retry as one route span over two upstream spans, which the committed rows could not show because the waypoint was dark then. They also show the matrix's Python rows gaining only the card-fetch hop, because that script runs the orchestrator in model mode. The same waypoint spans move the Go waypoint rows' attribution from one derive-layer rule to another while the label holds. That is the one change here a reader of the committed attribution entries needs to know: the shared-parent evidence they quote is no longer what the current configuration produces.

  One component could not be taken at the version its project calls latest. a2a-python's v1.1.3 and v1.1.4 exist only as GitHub tags, because upstream's PyPI publish job rejected their metadata. The lab stays on 1.1.2, the latest installable release, and the gap is upstream's, already filed there.
- Follow-up: none. No documented behaviour changed. The a2a-python packaging gap is upstream issue a2aproject/a2a-python#1199, filed by others and open, so no draft is added here.

Before this task a Helm-less host got through step 2 and then stopped at step 2b. One thing the brief expected did not hold. The images are not unchanged, only their sources are. The new digests, the Amazon Linux release and uv's version are recorded in `versions.yaml` as observations dated 2026-09-15, beside the earlier ones, and no pin moves.

## Gate 3 / both receivers / ingress namespace — With the ingress in its own ambient namespace and the control-plane namespace outside the mesh, do the counts, the trace shape and mTLS enforcement hold?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.13.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: the author's direction of 2026-09-12 — "why not from now to move the agentgateway ingress and egress each in its own namespace out of the control-plane namespace and in mesh?" — with the controller's qualification, which the author accepted: the egress already has its own namespace, `agentgateway-egress`, and stays outside ambient by agentgateway's documented egress shape, so only the ingress moves. No pin moves. Telemetry pins, all unmoved: collector=otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.160.0 (chart 0.173.1), jaeger=jaegertracing/jaeger:2.20.0 (chart 4.13.1), prometheus=prom/prometheus:v3.14.0 (chart 29.28.1), otel-go=v1.46.0, otel-go-contrib=v0.71.0, and the OpenTelemetry Python distro 0.65b0 with exporter 1.44.0.

  **The change** (commit "refactor(deploy): the agentgateway ingress in its own ambient namespace; the control-plane namespace left out of the mesh"):
  - The step-2b overlay creates the Namespace `agentgateway-ingress` with `istio.io/dataplane-mode: ambient`. The ingress Gateway, its `AgentgatewayParameters` and the port-15020 PERMISSIVE `PeerAuthentication` move there, the last with selector and ports unchanged.
  - The step-3 overlay moves the ingress's tracing and access-log `AgentgatewayPolicy` objects beside the Gateway.
  - The two HTTPRoutes in `lab` change `parentRefs[0].namespace`. The orchestrator's `PUBLIC_URL`, which its agent card advertises, becomes `http://agentgateway-ingress.agentgateway-ingress.svc.cluster.local`.
  - `make step-2b` no longer labels `agentgateway-system`. `agentgateway-values.yaml` loses the controller's `podLabels` opt-out and now sets nothing.
  - `REPLAY_INGRESS_NS`, the step-2b Programmed wait, and `INGRESS_NS` and the ingress `PROXY_NS` in `gate3-matrix.sh` and `gate3-gateway-retry-mechanics.sh` name the new namespace.
  - `versions.yaml`: `agentgateway-controlplane-ambient-optout` is marked `superseded`, and three keys are added for the documents read.

  **Documents read on 2026-09-15:**
  - Gateway API, attachment: "A Route can reference a Gateway by specifying the namespace (optional if the Route and the Gateway are in the same namespace) and name of the Gateway in a parentRef", and "All will allow Routes from all Namespaces to be attached" (concepts/api-overview).
  - Gateway API, grants: "Cross namespace Route -> Gateway binding follows a slightly different pattern where the handshake mechanism is built into the Gateway resource" (api-types/referencegrant). So the listener keeps `from: All` and no ReferenceGrant is added.
  - agentgateway chart v1.5.0 values: `rbac.gatewayNamespaces: []`, "An empty list preserves the default cluster-wide write access. ... Restricting this list means only Gateways in these namespaces can be used"; `discoveryNamespaceSelectors: []`.
  - agentgateway install page: "You can limit the namespaces that agentgateway watches for gateway configuration."
  - agentgateway's ambient-ingress page, re-read from the website repository at commit 3f96d16e: "For end-to-end ambient mTLS, both the namespace that runs the agentgateway ingress proxy and the namespace that runs the backend must be ambient-enabled." Its example then labels `agentgateway-system` and creates the Gateway there.

  - logs: `logs/`.
- Interpretation: the move holds on every figure checked, and mTLS enforcement does not depend on which namespace the control plane shares.

  The final mesh membership, and why:
  - **In:** the two agents, which are the traffic path.
  - **In:** the two istiod-driven waypoints, which terminate HBONE for the agents' Services in the enrolled `lab`.
  - **In:** the ingress proxy, whose hop to the orchestrator is HBONE because its namespace is enrolled, as agentgateway's ingress page requires.
  - **Out:** the egress proxy, by agentgateway's documented egress shape.
  - **Out:** the mock model, which stands in for an external provider and is reached in plaintext as the lab's external leg.
  - **Out:** the control plane, which is infrastructure. It serves XDS over its own TLS. Two of its three clients, the egress proxy and Prometheus, are outside the mesh; the third is the ingress proxy, which since this change dials it from inside the mesh, across the namespace boundary, and whose leg the hops table records.
  - **Out:** the telemetry namespace, because an in-mesh collector would refuse the plaintext OTLP of the uncaptured emitters.

  What changed is how the control plane is out. Before, it sat in a namespace enrolled for the ingress's sake and carried a per-pod opt-out, a label against its namespace. Now its namespace is not enrolled, so Istio's default leaves it out, and a request from a pod in that namespace is refused at both agents the way one from `telemetry` is.

  Against the documented shape, this is a deviation from agentgateway's ambient-ingress example, not from a requirement. The page's example creates the ingress Gateway in `agentgateway-system` and labels that namespace, while its stated requirement is only that the proxy's namespace be ambient-enabled. The lab meets the requirement with a namespace of its own. The Gateway API and the chart's defaults make that a change of namespaces and nothing more: a route's parentRef namespace, a listener already open to all namespaces, no ReferenceGrant, and a controller with cluster-wide write access. The rebuild showed the Gateway programmed, both routes accepted and both policies attached from the new namespace.

  The proof is a rebuild from a deleted cluster, because a change to who is captured is the case where a connection predating a policy can hide a refusal. The record is also plain that the host slept during that rebuild and its readings. The build's figures stand because every target exited 0 first time, with no hand on the cluster and no pod replaced or restarted across the sleeps. A check that a sleep interrupted was re-taken, not counted.

  Two readings in this entry are observations, not findings about the change. One is the registry 502 the kubelet recovered from. The other is what moves an image digest here: the orchestrator's because its build re-runs every layer, the Go images' because the commit is stamped into the binary. Neither changes a package, so a digest alone cannot decide whether to re-scan; the inputs a scan reads can, and they are unchanged. The Makefile item deferred from followups-11's review is closed: on a host without helm, a command line naming a Helm goal now stops before any goal runs, and README says that.
- Follow-up: none

## Gate 3 / both receivers / GenAI and agent spans — What does each agent emit under the GenAI semantic conventions at their Development revision, and does the added layer change any count?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.13.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: the author's direction of 2026-09-15 — name the lab's model call and its A2A call as the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions name them, after the controller's read of the sources that day. No pin in the line above moves. Telemetry pins, all unmoved: collector=otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.160.0 (chart 0.173.1), jaeger=jaegertracing/jaeger:2.20.0 (chart 4.13.1), prometheus=prom/prometheus:v3.14.0 (chart 29.28.1), otel-go=v1.46.0, otel-go-contrib=v0.71.0, the OpenTelemetry Python distro 0.65b0 with exporter 1.44.0, and **new here** opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-v2 2.4b0 with its transitive opentelemetry-util-genai 1.1b0.

  **The conventions, and what was taken from them.** They are not a release: the GenAI conventions moved into `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai`, which publishes none, so the pin is the repository commit read on 2026-09-16, `0c87594975195608dc91b3f702e250a7b240c151` (main, committed 2026-09-10). Both span pages read **`**Status**: [Development][DocumentStatus]`**. `versions.yaml`, `genai-semantic-conventions`, carries every rule quoted; the ones the lab implements are:
  - inference span: "**Span name** SHOULD be `{gen_ai.operation.name} {gen_ai.request.model}`"; "**Span kind** SHOULD be `CLIENT` … when the GenAI system being instrumented usually runs in a different process than its client"; `gen_ai.operation.name` and `gen_ai.provider.name` **Required**, `gen_ai.request.model` Conditionally Required "If available.", `gen_ai.response.id`, `gen_ai.response.model` and `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` Recommended, the two usage counts Recommended;
  - invoke agent client span: "Describes GenAI agent invocation over a remote service"; "**Span name** SHOULD be `invoke_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}` if `gen_ai.agent.name` is readily available"; kind CLIENT; `gen_ai.agent.name`, `gen_ai.agent.version` **and `gen_ai.agent.description`** each Conditionally Required "When available."; `gen_ai.conversation.id` "If and only if the instrumented library has one readily available", with "a new UUID, a trace identifier, or a hash of request content SHOULD NOT be used as a fallback value";
  - on both spans: `server.address` Recommended, `server.port` Conditionally Required "If `server.address` is set."; `error.type` Conditionally Required "If the operation ended in an error.", matching "the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library, the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier", with `500` among its example values;
  - and, on both: "If a transient issue happened and the request was retried automatically, the corresponding span SHOULD cover the duration of the logical operation with all retries." That sentence is why one span wraps a send including whatever the A.2 knobs re-send, which is also what keeps this instrumentation out of the knobs' code paths.

  **Two choices, recorded as choices.** `gen_ai.provider.name` is Required on both spans and the registry page says "If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used". None of its **16** well-known values names this lab's mock or an A2A agent. The deciding sentence for what to use instead is "The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider". So: **`openai` on the model leg**, because that flavor is OpenAI's chat-completions API and because the official Python instrumentation was *measured* to set exactly that against this same mock whatever the base URL is — anything else in Go would have made the two agents' chat spans incomparable; and **`a2a` on the agent leg**, a custom value, because the flavor there is A2A's. `gen_ai.agent.id` is set nowhere: it is Conditionally Required "If applicable", and an A2A v1.0 AgentCard carries no agent identifier (a2a-go's `a2a.AgentCard` and a2a-python 1.1.2's both have Name, Version and Description and no id field). `versions.yaml`, `genai-provider-name`.

PyPI on 2026-09-16: 2.4b0 is the latest of five releases, uploaded 2026-05-01T17:41:49Z, stated **"Development Status :: 4 - Beta"**, `requires_python >=3.10`, a `py3-none-any` wheel with classifiers through Python 3.14 — which is what answers the cp314 check here, a pure-Python wheel rather than a per-version one. `uv lock` resolved 66 packages with **no conflict** and moved nothing already pinned, adding two rows: the package and its one new transitive dependency **opentelemetry-util-genai 1.1b0** (also Beta, also `py3-none-any`).

- Interpretation: at this revision the conventions fit the lab's two operations without strain, and the added layer is additive in the strict sense — 46 count columns, the layer label, its derivation, the clean check, the trace shape, mTLS enforcement, the scrape targets and the scan all read exactly what they read before, and the only numbers that moved are span counts, by the spans added and by nothing else.

  What the run shows about the two ecosystems is asymmetric, and the asymmetry is the finding. Python has an official instrumentation for the model call and this lab did not write a line of code for it: the package produces a conformant `chat` span, with both Required attributes, from a dependency and an entry point. Go has none — `opentelemetry-go-contrib` carries no GenAI instrumentation and `a2a-go` no OpenTelemetry dependency — so the same span is a few dozen lines of this lab's own, and the conventions had to be read rather than imported. For the agent call neither ecosystem has anything: an A2A send is an HTTP POST to every instrumentation on the path, and the only component that knows it is an agent invocation is the caller, so both languages say so by hand. That is the shape of "end-to-end instrumented agentic traffic on CNCF projects" today: the model leg is solved on one side and not the other, and the agent leg is solved nowhere.

  Being written by hand cuts both ways, and the run measures both. The hand-written span carries more than the package's, because nothing stops it: `server.address`, `server.port` and the four `lab.*` identity attributes are on the Go `chat` span and on none of the package's. It also carries only what someone remembered to put there, which is why the first pass of this task shipped `invoke_agent` spans without `gen_ai.agent.description` — Conditionally Required, its condition met by a card the caller already held — and a `chat` span without the response model or the finish reasons the package had been emitting all along. The checker that now backs the claim tests three sets, not the two unconditionally Required attributes, and prints what each span lacks; a verifier that only checks what is easy to satisfy is not evidence for a sentence about completeness.

  Two properties of the lab survive the addition intact, and both were at risk. The first is the work item: a GenAI span is not an HTTP span, so the collector's `transform`, which reads captured headers, cannot reach it. Every span this lab writes therefore sets `lab.*` itself, and the share of a work item's spans that carry its id rose rather than fell. The package's `chat` span does not, which is recorded rather than worked around; it is reachable through the trace, not through an attribute query. The second is the A.2 and A.3 knob paths. One span wraps one logical invocation, including whatever a knob then re-sends, which is what the conventions ask for and what left `second_delivery_layer` and its `layer_reason` byte-identical on the R3 row — the derivation reads POST spans and parent chains, and the new spans are neither.

  The R3 row also produced the clearest single observation here. Its ledgers count two model invocations and the trace carries one `chat` span with two children, because the retry under test lives inside the openai client and the instrumentation wraps the call above it. Nothing is wrong on either side: the ledger counts what reached the endpoint and the span counts the logical operation, exactly as the conventions define it. It is a good illustration of this gate's rule that ledgers are ground truth and traces are the explanation, and a caution against reading a GenAI span count as a delivery count.

  The two provider names are the weakest part of this and are marked as such. The conventions leave the value open where none of their sixteen applies, so the lab chose, and the choice on the model leg was settled by measuring what the official Python instrumentation emits rather than by reasoning about it. Both pages read Status: Development and the Python package is published Beta with its own warning that breaking changes will come, so these names are the part most likely to need re-taking when either moves.

  What this round cost is worth recording beside what it found. Four builds ran and three were thrown away: one for a checkout that was not clean, one for a record that could not be read, and one because its own readings showed a comment wrong about the lab's topology. None of the three was discarded for a count — every count they took is the count this entry reports — and the decision each time was that a proof is the record as much as the numbers. The `server.address` correction is the useful one: it took a measurement to notice that this lab's clients are told an intermediary's address on three of their four legs, which is exactly the kind of thing a comment written from expectation gets wrong.
- Follow-up: none

## Gate 3 / go receiver / chat span on a failed model call — What does the GenAI span record when the model call fails, and does it agree with the ledgers?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.13.0
- Environment: kind

- Interpretation: on this binding the span does what the conventions ask of a failed operation, and the numbers agree with the ledgers. The pinned inference span makes `error.type` Conditionally Required "If the operation ended in an error." and says it "SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library, the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier", with `500` among its examples. Both readings carry a status code, the span status is ERROR as `recording-errors.md` (v1.44.0) says it SHOULD be, and the text the worker has always written is unchanged to the byte.

  What the attribute cannot say is **who made the status**, and the two readings differ exactly there.
  - In (b) the mock answered 500. The egress passed it through, and every span from the mock up to the chat span says 500.
  - In (a) the mock answered nothing. The egress waypoint synthesised the 503 when the mock's connection closed (`error.type=UpstreamFailure` on its own span), and the worker's client, which dials `model.lab.internal` and never sees the mock, records the 503 it received.
  - So `error.type=503` on a chat span means "the model leg answered 503 to this client", not "the provider said 503". The conventions' "error code returned by the Generative AI provider" is, to a client behind a proxy, the proxy's code. The ledger is what separates the two cases: `close/closed` in the invocation ledger against `http500/http500`.

  Two readings below the chat span disagree with the ledgers, and both are the instrumentation's defaults rather than faults in the lab.
  - The mock's server span reads `http.response.status_code=200` for a call its ledger records as closed with no response. otelhttp v0.71.0's response-writer wrapper starts at `http.StatusOK` as the "default status code in case the Handler doesn't write anything", and a hijacked connection writes nothing.
  - The egress waypoint marks its own synthesised 503 as an error but leaves a passed-through 500 UNSET.
  - Neither touches a count, and both are why the gate's rule holds: the ledgers count and the trace explains, and a span's status is evidence only after the ledger has said what happened.

  One small tension with the conventions is recorded rather than resolved. `recording-errors.md` says "It's NOT RECOMMENDED to duplicate status code or `error.type` in span status description", and the lab's description, the Go error's message, contains the code. The same document says "When the operation fails with an exception, the span status description SHOULD be set to the exception message", and the Go error's message is the nearest thing Go has to one. The lab keeps it for a reason of its own: the description is the execution ledger's error text, byte for byte, so a reader can join the span to its ledger line on that text. Changing it would take a code change in `internal/otel`, which this entry does not make. It is not an upstream gap, and whether to drop the code from the description is queued for the next code branch.
- Follow-up: none. There is no upstream gap. The span-description question above concerns the lab's own code and is queued for the next code branch.

The filter's `/healthz` span conditions sit ahead of `batch` in the traces pipeline (`deploy/step-3-stress/otel-collector-values.yaml`:149–155, pipeline :194) |
  | worker, orchestrator, mock, load client | **no metrics at all**: no `/metrics` route and no meter provider in the Go binaries (`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric` is only indirect, so otelhttp's instruments go to the no-op global meter); the orchestrator runs with `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none` | | |

  **Clean run: 20 work items, 10 per receiver** (`clean-hop-table.csv`, `clean-delta-*.csv`, `clean-ledgers.csv`). Before and after were read at 21:34:16.770Z and 21:44:47.766Z; every target was scraped within the 15 s before each reading, and all 9 were up both times.

  | hop | counter series (delta) | ledger, same 20 work items | spans in the same traces (requests) |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | → worker waypoint, SendMessage (both flows) | `requests_total{agentgateway-waypoint, lab/worker, POST, 200}` **20** | worker arrivals **20** | |
  | load Job → worker waypoint, agent card | `{…, GET, 200}` **10** | none (not a SendMessage) | |
  | control pod → worker waypoint, injector reset | `{…, POST, 204}` **20** | none (`/control/*` is excluded from the ledger) | |
  | worker waypoint, every series | **50** | worker arrivals 20 | 60 (30) |
  | load Job → orchestrator waypoint, agent card | `{agentgateway-waypoint-orch, GET, 200}` **10**, plus `{POST, 204}` 20 resets | none | 20 (10) |
  | load Job → ingress, SendMessage | `{agentgateway-ingress, lab/orchestrator-ingress, POST, 200}` **10** | orchestrator arrivals **10** | 20 (10) |
  | worker → egress, model call | `{agw-egress, POST, 200}` **20** | invocations **20** | 40 (20) |

  | worker; orchestrator; mock | no counter | arrivals / dispatches 20 / 20; 10 / 10; invocations 20 | 70; 540; 20 |

  - At L4, ztunnel counted **connections, not requests**:
    - load Job → worker waypoint 10, load Job → orchestrator waypoint 10, load Job → ingress 10 (reported by both ends), orchestrator → worker waypoint 10;
    - waypoint → worker **1**, orchestrator waypoint → orchestrator **1**, ingress → orchestrator **1**, worker → egress **1**: pooled connections, whatever the request count;
    - nothing on egress → mock, because neither end is captured.
  - The agentgateway downstream-connection counters agree with ztunnel's source reports, hop for hop: worker waypoint 40 = 10 load Jobs + 20 control-pod connections + 10 orchestrator; orchestrator waypoint 30; ingress 10; egress 1.
  - **Every trace was the committed shape**: 14 and 69 spans on all 20 work items, `hops_without_span` none.

  **With a retry on the path** (`r2-waypoint-table.csv`, `egress-table.csv`), 6 work items each, the dry run included:

  | row | proxy | `requests_total` | `retries_total` | requests + retries | `upstream_call_duration_seconds_count`, less the proxy's other requests | ledger |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | R2 waypoint | worker waypoint | **6** (`POST 200`) | **6** (`status="200"`) | 12 | 38 − 26 = **12** | deliveries at the worker **12**; dispatches 6; Tasks 6; invocations 6 |
  | egress | egress | **6** (`POST 500`) | **6** (`status="500"`) | 12 | 12 − 0 = **12** | invocations **12**; deliveries 6; dispatches 6; Tasks 6 |

  - **A hop counter that disagrees with the ledgers, with both numbers.** `agentgateway_requests_total` counts **6** on each row, where the worker counted **12** deliveries (R2) and the mock **12** invocations (egress). The counter records one request per downstream request, at its **final** status: R2 has no 503 series for the refused first attempt, and egress has one 500 per model call, not two.
  - **The proxy does expose a retry counter.** `agentgateway_retries_total` was absent from every proxy until its first retry. It appeared at 6 on the worker's waypoint and at 6 on the egress, carrying the retried request's **final** status (`200` and `500`), not the status that triggered the retry.
  - The second attempt is also a second sample of `agentgateway_upstream_call_duration_seconds_count`. That histogram has no route or status label, so the proxy's other requests have to be subtracted by hand: 20 control POSTs and 6 card GETs on the waypoint, which the matrix's own `control.txt` confirms (20 POSTs to the worker, all answered 204).
  - ztunnel shows nothing of either retry. It counted one waypoint → worker connection opened in the R2 window, and its access log shows that connection was the only one open for the whole stimulus, so it carried all 12 deliveries (`waypoint-connections.txt`, from the committed `waypoint-connections.sh`, read in the review round before the second rebuild deleted that cluster). The previous one closed at 21:45:50.177Z; this one opened at 21:46:05.747Z and closed at 21:50:59.421Z; the stimulus ran from 21:46:04Z to 21:49:22Z.
  - **What agentgateway's data-plane page says the two counters count** (1.5.x, `documents.txt`). The page opens: "Metrics are collected automatically for every request that passes through the gateway". Its table reads `agentgateway_requests_total` "The total number of HTTP requests sent." and `agentgateway_retries_total` "The total number of request retries."
    - The retry counter is **as documented**: 6 retries, and 6 counted, on each row.
    - The request counter's description is **ambiguous**, not silent. On a proxy whose series carry `backend` and `reason="Upstream"`, "requests sent" reads naturally as sent to the backend. On R2, 12 requests were sent to the backend and 6 were counted. The opening sentence ("every request that passes through the gateway") supports the other reading.
    - The measurement and the v1.5.0 source settle it the same way: one increment per downstream request, at its final status. Every HTTP metric is recorded in the request log's `drop()` (`crates/agentgateway/src/telemetry/log.rs`:1214), with labels that carry the final response status (:1261). `requests` gets `.inc()` (:1330) and `retries` gets `.inc_by(retry_count)` (:1346–1351) under the same labels. The HELP strings are at `metrics.rs`:420–421 and :561–562 (fetched in this session, sha256 in `documents.txt`).
    - Which `status` a retry's series carries is not on the page: measured, and in the source, it is the final status.
    - The page's own example "Error rate" query, `rate(agentgateway_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]) / rate(agentgateway_requests_total[5m])`, therefore counts only final statuses. A 503 that a route retry turned into a 200 never appears in it, as R2 shows.
    - A minimal draft asks the page to say so: `docs/upstream/agentgateway-requests-total-under-retry.md`.
  - Every row reproduced its committed values: R2 5 of 5 `2 1 1 1 1 task/TASK_STATE_COMPLETED gateway`; egress 5 of 5 `1 1 1 1 2 task/TASK_STATE_FAILED gateway`; each dry run the same.

  **What the counters cannot say**, as measured here:
  - **No family on any target carries a work-item, message or task identity.** Counts are per route, per status and per workload, never per work item. Which of the 20 deliveries belonged to which work item, and whether a second delivery was a replay of the first, only the ledgers (body hash, `messageId`, JSON-RPC `id`) and the trace can say.
  - **The agentgateway request counter has no path and no source label.** On the worker's waypoint a SendMessage, an agent-card GET and a control reset share one route. They were told apart here only because they differ in method or status (`POST 200`, `GET 200`, `POST 204`), and a failed SendMessage answered 204 would not be.
  - It also cannot tell the two flows' deliveries apart: the load Job's and the orchestrator's both arrive as `route=lab/worker`. ztunnel's source labels can split them, but only as connections, which pooling decouples from requests (one connection for 20 model calls).
  - **The receivers and the mock have no counter at all.** Dispatches, Tasks and invocations exist only in the ledgers, and the egress → mock leg only as the egress's upstream histogram.
  - **A retried request is one request with a retry on the side.** Anyone summing `requests_total` for "how many times did the model get called" gets half the answer under a route retry, and the retry counter's `status` label names the outcome, not the trigger.

  **Three families appeared that are not request flow**, and each was traced to its events rather than left unexplained (`failed-connections.txt`, from the committed `failed-connections.sh`):
  - `agentgateway_xds_connection_terminations_total{reason="Error"}` on both waypoints (21:42:26Z and 21:43:26Z) and `istio_xds_connection_terminations_total{reason="Reconnect"}` on both ztunnels (21:42:56Z and 21:43:56Z), each 1. They fell inside the clean window, 31–33 minutes after istiod started (pod start 21:11:21Z). They are control-plane connections, and no work item's count moved.
  - `istio_tcp_connections_failed_total{response_flags="CONNECT"}`, HELP "The total number of TCP connections that failed to establish (unstable)", rose four times. Each rise matches one ztunnel access-log line at level `error`, "connection complete … while closing connection: … broken pipe", and those are the only error lines either ztunnel logged since the rebuild.
    - The connections had been established for 293–782 s and had carried 648–13 792 bytes each way (`waypoint-connections.txt` and `failed-connections.txt`). The two orchestrator → waypoint ones carried about 750 bytes each, about one request's worth, and lingered: they had opened at 21:18:38Z and 21:43:50Z.
    - Two were orchestrator → worker waypoint, at 21:31:41Z and 21:56:52Z, both outside the counted windows.
    - Two were waypoint → worker and waypoint-orch → orchestrator, 51 ms apart at 21:50:59Z, inside the egress window, in the same second the egress row applied its route retry. That timing is observed, not attributed.
    - ztunnel 1.31.0's `src/proxy/metrics.rs` maps any error it does not recognise to `ConnectionFailure` (`CONNECT`), and counts every such connection as failed.
  - No delivery was lost to those closes, and the records show it two ways.
    - The committed ledgers of this task's two run directories hold 60 SendMessage arrivals, each with its response line: 12 in the previous entry's directory and 48 in this one.
    - The receivers' own logs over the whole period, 21:08:56Z to 22:01:22Z, hold **61** arrivals and **61** responses (worker 48, orchestrator 13), and 43 agent-card GETs, each paired (`pairs.txt`, from the committed `pairs.sh`, read in the review round before the second rebuild deleted that cluster). The 61st is `a3m-baseline-go-fmca-dry`, the previous entry's A.3 baseline dry run, whose directory `gate3-matrix.sh` deletes. None is unpaired.

  **Host** (`host-sleep.txt`, by pmset's event-kind field `$4`, windows in `windows.csv`): 0 Sleep, 0 Wake, 0 DarkWake and 0 Maintenance lines in any window, from 21:31:23Z to 21:59:27Z. The Assertions lines are listed in full, and a dated note of the review round attributes the `caffeinate -i -t 300` streams in them:
  - the one ending at :54 of each cycle is this task's agent;
  - the one ending at :17 is the controller's session;
  - the one ending at :04, which ended at 21:32:44Z, before the first counted run, is not attributed.

  Run outputs are under `experiments/runs/2026-09-19-metrics-per-hop/`:
  - `promql.txt`, `samples/*.json` (six readings);
  - `clean-delta-series.csv`, `clean-delta-hops.csv`, `clean-hop-table.csv`, `clean-ledgers.csv`, and the same four for `r2-waypoint` and `egress`, with `*-table.csv`;
  - `inventory.csv`, `families-start.csv`, `families-end.csv`, `documents.txt`, `prometheus-config.txt`, `failed-connections.txt`;
  - `clean/`, `r2-waypoint-go/`, `egress-go/`, `dry-runs/`, `logs/`, `host-sleep.txt`, `windows.csv`;
  - the tools `exposition.sh`, `read-hops.sh`, `counted-run.sh`, `delta.py`, `ledger-summary.py`, `inventory.py`, `hop-table.py`, `retry-table.py`, `failed-connections.sh`, `host-sleep.sh`;
  - the review round's: `pairs.txt` with `pairs.sh` and `pairs.py`, `waypoint-connections.txt` with its `.sh` and `.py`, and `collector-8888-extract.txt`.
- Interpretation: under this configuration Prometheus sees a work item's path only where agentgateway sits on it. The two waypoints, the ingress and the egress each count requests by route, method and status, and on a clean run those counts equal the ledgers', to the request, once the right series is chosen. Everywhere else the answer is no request-level count at all:
  - the receivers, the mock and the load client export nothing;
  - ztunnel counts connections, and connection pooling decouples those from requests;
  - the collector's metrics endpoint is empty, and its own span counters are served but not scraped;
  - istiod and the agentgateway control plane count configuration.

  On a clean path the ledger and the metric are two views of the same number.

  Under a retry they are not, and the difference is structural, not a miscount. `agentgateway_requests_total` counts what the proxy was asked to do, one request at its final status; the ledgers count what arrived at each end. A route retry doubled the deliveries at the worker and the invocations at the mock, and the request counter did not move beyond one per request. The retry is visible to Prometheus only through a counter that exists after the first retry, and whose `status` label names how the request ended, not why it was retried. Reading "how many deliveries did the receiver get" off the proxy therefore needs `requests_total + retries_total`. That sum matched the ledgers on both rows here, but it is still not a per-work-item count, and nothing in the metrics says which work item was delivered twice. That question belongs to the ledgers and to the trace, which shows the second attempt as its own span under the proxy's.

  Two of the lab's pages are wrong about what a reader will find, and both are drafted upstream.
  - Istio's ambient troubleshooting page says a waypoint brings "the full set of Istio and Envoy metrics". An agentgateway waypoint brings agentgateway's metrics and no `istio_requests_total`, and no Istio page says so.
  - ztunnel's `istio_tcp_connections_failed_total` says it counts connections that failed to establish. Here it counted four established connections that closed with an error.

  Neither affected a count in this entry. Both would mislead anyone building on these metrics without the ledgers beside them.
- Follow-up: three drafts, not filed: docs/upstream/agentgateway-requests-total-under-retry.md, docs/upstream/istio-agentgateway-waypoint-metrics-undocumented.md, docs/upstream/ztunnel-tcp-connections-failed-counts-closed-connections.md

## Gate 3 / both receivers / ztunnel certificate renewal across host sleep — Why did 24 h ztunnel leaves expire unrenewed on this kind cluster, and when does ztunnel renew after the host sleeps?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.13.0
- Environment: kind (Docker Desktop 4.91.0 build 239619, engine 29.8.0, Apple Virtualization framework: `UseVirtualizationFramework: true`; node kernel 7.0.12-linuxkit, both node containers privileged; host macOS 27.0 (26A428) arm64 on AC, `pmset -g custom` AC `sleep 0`, `powernap 1`)
- Method: one run, 2026-09-19T00:05:37Z–02:20:44Z: one forced host sleep, one ztunnel restart. No repetition.

  **The model tested**, from ztunnel's source at tag `1.31.0` (tag object `e6fdcc5b…`; the running ztunnel's own version line prints commit `44beaefc…`, RustVersion 1.94.0), lines re-read 2026-09-19T02:28:56Z. A leaf's refresh point is R = NOT BEFORE + half the lifetime, in wall-clock time (`src/tls/certificate.rs` 402–408). It is turned into a tokio `Instant` through a wall↔monotonic `Converter` (`src/identity/manager.rs` 413, `src/time.rs` 18–43) that is built once per process (`manager.rs` 570), and the worker sleeps until it (`manager.rs` 504). So the refresh should fire at the wall time t where **t − D(t) = R**, with D the guest's (wall − CLOCK_MONOTONIC) divergence accumulated since that ztunnel started. Predictions P0–P4 and the three competing explanations (renewal at wake; never; the VM's clocks do not diverge) were written before the run (`.superpowers/sdd/followups-16/phase-2-brief-draft.md`, not committed; the predictions are restated below with each verdict).

  **The lab.** Branch `followups-16` at `706485c`. The standard lab was rebuilt from a deleted cluster by the seven make targets (`teardown`, `cluster-kind`, `step-1`, `step-2`, `step-2b`, `step-2c`, `step-3`), each exit 0, 380 s in all; `git status --short` was empty before the teardown, and the deployed paths' status was empty before every target; `step-3`'s certificate check read VALID CERT true and did not restart ztunnel. Clean check: `1/1/1/1/1` and `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` on both receivers (`rebuild/`).

  **The driver.** One detached script, `driver.sh` (bash 3.2, started with `nohup` in its own session, pid 41413), ran every arm by itself; it runs no make target, starts no keep-awake and changes no power setting. Its offline suite (`test/`, every cluster and power command replaced by a simulator's reading) read 91 PASS, 0 FAIL before the start; shellcheck is not installed on this host.
  - **Throwaway configuration.** The Makefile's own ztunnel helm command with a second values file kept in the run directory: `env.SECRET_TTL: "10m"` and `logLevel: "info,ztunnel::identity=debug"`. Leaves are then 12 min (10 min + istiod's 2 min backdating), so R = issuance + 4 min. istiod was not touched.
  - **A fix before the start.** The first preflight failed with nothing applied: the standard lab's ztunnel DaemonSet already carries `RUST_LOG=info`, which the chart renders from its `logLevel` value (`manifests/charts/ztunnel/templates/daemonset.yaml` 130–131 at 1.31.0) before it appends the `env` map (187–191). The design's override put `RUST_LOG` under `env`; rendered locally with `helm template`, that gives the container two `RUST_LOG` entries. With `logLevel` the whole rendering differs from the committed one in two lines. The restore's readback was tightened at the same time: the whole DaemonSet env must equal the list captured at preflight (`ds-env.standard.txt`, 16 entries). Recorded in `rulings.txt` item 6 and `preflight.txt`.
  - **Instruments**, all reads. Guest clocks on both nodes every 10 s, every 5 s for 3 min after a gap: wall, CLOCK_MONOTONIC (`/proc/timer_list` "now at"), CLOCK_BOOTTIME (`/proc/uptime`), wall again, in one `docker exec`, bracketed by host reads; beside them the host's CLOCK_MONOTONIC − CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW, its own total of time asleep (`clock.csv`, 1270 rows). `istioctl ztunnel-config certificates` for both nodes every 30 s, every 15 s for 10 min after a gap (`certs.csv`, 492 Leaf rows; VALID CERT is istioctl's, by the host's clock). istiod's `citadel_server_csr_count` and `citadel_server_success_cert_issuance_count` every 60 s from istiod's port 15014 through the API server's pod proxy (`csr-counters.csv`). One in-mesh GET of the worker's Agent Card per minute from a probe pod in `lab`, `curl -sS --retry 0 --max-time 10`, no loop on failure (`probe.csv`, 104 rows). `pmset -g log` for the window and `pmset -g assertions` snapshots. ztunnel's identity debug lines. No read failed in the run (no `read-errors.log`).
  - **Arms.** C: 1802 s awake, instruments only. T: `pmset sleepnow` 30 s after a renewal of `lab/sa/default` on the worker node; a wake is a host-clock step of more than 60 s between two ticks of the 5 s loop; the window after it ends at 3900 s awake and two renewals since the last gap of 900 s or more (cap 8 h). P4: `kubectl -n istio-system rollout restart ds/ztunnel`, two renewals. Restore.
  - **Derivation** (`derive-renewals.py`). Per serial change: R_prev from the replaced leaf; t_w = NOT BEFORE of the new leaf + 120 s; D(t_w) between the two clock samples that bracket t_w on the guest's wall-clock axis, against the first sample after that ztunnel's start; **residual = t_w − D(t_w) − R_prev**. A residual whose bracketing samples straddle a step is marked ambiguous, not guessed; none was. Certificate stamps are whole seconds. So a second reading was **added after the run**, from its records only: `post-analysis.py` repeats the residual with the sub-second stamp of ztunnel's "certificate fetch succeeded" line (`renewals-logstamp.csv`; called "log stamps" below). Each collected line carries two stamps, the container runtime's first and ztunnel's own second, at most 0.343 ms apart on the run's 48 lines; the script pairs the first, and no number below changes at three decimals. No verdict leans on this reading: the 5 s predictions hold under both.
  - **Rulings of the controller** (`rulings.txt`). The gate after arm C ran with a 30 s tolerance instead of the 5 s of the prediction: it decides only whether arm T is worth the night. P1 below is judged against 5 s. The restore may try helm three times.

  **Scope of what was read.** The control-plane node's ztunnel holds no certificate in this lab (its table is the header line), so every renewal below is one of the worker node's two identities, `lab/sa/default` and `agentgateway-ingress/sa/agentgateway-ingress`. Clocks were read on both nodes and agree (one VM, one kernel).
- Result: `experiments/runs/2026-09-19-ztunnel-renewal/` (`summary.txt`, `renewals.csv`, `renewals-logstamp.csv`, `gaps-d.csv`, `d-series.csv`, `host-sleep.txt`, `post-analysis.txt`).

  **The host, from pmset's log** (`host-sleep.txt`, verbatim there). `pmset sleepnow`, issued 00:38:17Z without root, exited 0 ("Sleeping now..."). pmset logged `Entering Sleep state due to 'Software Sleep pid=54934'` at 00:38:22Z (3 secs), a DarkWake at 00:38:25Z for a Wi-Fi packet (11 secs), then `'Maintenance Sleep'` from 00:38:36Z (1023 secs). The wake at 00:55:39Z was **not the author**: `DarkWake from Deep Idle … rtc/Maintenance`, at the time a `dasd` timer had requested, and the host stayed in that DarkWake for 4400 secs. The whole observation window ran inside it. The one idle-sleep assertion held at the request (`PreventUserIdleSystemSleep`, the agent harness's `caffeinate`) did not stop the forced sleep. No `Wake` line is in the window.

  |---|---|---|---|

The host's own clocks put its sleep across the same samples at **1020.476 s**; pmset's two Sleep lines span 3 + 1023 s by their stamps; the driver's gap is 1026 s (00:38:33Z → 00:55:39Z). The 0.081 s between the two is pmset's first 3 "secs" sleep, of which the host's clocks count 0.082 s, before the last sample ahead of the gap.   | P3 | every later leaf is late by the same D until a restart | **held** | Next renewals 01:19:43Z and 01:40:43Z: **21 min 00 s apart = 4 min + 1020 s**. Residuals −0.557 and −0.555 s (certificate stamps); all six post-wake renewals **+0.015 / +0.034 / +0.059 s** by log stamps, the same as awake.   | P4 | a ztunnel restart returns the cadence to 4 min | **held**, over two cycles | Restart 02:00:45Z; the leaf it replaced had been past NOT AFTER for 602 s. Renewals 02:04:45Z and 02:08:45Z, residual ±0.000 s (certificate stamps), +0.005 to +0.020 s (log stamps), D 0.000 s. |

  **Three independent counts reconcile.** The run has **28 serial changes: 26 renewals and the 2 issuances of the P4 restart.** istiod's CSR counter rose 9 → 35, **+26**, equal in every window to the serial changes whose issuance falls in it: C 14, the wait before the sleep 2, T 6, P4 4 (the 2 restart issuances and the 2 renewals of 02:04:45Z); the success counter the same. Its last reading is 02:08:39Z, six seconds before the final pair of renewals (02:08:45Z), which no reading covers: 26 + 2 = 28. ztunnel's "certificate fetch succeeded" lines number **30 = the 2 issuances at Setup + 28**: 16 in the log collected after C (2 + 14), 24 after T (the same pods, cumulative), 6 after P4 (new pods: 2 + 4), 0 after the restore (default filter).

  **CLOCK_BOOTTIME did not count the freeze.** D from `/proc/uptime` and D from `/proc/timer_list` differ by at most 0.006 s over the whole run: both guest clocks stood still while the host slept. The guest kernel did not see a suspend.

  **Silent, and not re-requested.** ztunnel's log from its start to the end of arm T (699 lines) has 0 lines at warn or error. While the tracked leaf was past NOT AFTER, 33 probe requests crossed the mesh with that identity (by the guest's clock; 34 by the host's, see below) and the CSR counter did not move: in arm T it rose by exactly the 6 late renewals.

  **Not decidable from this run: whether connections fail while a leaf is expired.** All **104 probes returned HTTP 200. 34 of them fell while the tracked leaf was past NOT AFTER by the host's clock, 33 by the guest's wall clock**, the one ztunnel and its peers read: the first of the 34 (host 00:55:39Z) ran in the seconds after the wake, before the guest's wall clock was stepped, at about 00:38:39Z by the guest, nine minutes before NOT AFTER (`probe-by-validity.csv`, regenerated with both clocks). By window the 34 are 3 in the 184 s after the wake (that one among them), then 11, 10 and 10, the last window cut at 602 s by the restart. One request a minute stays inside ztunnel's pooled-connection idle release of 5 min (`src/config.rs` 105), so the run cannot tell a pooled HBONE connection, handshaken while the leaf was valid, from a new handshake. The design said so beforehand. Nothing here shows a failure, and nothing here shows that a new connection would succeed.

  **The restore, and the host sleep that interrupted it.** The driver issued no second sleep request (`sleep-attempts.txt` has one entry). The restore's first helm upgrade started at 02:08:56Z; the new ztunnel pods started at 02:08:58Z and 02:08:59Z; at 02:08:59Z the host, still in DarkWake, entered `'Maintenance Sleep'` (645 secs) — pmset's log puts the release of the last `dasd` BackgroundTask assertion and of the kernel's CPU and NETWORK assertions at that same second. On the DarkWake at 02:19:44Z the driver's 600 s cap on that command had passed on the wall clock, it ended helm, and helm recorded revision 3 as `failed: context canceled`. The driver's second route, the same upgrade from the chart archive it had pulled at Setup, completed at 02:20:07Z as revision 4. **Read back at 02:20:42Z (`restore-readback.txt`):** `helm get values` equal to `deploy/step-2-ambient-agw/ztunnel-values.yaml` alone; the DaemonSet env identical to the one captured at preflight, 16 entries, `SECRET_TTL=168h`, `RUST_LOG=info`; the same two values on both ztunnel pods; rollout 2/2/2/2, generation 4 observed; both worker leaves 604 920 s (168 h 02 min), VALID CERT true; active filter `hickory_server::server=off,info` on both pods; the probe pod absent; helm history 1 install, 2 override, 3 failed, 4 deployed. The controller read the same state independently at 02:22Z. Across that second sleep D grew 641.787 s against the host's 641.786 s. That recomputes from one clock sample per node after the gap, taken 25.8 s after the wake with the wall clock already stepped: the growth was measured a second time, the step's timing was not.

  **What the run showed about its own driver.** The cap on a long command counts wall time, so a host sleep inside the command spends it; that, not helm, ended the first restore attempt. `anchors.csv` has one malformed row at P4, for the old worker pod still terminating. A sleep shorter than 60 s (the first 3 s one) is not a driver gap by design; the host-sleep column covers it.

  **Left out of the commit** (`.gitignore` in the run directory says why): `chart/` (the pulled chart archive, a binary the Makefile's pins reproduce; its sha256 is in `driver-log.txt`), `logs/` (whole pod logs, 1.5 MB; every identity and TLS line is kept in `ztunnel-<node>-identity.after-<arm>.txt`), `host-sleep-window-raw.txt` (pmset's whole window), and `*.uncut`: the four `pmset -g assertions` snapshots as the driver wrote them. In the committed snapshots the Kernel Assertions block's nine lines of kind `0x4=USB` were cut after the run and one line put in their place, because each ends in `owner=<device name>`, the names of the host's USB peripherals, and no reading uses them; the system-wide totals by kind, every process-owned assertion with its owner, and the kernel assertions of kind THNDR, CPU and MAGICWAKE are as written. No other file of this commit carries those names, nor the host's name or serial number (searched). The repository's `.gitignore` leaves out `*.log`, so `driver.log` and the identity extracts are committed as `.txt` copies.
- Interpretation: as the source predicts, under this configuration and at this version. ztunnel 1.31.0's refresh deadline is a monotonic-clock deadline computed through a wall↔monotonic anchor taken once at process start. When the Mac sleeps, this Docker Desktop VM's monotonic and boot-time clocks both stand still and its wall clock is stepped forward about 25 s after the wake. From then on every refresh of that ztunnel fires late by the time the host slept — measured here to within 0.06 s, for the first renewal after the wake and for each one after it — and nothing re-anchors it but a restart. With a 12 min leaf and 17 min of host sleep, each leaf spent 11 of every 21 minutes past NOT AFTER, was still the leaf ztunnel held, was not re-requested while traffic used it, and produced no log line at warn or error. The three competing explanations are refuted for this platform. This reproduces a mechanism sufficient for the lab's two expiries of 24 h leaves (2026-09-11 and 2026-09-12), and one a ztunnel restart remedies, as it did then. It does not show that it was their cause: those nights are not re-measured, their host-sleep totals can no longer be read (they would have had to exceed 12 h 01 min after each ztunnel start), and one open point in the lab's record stays open (on 2026-09-09 a leaf was renewed on time after five hours without recorded activity on the host). By the same arithmetic, not measured here, a lab leaf of 168 h passes NOT AFTER unrenewed only once a ztunnel has accumulated more than 84 h 01 min of host sleep, which is why the longer lifetime masks the behaviour rather than removing it: the lab's certificate check before every mesh run stays. Arithmetic again, from this run's records: the ztunnel now standing took its anchor about one second before the 645 s maintenance sleep (pod start 02:08:58Z, sleep entry 02:08:59Z), so it already carries D ≈ 641.8 s and gains every later host sleep; its 168 h leaves are due for refresh 83 h 59 min + D after issuance, and would pass NOT AFTER first only on a cluster kept for many nights on a host that sleeps. The standing remedy, a recorded ztunnel restart, resets D. Two things the run adds that the lab did not know: this host enters maintenance sleep from a DarkWake on AC with `sleep 0` while unattended work is running, and a forced sleep needs no root.
- Follow-up: docs/upstream/ztunnel-renewal-after-host-sleep.md (a draft comment for istio/ztunnel#1481, open; not filed)

## Gate 3 / go receiver / the documented AgentgatewayPolicy tracing on an istiod-managed agentgateway waypoint — Does the policy of agentgateway's tracing page reach a waypoint that istiod manages?
- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.2 openai-python=3.13.0
- Environment: kind
- Method: a re-check at the author's direction of 2026-09-19, who pointed at agentgateway's Kubernetes tracing page ("there is no way this will not work for tracing … review your work again against it and let's confirm it is working, otherwise we need to report a bug") and then asked whether the lab's own route for the istiod-managed waypoints could be what conflicts with it. Two repetitions of one sequence on the standing cluster, each ending with the lab restored and read back.

  **The page**, fetched in this session (`sources.md`; one `curl --retry 0` per page, HTML not committed): https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/latest/documentation/observability/traces/configs/otel/ at 08:57:12Z, HTTP 200, 455 555 bytes, sha256 `4c43d051148d4277…`, the same bytes as the controller's fetch of 08:45:39Z; "Version 1.5.x". Its prerequisite is "Set up an agentgateway proxy"; its instruction is "Create an AgentgatewayPolicy that points the agentgateway proxy at the collector"; its manifest is an `AgentgatewayPolicy` (`agentgateway.dev/v1alpha1`) with `targetRefs` to a `Gateway` and `spec.frontend.tracing` {`backendRef` name, namespace, port 4317; `protocol: GRPC`; `randomSampling: "true"`}. The page's body names Istio, a waypoint or a GatewayClass 0 times; the prerequisite page (fetched 08:58:40Z) creates the Gateway the manifest targets with `gatewayClassName: agentgateway`. `2-doc-policy/policy.yaml` is the manifest field for field with four names changed (the policy's namespace, the target Gateway `lab/agentgateway-waypoint`, the collector Service and its namespace); both repetitions applied that one file (sha256 `2c1b5ae1…`).

  **The sequence**, on `lab/agentgateway-waypoint` only (GatewayClass `istio-agentgateway-waypoint`, whose `spec.controllerName` on this cluster is `istio.io/agentgateway-waypoint-controller`): (1) the lab's `parametersRef` overlay lifted, so istiod renders the waypoint with `args ["--config","{}"]`; (2) the page's policy applied, its status read, the waypoint's admin `/config_dump` read, the ingress's read beside it as the positive control (GatewayClass `agentgateway`, controller `agentgateway.dev/agentgateway`, holding the lab's standing tracing policy of the same shape plus `clientSampling`), the agentgateway controller's push lines extracted, one traced work item sent; (3) the author's question: the policy deleted, the lab's three Istio `Telemetry` objects deleted (0 left in the cluster), a new waypoint pod, `spec.infrastructure` `{}`, then the page's policy re-created and the same readings; the Gateway object keeps two annotations: `gateway.istio.io/agentgatewayImage`, step 2's pin of the proxy image (sourced from Istio's own code at tag 1.31.0, `pkg/kube/inject/inject.go` and the waypoint template, `versions.yaml` key `agentgateway`; Istio's agentgateway page names it 0 times), and kubectl's `last-applied-configuration`, which still holds the `parametersRef` while, in the same block of the record (`rep-2/3-doc-policy-nothing-custom/steps.txt` lines 11–13), the args read `["--config","{}"]` and `spec.infrastructure` reads `{}`: istiod rendered from the spec, not from the annotation; (4) restore: the policy deleted, `deploy/step-3-stress/istio-tracing.yaml` applied by file, the `parametersRef` put back, one traced work item per receiver. What stayed in place through (3), touched by no step of either repetition (read live at 09:48:26Z and 10:03:09Z, `sources.md` §8, and in the committed file named): istiod's `PILOT_ENABLE_AGENTGATEWAY=true`, the lab's setting, on which the class depends (Istio's page: "agentgateway support is gated behind the `PILOT_ENABLE_AGENTGATEWAY` feature flag on istiod, and is disabled by default."), and `PILOT_TRACE_SAMPLING=1`, which is not the lab's: it is the istiod chart's default (`values.yaml:18` at 1.31.0, `traceSampling: 1.0`), absent from helm's user-supplied values and set nowhere under `deploy/`; the mesh configuration's `enableTracing: true` and its `otel-tracing` extension provider (`deploy/step-2-ambient-agw/istio-values.yaml`), which the three `Telemetry` objects only selected; the mesh-wide STRICT `PeerAuthentication` `istio-system/default` and the ingress's port-15020 scrape exception; `HTTPRoute lab/worker` (parentRef Service `worker`, status from `istio.io/agentgateway-waypoint-controller`) and `ServiceEntry lab/model-external`; the two Gateway annotations above; and the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt` annotation that step (3)'s own `rollout restart` writes on the Deployment's pod template.

  **Repetition 1** was run by hand by the controller, 08:46:45Z–08:52Z, and began with one work item on the standing configuration. **Repetition 2** is `reproduce.sh`, run once, 09:12:04Z–09:15:44Z, exit 0 (an attempt at 09:07:53Z that ended on the script's own port-forward defect before any work item was sent, the restore read back, is kept as `rep-2-aborted/` with `ABORTED.txt` and is not counted): it refuses a start that is not the standard state, waits only by reading objects (a Deployment's args and rollout, a Gateway's pods, the policy's conditions until they exist, whatever they read), reads each dump with one `curl --retry 0` through a port-forward, and sleeps a fixed 30 s between the status read and the dump because there is nothing to poll for a delivery that may never come. It adds two readings repetition 1 did not take: a second dump after the traced work item, and from it the waypoint's own per-endpoint `totalRequests` counter (`requests-carried.py`, added after the run from its records). Traced work items are sent by `experiments/gate3-trace-per-work-item.sh` unchanged with `REPS=1` (one Job, `backoffLimit 0`, one send, no retry knob set); dangling parents are counted from `spans.csv` by `dangling-parents.py`. Telemetry pins unmoved (collector=otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.160.0, jaeger=jaegertracing/jaeger:2.20.0, prometheus=prom/prometheus:v3.14.0, read from the running Deployments). Worker, mock and orchestrator images were not rebuilt; the load client was built by ko from a tree that held the untracked run directory and, for three of repetition 2's four builds, a modified `versions.yaml` as well (edited at 09:12:59Z while the run was under way; ko's stderr lists ` M versions.yaml` from the second build on; no source an image is built from was touched), so it carries `vcs.modified=true` (ko's "git is in a dirty state" is on record for repetition 2's four builds; repetition 1 kept no record of that line). All four builds loaded one image, and every Job of both repetitions ran it: digest `5f6ccb6f…`, one kubelet-resolved imageID on all nine Jobs, read live at 09:48:45Z (`loadgen-job-images.csv`). So the edit changed no binary, and repetition 1's load client is the same binary as repetition 2's.
- Result: `experiments/runs/2026-09-19-waypoint-policy-recheck/` (repetition 1: the numbered directories, `rep-1-extracts.txt`, `rep-1-dangling-parents.csv`; repetition 2: `rep-2/`, with `run.txt`, `requests-carried.csv`, `4-restored/readback.txt`, `notes.txt`).

  | | reading | repetition 1 | repetition 2 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | overlay lifted: args; dump | `["--config","{}"]`; policies 0, `config.tracing` null, xDS `istiod.istio-system.svc:15012` | the same |
  | 2 | the page's policy: status, controller | Accepted=True (Valid, "Policy accepted"), **Attached=True ("Attached to all targets")**, `agentgateway.dev/agentgateway`; read 1 s after the apply | the same; both conditions' `lastTransitionTime` is the second the policy was created (09:12:08Z) |
  | 2 | waypoint dump after the status | **policies 0, tracing null**, 10 s after the apply; the same bytes as the dump before the policy | **policies 0, tracing null**, 31 s after; the same bytes as the dump before the policy |
  | 2 | ingress dump, same minute (control) | policies 2, one of them `frontend/agentgateway-ingress/tracing:frontend-tracing:…`, named `AgentgatewayPolicy tracing`; xDS `agentgateway.agentgateway-system.svc.cluster.local:9978` | the same, read in the same second as the waypoint's |
  | 2 | controller's push line | 08:48:21.992Z, cause `policy/frontend/lab/tracing:frontend-tracing:lab/agentgateway-waypoint` | 09:12:08.808Z, the same cause |
  | 2 | one work item | **10 spans**, 2 trace ids, hop without a span: `agentgateway-waypoint`; **2 dangling parents** | **10 spans**, 2 trace ids, the same hop; **2 dangling parents** |
  | 2 | waypoint dump after the work item | not taken | policies 0, tracing null, 63 s after the policy; **`totalRequests` to the worker 0 → 3**; status still Attached=True |
  | 3 | nothing custom, policy re-created: status | Accepted=True, Attached=True | the same, in the second it was created (09:13:15Z) |
  | 3 | waypoint dump after the status | policies 0, tracing null, 11 s after; the same bytes as before the policy | policies 0, tracing null, 30 s after; differs from the dump before the policy by one workload entry (step 2's control pod, terminating) |
  | 3 | one work item | **10 spans**, hop without a span: `agentgateway-waypoint`; **2 dangling parents** | **10 spans**, the same hop; **2 dangling parents**; after it policies 0 and `totalRequests` 0 → 3 |
  | 4 | restored: dump | policies 1, key `frontend/tracing`, from `config.tracing` | the same |
  | 4 | one work item per receiver | worker **14** spans (`agentgateway-waypoint=4`), orchestrator **69** (`agentgateway-waypoint=2`, `agentgateway-waypoint-orch=2`); no hop without a span; 0 dangling parents | worker **14**, orchestrator **69**, the same by service; no hop without a span; 0 dangling parents |

  Repetition 1's first work item, on the standing configuration before anything was lifted: 14 spans, `agentgateway-waypoint=4`, no hop without a span, 0 dangling parents.

  **The ledgers do not move.** All nine work items of the two repetitions read the same whether the waypoint exported spans or not: on the worker path one `SendMessage` arrival (200) on the ingress ledger, one `execute` and one Task ending `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` on the execution ledger, one model call with outcome `ok` on the invocation ledger; on the orchestrator path two arrivals, two executes, two Tasks completed, one model call. The client line reads `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` on all nine. What the policy's absence changes is the trace and nothing else: the four spans the waypoint exports when it has somewhere to send them (14 − 10), and with them the parents of the worker's two server spans (`GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` and `POST /`), which then name a span id no exported span carries.

  **The restore, read back** (`rep-2/4-restored/readback.txt`, 09:15:44Z): 10 checks, 0 FAIL. The state equals the one captured at preflight (the four Gateways' class, `parametersRef` and Programmed; the three Telemetry objects; the four standing policies Accepted and Attached, none in `lab`; both waypoints' args); the waypoint's dump holds `frontend/tracing`; 14 and 69 spans with no hop without a span. Read again independently at 09:16:29Z: the same, no port-forward process left, the control pod gone. One residue lies outside what the readback reads: the waypoint Deployment's pod template carries `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt` (live value `2026-09-19T12:13:11+03:00`, written by step 3 of repetition 2; `agentgateway-waypoint-orch` has none). Repetition 1's step 3 had written one at 08:49:59Z, and the pod-template hashes agree with that: repetition 2's lifted pod is `7d5d8f4f56`, repetition 1's variant-3 hash, not repetition 1's lifted hash `6dd7855fcd`, so repetition 2's variants 1 and 2 ran on a template that carried repetition 1's annotation. It is inert, the state the readback compares does not include it, and it was left in place: no cluster change was made for it. pmset's log has no Sleep, DarkWake or Wake line between 09:05Z and 09:20Z.

  **Where repetition 1's records and their description differ.** `2-doc-policy/config-dumps.txt` says its dump was taken "25+ s after the policy reported Attached"; its stamps give 10 s (apply 08:48:21Z, dump 08:48:31Z). Repetition 2's 31 s, and 63 s with traffic in between, cover what that remark claimed. Its `steps.txt` prints one Gateway annotation where the object has two (the second is kubectl's).

  **Left out of the commit:** the full `/config_dump` files, about 46 KB each (`.gitignore` in the run directory says so). They were searched first: no PEM block, no JWT, no key or password field; the `token` and `caCert` entries are file paths inside the pod. `extract-config-dump.py` cuts the three parts read here (`policies`, `config.tracing`, `config.xds`) into the committed `*.extract.json`, with each dump's byte count and sha256.
- Interpretation: found twice, under this configuration and at these versions: the policy of agentgateway's tracing page does not reach a waypoint that istiod manages, and the policy's status says it does. What the page covers is a proxy of class `agentgateway` — its prerequisite creates the Gateway with `gatewayClassName: agentgateway`, and the page says nothing about Istio — and on a Gateway of that class the same policy shape is delivered: the ingress here holds it, from the same controller, read in the same second in which the waypoint held none. Istio's page draws the other side of the line ("agentgateway’s own native configuration format and custom resources are likewise not managed by Istio; Istio programs the proxy solely through the Gateway API resources described in this guide", re-read 2026-09-19), and the dumps show the mechanism: the waypoint is a client of istiod's xDS (`istiod.istio-system.svc:15012`), the agentgateway controller translated the policy and pushed it on its own xDS (`:9978`), of which the waypoint is not a client. So non-delivery is as documented. The lab's own tracing pieces are not the cause, which was the author's question: with the overlay lifted, the three `Telemetry` objects deleted and a new pod, the result is the same to the span — 10 spans, the waypoint hop without a span, 2 dangling parents, policies 0 — while the waypoint's own counter rose 0 → 3 across the work item: the work item's two requests through it (the Agent Card GET and the `SendMessage` POST) and the trace script's `POST /control/reset` to the worker from its control pod (`experiments/gate3-trace-per-work-item.sh` lines 103–110, which the ingress ledger excludes by design). So it carried that traffic holding no policy. What stayed in place through that variant, named in the Method, cannot be the cause either, because the two readings that decide the question depend on none of it: the waypoint's xDS address is istiod's (`:15012`) where the ingress's is the agentgateway controller's (`:9978`), and the controller's own log shows the policy pushed on that second xDS; of the pieces that stayed, Istio's page names `PeerAuthentication` among the APIs that "are not applied to agentgateway proxies" (the same sentence names `Telemetry`, which did not stay: its three objects were deleted in that variant). The defect is the status: `Attached=True`, "Attached to all targets", written by `agentgateway.dev/agentgateway` within the second for a Gateway whose class belongs to `istio.io/agentgateway-waypoint-controller`, and still reading so a minute later with traffic crossing a proxy that holds no policy. A user who follows the page against such a Gateway is told the policy is in force. Where that status comes from was read at tag v1.5.0, stated as read and with no claim of intent (`sources.md` §9): for a target of kind Gateway, `LookupGatewaysForTarget` returns the Gateway itself (`reference_indexes.go` 406–410, "// Trivial case"), `resolvePolicyAncestorRefs` makes it the ancestor ref (`traffic_plugin.go` 371–398) and the base conditions set Accepted and Attached true (347–356); neither file names a GatewayClass. The lab's `parametersRef` route remains the only configuration measured here that makes these waypoints export spans (14 and 69 after each restore), and it remains a join neither project documents. A waypoint of class `agentgateway` exists in this lab only as a spike, not a record. One caveat travels with the report: agentgateway's version table gives 1.5.x an Istio range of 1.23 – 1.30 (re-read 2026-09-19) and this cluster runs 1.31.0, the release in which the `istio-agentgateway-waypoint` class first exists, so no Istio inside the stated range has the class at all. Both projects are at their latest release (v1.5.0, 1.31.0; v1.6.0-alpha.1's notes do not name this). No issue or pull request was found that reports this status on a Gateway target (15 queries, `sources.md` §6); two related items exist. agentgateway/agentgateway#1872, an open pull request ("fix(controller): dont write pending status for resources we dont own"), adds the ownership test `string(gc.Spec.ControllerName) != agw.ControllerName` for route and ListenerSet targets on the Pending path, in the same file the status above comes from, and a collaborator's review comment on it asks "Does not emitting an error mean we emit a success? that seems wrong". istio/istio#60024, "Support agentgateway as a waypoint" (open), lists under "Out of scope for initial support" both "Graceful handling of policies applied directly to the waypoint (gateway ParentRef)" and "Status or other indication to the user than non gateway api defined policies are not being enforced at the agw-based waypoint": Istio names this gap itself.
- Follow-up: docs/upstream/agentgateway-policy-attached-to-istiod-driven-waypoint.md (draft, made fileable on 2026-09-19; not filed)
